units.title: Science and Technology - Nature and Scope, Relevance to Daily Life, National S&T Policy, Institutions and Prominent Indian Scientists

rows.title: Nature, scope and characteristics of science and technology; science vs technology

secs.t: Science and technology — definitions, types and FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: "which has NOT been considered a science" - astrology.
Science produces laws and theories; technology produces products and processes; basic research is curiosity-driven; applied research addresses a set problem.

Biotechnology combines biology and engineering; geoinformatics combines geography and IT; data science combines statistics and computing; cyber-physical systems combine computing with physical systems through sensors.

secs.t: Scientific method and Technology Readiness Levels → stages

x: After a conclusion,
replication and peer review
help check the reliability and acceptance of the findings.
The Technology Readiness Level scale ranges from
TRL 1 to TRL 9
and originated with NASA.
The RDI Scheme finances projects at
TRL 4 and above
, along with strategic technologies and a Deep-Tech Fund of Funds.

secs.t: Persons, Articles, policies and movements → scientific temper and S&T

x: The Scientific Policy Resolution of 1958 resolved to
foster, promote and sustain science
Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad dates to 1962; the Statement on Scientific Temper to 1981; the Maharashtra Anti-Superstition Act to 2013; and National Science Day is observed on 28 February.
Vigyan Jyoti is intended to encourage
girls
to pursue Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics.

secs.t: Technology terms → meaning

x: Biometrics identifies a person using distinctive physical or behavioural characteristics such as fingerprints, iris patterns or facial features.
Digital embossing produces raised tactile printing and is used for
braille maps
for visually impaired persons.
Wearables may be worn as accessories or clothing, implanted or tattooed on the skin, and generally combine sensors, software and wireless connectivity as part of the Internet of Things.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The 1950s–1970s focused on institution-building and scientific temper, the 1980s on self-reliance, the 2010s on innovation, and the present phase on artificial intelligence, quantum technology and semiconductors.
India's 2025 Global Innovation Index rank was 38th, while its Network Readiness Index rank was 49th in 2024 compared with 79th in 2019.

rows.title: Relevance of science and technology to day-to-day life - health, food, transport, communication, household

secs.t: Food and health terms — definitions and types

x: Preservatives, colours, emulsifiers, sweeteners and flavour enhancers such as MSG are food additives.
Food irradiation uses ionising radiation to destroy harmful organisms without altering nutrition.
Oil and milk get vitamins A and D; iron, folic acid and B12 go into rice.
Dense bone absorbs more X-ray radiation, making X-rays useful for detecting fractures.

secs.t: Health devices and imaging → working principle

x: X-ray uses ionising electromagnetic radiation; CT reconstructs multiple X-ray images; MRI uses magnetic fields and radio waves; ultrasound uses sound waves and echoes.
Both statements are true, and the absence of ionising radiation explains the use of ultrasound in monitoring foetal development.
Wearables can provide doctors with real-time patient data, supporting smarter health tracking.

secs.t: Household and transport technologies → working principle — Household appliances

x: Microwave ovens use microwaves of about
2.45 GHz
, which make water molecules rotate and thereby generate heat.
In a vapour-compression refrigerator, the refrigerant absorbs heat while evaporating inside and releases heat at the condenser.
Induction cooking uses electromagnetic induction and eddy currents in a ferromagnetic vessel.
LED = electroluminescence at a p-n junction.

secs.t: Household and transport technologies → working principle — Smart materials and sensors

x: Hydrogels are water-absorbing polymers used in
contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers and drug delivery
Accelerometers are also used for step counting.
Graphene- or carbon-fibre-electrode flexible batteries can power
wearables and flexible displays

secs.t: Household and transport technologies → working principle — Transport technologies

x: FASTag is a passive RFID system powered by the reader's field.
NavIC
is India's own satellite-based navigation system and supports location-related services.
C-V2X uses 4G/5G and DSRC is Wi-Fi-based.
NM-ICPS was approved in 2018.
H2 + O2 gives electricity and only water.

secs.t: Food → adulterant; product → harmful chemical

x: Exam angle: product → banned chemical matching from recent state bans.
Aristolochic acid occurs in Aristolochia plants used in some herbal medicines and is associated with
kidney damage and urinary-tract cancer
Lead is associated with old paints, pipes, some cosmetics and lead-chromate-adulterated spices, not MRI contrast agents.
BPA, triclosan and phthalates have endocrine-related concerns, while lead is neurotoxic and especially harmful to children.

secs.t: Schemes, platforms and missions → purpose

x: Geospatial tools support contact tracing, hotspot mapping and the selection of suitable locations for PHCs and hospitals.
The mission joins the
Health, Animal Husbandry, Environment and Science and Technology
ministries to address zoonoses and antimicrobial resistance.
Anna Chakra optimises PDS routes to about 4.37 lakh fair price shops, saving about Rs 250 crore a year.

secs.t: Impacts and debates — positive vs negative

x: Wearables support health tracking; digital payments relate to e-governance, while screen time and cyber fraud are negative consequences.
In August 2026, the Supreme Court sought the Centre's reply on a plea concerning high-risk AI, including biometric surveillance and risk-scoring in food, health, pension and scholarship delivery.
Decreased privacy
is a negative impact of technology (APPSC-GS 2022).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Current relevance:.
SC notice on unregulated welfare AI (Aug 2026)
Food-safety reform roadmap (Jul 2026)
AP angle:.
VFSTR Guntur ties with Taiwan's Asia University in semiconductors and AI (Aug 2026)

rows.title: Science, Technology and Innovation Policy - 1958 Resolution, 1983, 2003, 2013 policies and the STIP draft
sub: Group-II M2-B-1: National Science and Technology Policy - evolution from 1958 to the recent STI Policy

secs.t: S&T policies → year, Prime Minister, core focus; FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: match policy-year-PM, or "which was the first/fifth policy".
All three statements correctly describe the Technology Policy Statement, 1983, associated with technological competence, self-reliance, technology absorption and reduced import dependence.
DRDO was formed by merging the Technical Development Establishment, the Directorate of Technical Development and Production, and the Defence Science Organisation.

secs.t: Policy objectives and provisions — STP 2003, Decade of Innovation, STI 2013, STIP 2020 — S&T Policy 2003

x: All four objectives were associated with the Science and Technology Policy, 2003, including the optimal utilisation of existing physical and knowledge resources.
The 2013 policy envisaged direct STI intervention in about ten high-impact sectors and the use of modern science for traditional knowledge.
The National Innovation Council was established in 2010 under Sam Pitroda, with inclusive innovation as its goal.

secs.t: Policy objectives and provisions — STP 2003, Decade of Innovation, STI 2013, STIP 2020 — Draft STIP 2020

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT an outcome/objective" of a given policy.
The Draft STIP 2020 envisioned India becoming
one of the top three scientific superpowers in the coming decade
and proposed a people-centric STI ecosystem.
Periodic review and exit strategies
were proposed to improve accountability and enable the discontinuation or restructuring of programmes when necessary.

secs.t: GERD targets and data — policy comparison and reality

x: SPR 1958 (and TPS 1983) had no numeric GERD target.
The draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling full-time-equivalent researchers, GERD and the private share of GERD every five years.
GERD reached
of GDP in FY 2023-24, a 15-year high.

secs.t: Bodies → role in S&T policy

x: The Prime Minister is the President of ANRF, while the Ministers of Science and Technology and Education are its Vice-Presidents.
The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) was established in 1985 and is the parent department of CSIR.
CSIR and the Department of Biotechnology act as India’s lead agencies for BRICS science and technology cooperation during India’s chairship.

secs.t: Bodies → role in S&T policy — ANRF

x: The proposed funding is ₹50,000 crore for 2023–28, of which about ₹36,000 crore is expected from non-government sources; therefore, the entire amount is not expected from non-government sources.
NITI Aayog
is the nodal agency for improving India’s GII rank and publishes the India Innovation Index.
The report states that approximately
of ANRF funds go to IITs and also points to slow approvals.

secs.t: Bodies → role in S&T policy — State councils - APCOST

x: State S&T councils frame state S&T policy, provide research grants and popularise science.
APCOST works under the Andhra Pradesh
Environment, Forests, Science and Technology Department
APCOST and similar state councils receive support under the Department of Science and Technology’s
State S&T Programme

secs.t: Schemes and funds → full form and purpose

x: The recommendations called for GERD to reach 2% of GDP within four to five years through the private sector, proposed NISPG, and suggested a unified fellowship called Vigyan Nidhi.
INSPIRE stands for Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research and covers a continuum from school awards to PhD fellowships and faculty posts to attract young talent to science.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The draft proposes three-tier governance.
The 2% GERD target has not been achieved under any policy, and ANRF grants have been criticised for favouring IITs; this is a distributional criticism distinct from health-research spending targets.
The DST-STI Hub at SPMVV, Tirupati focuses on
sericulture, agriculture and livelihoods for SC/ST women
through a three-year project.

rows.title: Research and development spending in India; GERD, innovation indices, patents ecosystem

secs.t: R&D data — GERD, private share, researchers, publications — GERD as % of GDP - India vs USA, China, Israel, South Korea

x: India's GERD was
of GDP in FY 2023–24, described as a 15-year high after reversing a decade-long decline.
The order is South Korea, Israel, China and India, corresponding approximately to 5.3%, 5%, 2.4% and 0.84%, respectively.
India's private share was about 36%, compared with about 70% in the USA and 76% in South Korea.

secs.t: R&D data — GERD, private share, researchers, publications — Government vs private share

x: Private industry accounted for
of R&D expenditure in FY 2023–24 and overtook public funding for the first time.

secs.t: R&D data — GERD, private share, researchers, publications — Researchers, publications and grants

x: India had approximately 262 FTE researchers per million people.
India ranked
third
globally in scientific publications; its nanoscience publications also ranked third after China and the USA.
Indian agencies fund less than 10% of applications, while the corresponding figures cited are 26% for the US NSF and 19% for UKRI.

secs.t: Acts, policies and schemes → year and provision — Patent and IP law

x: TRIPS Article 28 gives product-patent rights.
IPAB was abolished in 2021 by the Tribunals Reforms Act and appeals now go to High Courts.
Resident or domestic applicants accounted for about
of filings in 2024–25, marking a policy-driven shift.

secs.t: Acts, policies and schemes → year and provision — R&D funding schemes

x: The scheme gives concessional finance for private R&D (AI, quantum, biotech, energy).
The PM Research Chair seeks to bring Indian-origin researchers back to India, thereby promoting brain gain.
The Pharma-MedTech Research Scheme provides for
seven Centres of Excellence
at NIPERs.
India ranked sixth in the world in patent filing activity according to WIPO 2023.

secs.t: Innovation indices → publisher and India's rank

x: The Global Innovation Index is published by the World Intellectual Property Organization (
WIPO
The 2021 leaders were Karnataka among Major States, Manipur among North-East and Hill States, and Chandigarh among UTs and City States.
India ranked 49th in the Network Readiness Index 2024 (133 economies), up from 79th in 2019.

secs.t: Organisations and ecosystem → role and scale

x: WIPO was established in 1967, is headquartered in Geneva and is a specialised agency of the United Nations.
India is the
third
-largest start-up hub and had 1.59 lakh DPIIT-recognised start-ups according to the cited figure.
The Atal Innovation Mission promotes innovation through school tinkering labs, incubation centres and a mentor network.

secs.t: Issues and debates — why R&D lags

x: The identified reasons are private risk aversion, weak lab–industry linkages and a shortage of deep-tech capital.
Approximately 80% of ANRF funding is reported to go to IITs.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism is that improved rankings can coexist with weak R&D intensity, low researcher density and poor commercialisation of research.
The continuing concern highlighted is that India has had no Nobel Prize in science for nearly a century.
IISER Tirupati was placed
20th
among Indian institutions in the Nature Index 2026.

rows.title: S&T institutions - CSIR and its laboratories, DST, DBT, DSIR, SERB

secs.t: Departments and councils → year, parent, head; FIRSTs — CSIR leadership and network

x: The National Biotechnology Board was established in 1982 with
DST, UGC, ICMR and CSIR
, and was upgraded to the Department of Biotechnology in 1986.
BRIC was established in 2023 as an apex body integrating 14 DBT institutions, with the Union S&T Minister as Chair and the DBT Secretary as ex officio Director-General.

secs.t: Departments and councils → year, parent, head; FIRSTs — DSIR recognition

x: FAIR is funded equally by DST and DAE, in a
proportion.
CSIR, DAE, DoS, ICMR and ICAR
were allowed to bypass GeM for scientific equipment.
DSIR recognition makes the recognised institutions eligible for
income tax and customs duty exemptions
The ANRF Act, 2023 repealed the SERB Act, 2008 and subsumed SERB into ANRF.

secs.t: CSIR laboratories → location, founding year, field

x: Exam angle: "headquarters of X is located in" - Nagpur, Hyderabad, Lucknow and Bhavnagar recur.
The National Physical Laboratory (
NPL
), New Delhi, maintains national measurement standards and keeps Indian Standard Time.
IMTECH, Chandigarh, works in microbial technology and hosts the MTCC gene bank, an IDA under the Budapest Treaty.
CDRI, set up in 1951 for drug research, is at
Lucknow
(CIMAP is also in Lucknow).

secs.t: DBT, DST and other institutes → location, founder/year

x: The
Centre of Innovative and Applied Bioprocessing
(CIAB), Mohali, is a DBT institute (APPSC-G2 2025).
IISc, Bengaluru, was founded in 1909 with the vision of
Jamsetji Tata
The National Centre for Earth Science Studies (NCESS) was established in Kerala in 1978 and has been under the Ministry of Earth Sciences since 2014.

secs.t: CSIR technologies in news → developing lab

x: Saheli, a centchroman-based weekly oral contraceptive, was developed by the Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI), Lucknow.
NCL, Pune
, developed and scaled up methanol-to-DME technology, with DME serving as an LPG substitute.
CSIO transferred the MSCOPE motor stethoscope, power-quality analyser and Su-30 HUD optics.
The Smart Village at Kusunpur, Kendrapara, Odisha, uses an AI crocodile-alert system.

secs.t: Schemes, grants and fellowships → purpose

x: DST is also the nodal department for the RDI Scheme.
PRISM, PACE, BIRD-crf and A2K+ are all components of DSIR’s Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme.
SERB-POWER is for women researchers.
Ramalingaswami Re-entry is for life sciences.

secs.t: CSIR, DBT and other laboratories in AP and Telangana

x: CCMB, IICT and NGRI
are CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad.
CDFD is a DBT institution in Hyderabad.
The NIO Regional Centre in Andhra Pradesh is located at
Visakhapatnam
The MoU focuses on converting shrimp waste into
chitin and glucosamine

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The proposals included reserving half of the top posts for mid-career scientists and evaluating laboratories through patents and technology transfer.
The Andhra Pradesh angle includes the
shrimp-waste value chain with IICT and research at AIIMS Mangalagiri
HANSA-3 (NG) is a
trainer aircraft developed by NAL
, and Letters of Intent were reported for 114 aircraft.

rows.title: S&T institutions - ICAR, ICMR, ICFRE, DRDO, ISRO, DAE, DoS and their mandates

secs.t: Councils and departments → year, parent, head; FIRSTs

x: ICFRE, set up in 1986 and an autonomous council under MoEFCC since 1991, is headquartered at
Dehradun
(also home of FRI).
INCOSPAR was formed in 1962 under Vikram Sarabhai and the Department of Atomic Energy; ISRO was established in 1969.
ICMR is under DHR, ISRO under DoS, DRDO under the Department of Defence R&D, and CSIR under DSIR.

secs.t: Councils and departments → year, parent, head; FIRSTs — Chiefs

x: The stated foundations are strengthening health research capacity, leveraging traditional medicine and aligning with the National Health Policy.
The Atomic Energy Commission undertakes policy and strategic planning, oversees BARC, NPCIL and AERB, and is chaired by the Secretary, DAE.
Antrix was established in September 1992 and became a Miniratna in 2008; NSIL was established in 2019, and IN-SPACe was created in 2020 for private players.

secs.t: ICAR network, KVKs and agricultural institutes → location, founding year

x: ICRISAT is at Patancheru, IARI at New Delhi, CRRI/NRRI at Cuttack and CIFA at Bhubaneswar.
CRRI is at Cuttack, CTRI at Rajahmundry and the NRC on Camel at Bikaner.
The order is IARI (1905), NDRI (1923), CRRI (1946) and CTRI (1947).
KVKs are district-level, 100% centrally funded under ICAR, and each functions under one of 11 ATARIs.
Unjha in Mehsana, Gujarat, is
Asia's largest seed-spice trading hub

secs.t: ICFRE and ICMR institutes → location

x: TFRI is at Jabalpur, CSFER at Prayagraj, HFRI at Shimla and IFB at Hyderabad.
The Arid Forest Research Institute is at Jodhpur, the Rain Forest Research Institute at Jorhat and the Institute of Forest Productivity at Ranchi.
NIV is at Pune, NIN at Hyderabad, and both NIE and NIRT are located at Chennai.

secs.t: Atomic energy units and reactors → function

x: The Heavy Water Board produces heavy water, IREL handles beach-sand minerals and rare earths, and AERB regulates nuclear and radiation safety.
IGCAR, Kalpakkam does fast breeder reactor R&D. The others are wrong: NPCIL builds and runs nuclear power plants.
HBNI was ranked
7th among research institutions, 12th among universities and 20th overall
in the stated NIRF 2025 rankings.

secs.t: ISRO — commercial arms, regulator and launches

x: LVM3-M6, launched on 24 December 2025, carried BlueBird Block-2, described as the heaviest payload ever launched from India.

secs.t: Mega-science projects → site and Indian lead institutions

x: NCRA-TIFR, Pune
is the Indian lead institution for the Square Kilometre Array, whose facilities are located in South Africa and Australia.
All four are associated with IIA Bengaluru under DST: the VELC payload, Hanle Dark Sky Reserve, Himalayan Chandra Telescope and Kodaikanal Solar Observatory.
LIGO detected gravitational waves in 2015, and the Nobel Prize was awarded in 2017 to Rainer Weiss, Barry Barish and Kip Thorne.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: NARL is located at Gadanki.
The memo barred resignations of Group-A staff working on Gaganyaan after approximately 100 personnel had exited.
APSARA was Asia’s first research reactor, while the first Krishi Vigyan Kendra was established in Puducherry in 1974.

rows.title: Academies and promotion bodies - INSA, IASc, NASI, Vigyan Prasar, National Innovation Foundation

secs.t: Academies and associations → founder, year, HQ; FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: order of founding NASI (1930) → IASc (1934) → INSA (1935); Raman = IASc, Saha = NASI.
The 88th session (2001, New Delhi) had the theme '
Food, Nutrition and Environmental Security
' (asked in UPSC 2001). 'S&T for Sustainable Development with Women Empowerment' was the theme of the 108th session (Jan 2023, Nagpur).

secs.t: Science communication and educational channels → run by

x: Exam angle: "two new science communication platforms" =
DD Science and India Science
, not Gyan Darshan/Gyan Vani or DD Kisan.
Vigyan Dhara is a DST umbrella scheme merging schemes concerning S&T institutional and human capacity building, research and development, and innovation, technology development and deployment.
Gyan Darshan was launched on
26 January 2000
as an educational television channel involving MHRD, IGNOU and Prasar Bharati.

secs.t: Outreach bodies, exhibitions and festivals → organiser

x: The ‘Science on Wheels’ mobile laboratories are an NCSTC initiative; the programme also includes Alluri Sitharama Raju district in Andhra Pradesh.
Rashtriya Avishkar Abhiyan was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of HRD, now the Ministry of Education, to encourage practical and inquiry-based science and mathematics learning in schools.
ICMR-SHINE, expanded as Science & Health Innovation for the Nextgen Explorers, is an outreach initiative for
students of Classes 9–12

secs.t: Science days → date and event commemorated

x: National Mathematics Day commemorates
Srinivasa Ramanujan
's birth anniversary.
National Science Day is observed on 28 February, marking C.V. Raman's discovery of the Raman Effect (1928).

secs.t: National Innovation Foundation (NIF) — origin, mandate, competitions

x: NIF-India was set up in March 2000 with the support of the
Department of Science and Technology
and functions as an autonomous body of DST.
NIF's mandate is
to scout, support and spread grassroots technological innovations and outstanding traditional knowledge
STIP 2020 envisages helping grassroots innovators with intellectual property rights and patent filing through higher education institutes.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The second edition of ICMR-SHINE concluded in
August 2026
and was linked to the Prime Minister’s ‘One Day as a Scientist’ call.
NASI was founded in 1930 by Meghnad Saha as the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Sciences and is regarded as the oldest science academy in India.
The first session of the Indian Science Congress was held in 1914 at the Asiatic Society in Kolkata and was presided over by Sir Ashutosh Mukherjee.

rows.title: Programmes promoting S&T and innovation - INSPIRE, Ramanujan and J.C. Bose fellowships, Atal Innovation Mission, Atal Tinkering Labs

secs.t: INSPIRE components → full form and target group

x: INSPIRE, or Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research, is a flagship programme of the
Department of Science and Technology
launched in 2008.
SHE is the higher-education scholarship component, while AORC covers research-career opportunities through INSPIRE Fellowship and INSPIRE Faculty.
MANAK =
Million Minds Augmenting National Aspiration and Knowledge
, for Classes VI-X (age 10-15).

secs.t: Fellowships and brain-gain schemes → awarding body and target

x: The Ramanujan Fellowship, administered by SERB and now under ANRF, is intended to attract Indian scientists working abroad back to India.
The Swarnajayanti Fellowship began in 1997 to mark
50 years of India’s Independence
and supports young scientists with a proven record.
The
Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship
is a DBT (Department of Biotechnology) scheme for Indian life-science and biotech scientists abroad who return, so it is the odd one out.

secs.t: Women and inclusion in STEM — schemes → target group

x: Exam angle: senior women scientists + interdisciplinary =
WIDUSHI
; Vigyan Jyoti =
women/girls
in STEM.

CURIE relates to research facilities for 22 Women PG Colleges; WiSLP works with early- and mid-career women scientists and the British Council; SEED has established STI Hubs for SC/ST communities; GATI promotes institutional gender equity.

secs.t: Student programmes and start-up support → partners and objective

x: The Smart India Hackathon is partnered by the Ministry of Education’s Innovation Cell and AICTE and addresses problems posed by ministries and industry.
NIDHI, or National Initiative for Developing and Harnessing Innovations, was launched in 2016 by the
Department of Science and Technology
NIDHI includes PRAYAS, Entrepreneur-in-Residence, Seed Support System, Technology Business Incubators, Accelerators and Centres of Excellence.

secs.t: National technology missions — NSM (PARAM systems), NM-ICPS, NQM

x: PARAM Shivay is hosted by IIT (BHU) Varanasi, PARAM Brahma by IISER Pune, PARAM Pravega by IISc Bengaluru and PARAM Ganga by IIT Roorkee.
NM-ICPS was approved by the Cabinet in 2018 with Rs 3,660 crore (for nine years per current sources; older sources say five), and set up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs.

secs.t: Atal Innovation Mission and Atal Tinkering Labs — components and data

x: ATLs operate in schools, AICs support start-ups, and ACICs focus on rural and underserved areas.
ATLs are established in schools for students in grades 6–12 and provide exposure to technologies such as IoT, 3D printing and robotics.
LIPI, 2,500 new ATLs, 10 Atal Sectoral Innovation Launchpads and the Deeptech Reactor are all associated with AIM 2.0.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All four statements correctly describe the RDI Scheme’s approval, funding, first-year allocation and institutional steering arrangement.
The 8th Youth Co:Lab challenge 2026 is a UNDP–Atal Innovation Mission initiative.
Amaravati Quantum Valley is an Andhra Pradesh initiative.

rows.title: National strategies and missions in S&T - Quantum Mission, Supercomputing, Deep Ocean, Bio-E3, Anusandhan NRF
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-8

secs.t: Supercomputers → developer and host; FIRSTs — Early machines

x: The systems are linked on the National Supercomputing Grid over the
National Knowledge Network
The indigenous stack comprises the Rudra server board, Trinetra interconnect and open-source AlmaLinux software.
Vijay Bhatkar is recognised as the
father of Indian supercomputing
Flosolver is associated with NAL Bengaluru, Anupam with BARC, Pratyush with IITM Pune and Mihir with NCMRWF, Noida.

secs.t: Supercomputers → developer and host; FIRSTs — NSM machines → host

x: Exam angle: machine → host pairs (PARAM Shivay is NOT at IIT Guwahati).
PARAM Shivay is at IIT (BHU), PARAM Porul at NIT Tiruchirappalli, PARAM Pravega at IISc Bengaluru and PARAM Ananta at IIT Gandhinagar.
The Rudra machines are built on the Rudra server, while AUM is a separate C-DAC high-performance computing chip programme.

secs.t: National Quantum Mission — approval, targets, hubs

x: The mission is under DST, has an outlay of ₹6,003.65 crore and covers eight years from 2023–24 to 2030–31.
The target is intermediate-scale computers with 50 to 1000 physical qubits within eight years.
Quantum Computing is hosted by IISc Bengaluru, Quantum Communication by IIT Madras, Quantum Sensing and Metrology by IIT Bombay, and Quantum Materials and Devices by IIT Delhi.

secs.t: Missions, policies and ANRF → ministry, year, outlay

x: Inter-city quantum key distribution
is a National Quantum Mission objective, not a Bio-E3 thematic sector.
The Prime Minister
is the ex officio President of the ANRF Governing Board.
ANRF is the custodian of the ₹1 lakh crore RDI Fund through a
two-tier Special Purpose Fund
The National Geospatial Mission is associated with DST through the Survey of India, appears in Budget 2025–26 and runs till 2031.

secs.t: AP quantum push — Amaravati Quantum Valley → places and FIRSTs

x: The seven MoUs included a UNICC Centre of Excellence, IBM's training initiative for one lakh youth and a NIELIT Quantum AI deemed university.
Andhra Pradesh
is the first State with a dedicated quantum computing policy and aims to make the Amaravati Quantum Valley one of the top five global quantum hubs by 2030.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India-Germany quantum and deep-tech cooperation is being pursued through the Indo-German Science and Technology Centre (IGSTC) and the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF).
PARAM 8000
(1991) was built by C-DAC under Vijay Bhatkar and was India's first supercomputer.

rows.title: Prominent Indian scientists - C.V. Raman, J.C. Bose, S.N. Bose, Ramanujan, Meghnad Saha, Homi Bhabha

secs.t: Scientists → contributions

x: J.C. Bose pioneered microwave and millimetre-wave radio research and worked with a coherer and a galena semiconductor detector.
C.V. Raman announced the Raman Effect on 28 February 1928 at IACS, Kolkata, and that date is now National Science Day.
Meghnad Saha formulated the Saha, or ionisation, equation from his theory of
thermal ionisation of elements
Meghnad Saha was regarded as the chief architect of river planning in India and prepared the original plan for the Damodar Valley Project.

secs.t: Terms and discoveries → meaning

x: The Saha equation helps interpret stellar spectra by indicating the
temperature and ionisation state of stars
S. N. Bose sent the paper to
Albert Einstein
, who translated it into German and arranged its publication.
Bose–Einstein Condensate is described as the fifth state of matter, and NASA experiments on the ISS observed it in space.

secs.t: Institutions → founder and year

x: The Bose Institute was founded in 1917, the Indian Academy of Sciences in 1934, TIFR in 1945 and the Raman Research Institute in 1948.
The Atomic Energy Establishment at Trombay was founded in 1954 and was renamed BARC after Homi Bhabha's death in 1966.

secs.t: Books, papers and films → author

x: The Nervous Mechanism of Plants
was written by J.C. Bose.
Rabindranath Tagore dedicated *Visva-Parichay*, published in 1937, to
S. N. Bose

secs.t: Women scientists — FIRST achievements and field

x: Janaki Ammal was a botanist and cytogeneticist associated with plant breeding, sugarcane hybrids, the cited book and the Padma Shri of 1977.
Bibha Chowdhuri worked on cosmic rays and mesons with D.M. Bose and completed her Ph.D. under P.M.S. Blackett.
Kamala Sohonie
, a biochemist, earned her PhD from Cambridge in 1939 and was also the first woman admitted to IISc.

secs.t: Awards, honours and commemorations

x: C. V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in 1930, was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954 and was knighted in 1929.
All three pairs are correctly matched.
Bhabha received the FRS in 1941 and Padma Bhushan in 1954, while S. N. Bose received Padma Vibhushan in 1954 and FRS in 1958.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: IACS was founded in Kolkata in 1876 by
Mahendra Lal Sircar
IACS is described as the oldest institute for basic research and is funded by the Department of Science and Technology and the Government of West Bengal.
The Matilda effect is the leaving out of women scientists such as Janaki Ammal and Anna Mani from public memory.

src: Sources: CDI (Block01 Achievements of Indian Scientists - Raman, S.N. Bose, Saha, Chandrasekhar); UPSC S&T notes p.184-186; UPSC Post-Independence History p.127; LENS Jun 2026 p.84 (IACS); LENSD 27 May 2026; TH 30 Jul 2026, 12 Mar 2026

rows.title: Prominent Indian scientists - Vikram Sarabhai, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, M.S. Swaminathan, Har Gobind Khorana, Venkatraman Ramakrishnan, C.N.R. Rao

secs.t: Scientists → contributions and titles — Vikram Sarabhai

x: Sarabhai headed INCOSPAR from 1962; it became ISRO in 1969, and he served as ISRO’s first Chairman until his death in 1971.
Venkatraman Ramakrishnan is known for determining the
atomic structure of the 30S ribosomal subunit
, which provided insight into protein synthesis.
Khorana was recognised for interpreting the genetic code and explaining its role in protein synthesis.

secs.t: Scientists → contributions and titles — M.S. Swaminathan

x: Kalam led the
Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme
, associated with missiles such as Agni, Prithvi, Akash, Trishul and Nag.
The correct order is SLV-3 placing Rohini in orbit in 1980, Pokhran-II in 1998, the beginning of Kalam’s presidency in 2002 and the renaming in 2015.
In 2006, Kalam, India's 11th President (2002-2007), flew in a
Sukhoi-30 MKI
and became the first President to fly a fighter (RPSC 2007).

secs.t: Other scientists → organisation led and area of work

x: K. Kasturirangan served as ISRO Chairman from 1994 to 2003 and chaired the drafting committee of NEP 2020.
Tessy Thomas of DRDO was the project director of Agni-IV and is popularly known as the “Missile Woman.”.
Birbal Sahni is associated with palaeobotany, P. Maheshwari with plant embryology, K.C. Mehta with cereal rusts and G.N. Ramachandran with protein structure.

secs.t: Institutions founded and named after scientists

x: Vikram Sarabhai founded the
Physical Research Laboratory
in Ahmedabad in 1947.
The Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station was renamed the
Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre
at Thiruvananthapuram.
The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal, constituted in 1990 by COSPAR and ISRO, recognises
space scientists from developing countries

secs.t: Awards and honours → year

x: The 2009 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Venkatraman Ramakrishnan,
Thomas A. Steitz and Ada Yonath
for studies of the ribosome.
Khorana shared the 1968 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with
Robert W. Holley and Marshall W. Nirenberg
M.S. Swaminathan was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024 for his contribution to agriculture.

secs.t: Scientists from AP — SubbaRow and Nayudamma

x: Yellapragada SubbaRow was born at
Bhimavaram
Yellapragada SubbaRow contributed to understanding the role of
ATP and phosphocreatine
in muscle through the Fiske–SubbaRow method.
SubbaRow contributed to folic acid synthesis and was associated with methotrexate, aureomycin and Hetrazan.
Nayudamma died in the Kanishka bombing in 1985, not 1986.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Annapurni Subramaniam
won the COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal in 2026, becoming the first Indian woman and the fourth Indian recipient.
The debate invoked Vikram Sarabhai, Satish Dhawan, Brahm Prakash, U.R. Rao and A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the first Indian Head of State to fly a fighter aircraft.

rows.title: Science awards and recognitions - Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize, Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar, Nobel laureates of Indian origin

secs.t: Nobel Prize — origin, categories and FIRSTs

x: The prize comes from Alfred Nobel's will.
The original five categories were
Physics, Chemistry, Physiology or Medicine, Literature and Peace
Economics was not one of the original five prizes in Nobel's will.
The Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences is awarded by the
Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences
Nobel laureate status cannot be transferred, shared or revoked.

secs.t: Nobel laureates of Indian origin or citizenship → year, field, discovery

x: Exam angle: "first Indian scientist to win Nobel" = Raman (not Khorana/Chandrasekhar); Khorana and Chandrasekhar were US citizens when awarded .
Abhijit Banerjee, along with Esther Duflo and Michael Kremer, received the 2019 Economics Nobel for
an experimental approach to alleviating global poverty
Beyond the Chandrasekhar limit, a white dwarf can collapse into a neutron star or a black hole.

secs.t: Indian science awards — Bhatnagar Prize and Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar

x: The seven disciplines include biology, chemistry, earth/atmosphere/ocean/planetary sciences, engineering, mathematics, medicine and physics.
Ecologist Madhav Gadgil was associated with People's Biodiversity Registers and chaired the 2010 Gadgil Commission on the Western Ghats.
The Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar replaced multiple ministry awards, incorporated the Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize as Vigyan Yuva-SSB, and spans 13 domains.

secs.t: International awards → Indian-origin winners

x: Jainendra K. Jain was recognised for the
composite fermion model for the fractional quantum Hall effect
and was the first Indian-origin recipient of the Wolf Prize in Physics.
The Kalinga Prize was instituted in 1952 with a donation from Biju Patnaik through the Kalinga Foundation Trust.
Jagjit Singh received it in 1963, Narender K. Sehgal in 1991, Jayant V. Narlikar in 1996 and Yash Pal in 2009.

secs.t: Awards → field of contribution

x: The COSPAR Vikram Sarabhai Medal is associated with space research by scientists from developing countries, not political science.
The J.C. Bose Fellowship or Grant supports
science and engineering research
and is associated with ANRF.
The Infosys Prize covers engineering and computer science, humanities and social sciences, life sciences,
mathematical sciences
and physical sciences.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The first Nobel Prize was awarded in 1901, C. V. Raman became the first Indian scientist laureate in 1930, and the first Indian-origin Wolf Prize in Physics recipient was recorded in 2026.
C.V. Raman was awarded the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering and explaining the Raman Effect, involving
the scattering of light

units.title: Information and Communication Technology - Nature and Scope, ICT in Daily Life, ICT and Industry, ICT and Governance, Netiquettes, Cyber Security

rows.title: Nature and scope of ICT; basics of hardware, software, memory and operating systems

secs.t: Computer generations, types and FIRSTs

x: The correct sequence is vacuum tubes, transistors, integrated circuits and microprocessors, corresponding broadly to the first through fourth generations.
The fifth generation is associated with artificial intelligence, ultra-large-scale integration and parallel processing.
“Technology preservation” is associated with a
computer museum
, where earlier technologies are retained and displayed.
FLOPS means
floating-point operations per second
and is used particularly to indicate supercomputer performance.

secs.t: Persons → inventions and contributions

x: All four pairs are correctly matched.
Tim Berners-Lee
is associated with the World Wide Web, developed in 1989.
John von Neumann
gave the stored-program architecture, in which programs and data are kept in the same memory.
Richard Stallman initiated the GNU project in 1983.

secs.t: Hardware — CPU and input/output devices → function

x: The control unit fetches, decodes and directs operations, while registers provide very fast internal storage.
A conventional barcode consists of
machine-readable vertical bars of varying widths
Print quality is measured in dots per inch (dpi), while speed may be expressed in pages per minute (ppm).
A mouse only sends signals to the computer, so the communication is one-way, or
simplex
(APPSC 2019).

secs.t: Memory and storage → units, types, speed order

x: RAM temporarily stores data and instructions currently in use and loses its contents when power is removed.
An SSD uses flash memory, has no moving parts and is generally faster than an HDD.
Magnetic tape
is a sequential-access medium commonly used for backup and archival purposes.
A single-layer CD stores about 700 MB, a single-layer DVD about 4.7 GB and a single-layer Blu-ray disc about 25 GB.

secs.t: Software and operating systems → types and functions

x: Operating systems, disk-cleanup tools and word processors are correctly classified.
Open-source software makes source code available for viewing, modification and sharing under the applicable licence.
An operating system manages hardware resources, processes, memory, files and drivers.
Batch OS groups jobs and runs them without user interaction.
Android is Linux-based and associated with Google
, while iOS is associated with Apple.

secs.t: Programming, number systems and logic → terms and meaning

x: Second-generation assembly language uses mnemonics and is converted into machine language by an assembler.
A compiler processes the complete program before execution, while an interpreter translates and executes line by line, making debugging easier.
An oval represents start or end; a diamond represents decision, a parallelogram input/output and a rectangle a process.
A
flowchart
is the pictorial form of an algorithm, which is a finite step-by-step procedure (APPSC 2019).

secs.t: Performance terms and supercomputers → meaning and unit

x: The Linpack, or HPL, benchmark measures floating-point power in solving large dense linear systems and is used for world supercomputer rankings.
Param Shakti at IIT Madras was launched by MeitY, has 3.1 petaflops capacity, uses C-DAC RUDRA servers and runs open-source AlmaLinux.
Q-Day denotes the anticipated point when quantum computers can break RSA-2048 public-key encryption through Shor’s algorithm, proposed in 1994.

secs.t: File formats and acronyms → expansion or type

x: MP4 stands for MPEG-4 Part 14 and is a video file format.
PNG stands for Portable Network Graphics, not Portable Network Graphics Interface.
ASCII is a 7-bit code representing 128 characters, while Unicode extends the range of character representation.
JPEG, or Joint Photographic Experts Group, is an image format commonly associated with lossy compression.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ICT covers devices and applications used to
access, store, transmit and manipulate digital information
, including mobiles, networks, software, the internet and satellites.
Privacy risks, the digital divide, job insecurity and over-reliance on technology are identified concerns.
ICT aims at efficient human-human, human-machine and machine-to-machine communication.

src: Sources: UPSC S&T notes p.128-130; CDI (Block02 ICT and E-Governance - Intro to ICT); APP (S&T Unit 1 - ICT advantages/disadvantages); VIS PT365 2026 Pt 1 p.85 (Supercomputer); LENSD 11 Jul 2026; LENS Dec 2025 p.92; CDCA Aug 2026 p.44

rows.title: Networks and the internet - LAN/WAN, protocols, IP, DNS, web technologies

secs.t: Internet history — FIRSTs and pioneers

x: ARPANET was developed under the
United States Department of Defense
in 1969 and became the forerunner of the Internet.
Tim Berners-Lee founded the W3C in 1994.
ERNET began in 1986, public internet was launched by VSNL on 15 August 1995, and Satyam Infoway became the first private ISP in 1998.

secs.t: Network types and topologies → scope and resilience

x: A VPN creates an encrypted tunnel through a public network, improving the privacy of communication.
In a star topology, failure of one node is generally isolated; failure of the central hub can stop the network.
In a
mesh
topology, every node is linked to every other node, making it highly resilient but costly.

secs.t: OSI model and network devices → layer

x: Exam angle: device-to-layer matching (switch = 2, router = 3).
A hub broadcasts to all ports, a switch forwards frames by MAC address, a router routes using IP, and a modem converts between digital and analogue signals.

The Presentation layer handles encryption, compression and formats; the Session layer opens and closes sessions; the Transport layer uses TCP and UDP; and the Data Link layer handles MAC-based frame operations.

secs.t: Transmission modes, connections and wireless standards

x: Simplex permits one-way transmission, half duplex permits two-way transmission one at a time, and full duplex permits simultaneous two-way transmission.
DSL uses telephone copper lines, cable Internet uses coaxial TV cable, and fibre Internet uses optical fibre carrying light pulses.
Satellite Internet has
space, ground and user (VSAT) segments
and does not require a terrestrial wire connection.

secs.t: Protocols → function

x: DNS acts as the Internet’s directory by translating human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses.
Within
TCP
/IP, TCP ensures reliable delivery, while IP addresses and routes packets.
Syntax specifies the format of data, semantics specifies the meaning of each field, and timing specifies when and how fast data is sent.

secs.t: IP and MAC addresses → length, notation, classes

x: IPv4 = 32 bits, dotted decimal.
Classes A, B and C have ranges 1–126, 128–191 and 192–223 respectively.
The 127.x.x.x range is used for loopback.

secs.t: Web terms → meaning

x: Exam angle: "which one displays webpages" (browser) vs "which one stores them" (server).
The server stores and serves pages, the browser displays them, and the search engine indexes them for discovery.
W3C develops and maintains web standards so that webpages function consistently across different browsers.
The dark web is a small hidden subset of the deep web and is associated with anonymous access through tools such as Tor or I2P.

secs.t: Internet governance — bodies and Acts

x: NIXI was established in 2003, functions as a not-for-profit organisation under MeitY, and runs Internet exchange points, the .in registry and IRINN.
Sections 69A and 79 of the Information Technology Act, 2000 are associated with orders to ISPs and intermediaries for blocking content.
The
Telecommunications Act, 2023
replaced the Telegraph Act and contains the power to suspend Internet services.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ISPs may block sites through DNS poisoning, HTTP interception or SNI filtering on HTTPS.
BharatNet fibre reaches approximately
2.18 lakh
gram panchayats according to the stated 2025–26 figure.
The discussion concerned
last-mile connectivity, data centres and an undersea cable landing station
for Andhra Pradesh.

src: Sources: UPSC (S&T pp.131-132, 144); CDI (Block02 ICT and E-Governance; Block15 Cyber Laws - three webs; Block03 Space - satellite internet); APP (S&T Unit 1 - Web 3.0/OCEN, NFC); LENS Apr 2026 p.9; TH 7 Apr 2026, 29 Jun 2026; ES 2025-26 p.87

rows.title: ICT in day-to-day life - mobile telephony, social media, e-commerce, digital media

secs.t: Mobile telephony, QR code and NFC — FIRSTs and terms

x: SIM stands for
Subscriber Identity Module
, the card that identifies the subscriber on a mobile network.
QR means Quick Response; Denso Wave designed the codes in Japan in 1994 for the car industry, and phone cameras can read them quickly.
NFC works over a few centimetres, supports approximately 106–424 kbps, and generally offers easier pairing and lower power use than Bluetooth.

secs.t: Mobile applications and platforms → sector

x: Agrimarket uses GPS, obtains data from Agmarknet, covers markets within 50 km, and provides information in English and Hindi.
The
Sugamya Bharat
app crowdsources reports of inaccessible places and belongs to the m-governance sector.
Agrimarket is an m-agriculture application. eSanjeevani provides telemedicine, Tele-MANAS concerns tele-mental health, and Doctor on Demand is a US health application.

secs.t: E-mail, video conferencing and multimedia → components

x: BCC
, or blind carbon copy, sends copies while hiding the recipients' addresses from one another.
An e-mail address has the form
username @ domain name
; in name@gov.in, 'name' is the username and 'gov.in' the domain.
Video conferencing needs a camera, microphone, speaker/display, a broadband link and conferencing software (codec).
Multimedia may contain text, images or graphics, audio, video and animation.

secs.t: Social media → founder, parent and terms

x: LinkedIn was founded by
Reid Hoffman
in 2003 and is used mainly for professional networking.
The hashtag (#) was popularised on
Twitter
(APPSC 2019), the micro-blogging platform founded by Jack Dorsey and others in 2006 and renamed X in 2023.
LinkedIn was founded in 2003, Facebook in 2004, LinkedIn came under Microsoft ownership in 2016, and Twitter was renamed X in 2023.

secs.t: E-commerce — models and ONDC

x: B2B denotes business-to-business transactions, B2C business-to-consumer transactions, C2C consumer-to-consumer transactions, and D2C direct brand-to-consumer sales.
ONDC is a network-based protocol rather than a single platform.
The stated textbook position permits 100% FDI under the automatic route in the marketplace model but does not permit FDI in the inventory model.

secs.t: Acts and rules on digital platforms → year and provision

x: The IT Rules, 2021 cover social media, OTT and digital news platforms, and contain both a Code of Ethics and a three-tier grievance redressal mechanism.
The 2023 amendment links failure to comply with government orders on false content with loss of safe-harbour protection under
Section 79
of the IT Act.
The draft dated 30 March 2026 proposed enabling the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting to send takedown notices to individual users.

secs.t: Digital-age disorders → terms, places and initiatives

x: Nomophobia is fear of being without one's mobile phone (a-iii), FOMO is fear of missing out (b-iv), doomscrolling is endless scrolling through bad news (c-i) and cyberchondria is health anxiety fed by online symptom searches (d-ii), so A. B swaps both a/b and c/d, C swaps only doomscrolling and cyberchondria, and D gives nomophobia the meaning of doomscrolling.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The DPDP Act treats anyone below 18 as a child.
The proposed approach favours graded limits based on age instead of imposing a blanket ban on all persons below a specified age.
The Supreme Court directed the government to frame guidelines concerning
online content

rows.title: ICT and industry - Industry 4.0, Internet of Things, robotics and automation

secs.t: Industrial revolutions — stages, definitions and FIRSTs

x: Industry 1.0 involved steam-powered mechanisation; Industry 2.0 electricity and mass production; Industry 3.0 computers and electronics; and Industry 4.0 cyber-physical systems.
Industry 4.0 is characterised by cyber-physical systems, IoT, networks, AI and big data.
Klaus Schwab (WEF founder) coined the term in 2016.
India’s first 3D-printed post office was established in
Bengaluru in 2023

secs.t: Terms → meaning (automation, IoT, manufacturing, extended reality)

x: PLC controls machines as a rugged industrial computer; SCADA enables remote monitoring; a digital twin is a virtual replica; and a cobot works collaboratively with humans.
mMTC means massive machine-type communication and is intended to support dense IoT sensor deployments in 5G networks.
The metaverse is a persistent and shared 3D virtual space that uses extended reality, avatars and digital assets.

secs.t: IoT — layers, variants, IoT vs AI and RFID tags

x: The three-layer IoT model consists of the perception layer, network layer and application layer.
An active RFID tag has its own battery and transmitter, broadcasts by itself and generally offers a longer range.
A semi-passive tag’s battery powers its chip, but it still uses the reader’s field to send its response.

secs.t: Applications — IoT, wearables, 3D printing and drones

x: Wearables track health and fitness indicators, support biometric authentication and function as typical IoT end-devices.
Kisan drones are used to spray crops and map land; 100 were flagged off in February 2022.
Namo Drone Didi provides drones to
women’s Self-Help Groups for agricultural services

secs.t: Robots and drones → developer, types and weight classes

x: Bandicoot (Genrobotics, Kerala) cleans manholes/sewers to end manual scavenging (a-iii); HomoSEP (IIT Madras) cleans septic tanks (b-i); Daksh (DRDO) handles and defuses IEDs/bombs (c-ii); Vyommitra (ISRO) is the half-humanoid astronaut for the uncrewed Gaganyaan flight (d-iv).
Bandicoot was developed by Genrobotics of Kerala for manhole and sewer cleaning, helping to end manual scavenging.

secs.t: Indigenous processors → developer and India Semiconductor Mission

x: The India Semiconductor Mission was launched in 2021, provides a ₹76,000 crore PLI, and has ₹65,000 crore committed under it.
DHRUV64 was developed by C-DAC, SHAKTI by IIT Madras, AJIT by IIT Bombay and Vikram 3201 by ISRO’s Semi-Conductor Laboratory, Chandigarh.
DHRUV64 is a 64-bit RISC-V processor developed by C-DAC for 5G, IoT and automotive applications.
The OSAT pilot line under the India Semiconductor Mission is at
Sanand, Gujarat

secs.t: Missions, policies, standards and Centres of Excellence → body

x: SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0, meaning Smart Advanced Manufacturing and Rapid Transformation Hub, is a Ministry of Heavy Industries initiative that promotes Industry 4.0 through demonstration centres.
The MeitY-NASSCOM IoT Centres of Excellence are located at
Bengaluru, Gurugram, Gandhinagar and Visakhapatnam
The measures include liberalised Drone Rules, 2021, DigitalSky, PLI, Drone Shakti, DGCA-approved training institutes and Bharat Drone Mahotsav.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Sri Sathya Sai district
, near Bengaluru, was offered for aerospace, drone and semiconductor manufacturing.
Andhra Pradesh has an
Industry Policy 4.0
(the Industrial Development Policy 4.0, 2024-29), matching the Industry 4.0 / Fourth Industrial Revolution theme; the WEF is also setting up a Fourth Industrial Revolution Centre in the State.

rows.title: Artificial intelligence and machine learning - concepts, applications, national AI strategy, ethical concerns

secs.t: AI — types, learning methods and terms

x: NLP lets machines understand and generate human language, as in chatbots and translation (a-iii); computer vision interprets images, as in facial recognition (b-ii); generative AI creates new text, images and music (c-iv); recommender systems suggest content from past behaviour, as on Netflix (d-i).
LLMs are general-purpose models trained on massive datasets and can perform multiple language tasks without task-specific retraining.

secs.t: AI tools and platforms → developer

x: Pratham was developed by Assert AI, Hanooman is associated with the BharatGPT ecosystem and Seetha Mahalakshmi Healthcare, Krutrim with Ola, and OpenHathi with Sarvam AI.
Bhashini is linked to MeitY and the National Language Translation Mission, was launched in July 2022, covers 22 scheduled languages and uses crowdsourcing through Bhasha Daan.

secs.t: AI applications → sector (agriculture, health, security)

x: The Microsoft–ICRISAT AI sowing application was piloted in
Kurnool
district in 2016 to provide yield-oriented sowing advisories.
The AI4AP Police Project is being piloted in
Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya
for traffic management, crime prediction and investigation.
AI in counter-terrorism includes risk forecasting, CCTV analytics and tracking of terror financing.

secs.t: National AI strategy, missions and programmes → year and outlay — NITI Aayog strategy

x: Compute Capacity provides affordable GPU compute, the Innovation Centre develops indigenous foundation models and LMMs, the Datasets Platform provides public-sector datasets, and FutureSkills supports courses and labs.
The IndiaAI Mission was launched in 2024 with an outlay of ₹10,371.92 crore and includes sovereign compute of more than 10,000 GPUs, AI start-ups, Indian datasets and foundation models.

secs.t: National AI strategy, missions and programmes → year and outlay — Compute and hubs

x: AIRAWAT is a common AI compute platform.
MATH is an AI/ML hub involving the Department of Science and Technology, the Telangana Government and T-Hub.
YUVAi is intended for students of classes 8 to 12.

secs.t: AI education — FIRSTs and institutes

x: The NIELIT campus at Amaravati is billed as India's first dedicated Quantum and AI university campus.
The programme has 66 seats and is the first engineering programme offered by a Sanskrit university.
AICTE declared 2025 the ‘Year of AI’.
IIT Hyderabad
was the first in India to offer a full B.Tech in AI (2019).

secs.t: Ethical concerns, threats and challenges

x: GPU shortages, dependence on imported chips and a shortage of frontier-AI skills are all identified as challenges.
Identification without consent, mass surveillance and predictive policing that threatens due process are ethical concerns.
Deepfakes can occur as text, voice, image or video, and facial-recognition accuracy can vary with lighting and pose.

secs.t: Global AI governance — summits → host city, GPAI, EU AI Act

x: The EU AI Act sorts AI systems into unacceptable, high, limited and minimal risk categories. ‘
Unlimited risk
’ is not one of those categories.

REAIM 2023 was held at The Hague (a-ii), the AI Seoul Summit 2024 in Seoul (b-iii) and the AI Action Summit 2025 in Paris (c-i), so A. B swaps The Hague and Paris, C swaps The Hague and Seoul, and D swaps Seoul and Paris.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The issue concerned the lack of a statutory framework for high-risk AI used in
welfare delivery
The criticism is expressed as ‘safety is declining, and big money is on the rise’, indicating a shift from safety emphasis towards scale and investment.
The Economic Survey 2025–26 favours
small, application-specific models and a state-built AI-OS modelled on UPI and Aadhaar

rows.title: Emerging technology frontiers - artificial intelligence, quantum computing, robotics, 3D printing, advanced materials
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-16

secs.t: Pioneers → contributions (father of AI, Turing test)

x: John McCarthy coined the term ‘Artificial Intelligence’ in 1956 at the Dartmouth conference.
The Turing test examines whether a machine’s responses can be distinguished from human replies.
Turing originally called his test the '
Imitation Game

secs.t: Terms → meaning (AI and quantum)

x: LLMs are trained on very large collections of text and are designed to generate or process language.
GPUs are well suited to parallel computation, while FPGAs can be reprogrammed for customised acceleration.
Q-Day denotes the future point when quantum computing becomes capable of breaking widely used public-key cryptography.
The spherical C60 fullerene molecule is commonly called a
buckyball

secs.t: AI platforms, labs and Centres of Excellence → developer

x: CAIR is a DRDO laboratory dealing with AI and robotics and is located in Bengaluru.
NM-ICPS
Technology Innovation Hubs
include AI and machine-learning verticals.
BharatGen is a government Indian-language multimodal AI project; Bhashini is associated with MeitY; BharatGPT was developed by CoRover; and AIRAWAT is the C-DAC Pune AI supercomputer.

secs.t: Quantum — applications, milestones, FIRSTs and days

x: Entanglement sudden death denotes abrupt total loss of entanglement, and the Raman Research Institute demonstrated that a suitably timed local quantum flip could delay or prevent it.
The report sets 2029 for Critical Information Infrastructure and 2033 for other systems.
The UN declared 2025 the International Year of
Quantum Science and Technology
, marking the centenary of quantum mechanics.

secs.t: Nanotechnology and advanced materials → developer

x: IIT Mandi developed the biodegradable nanoparticles; IISc Bengaluru worked on carbon-nanotube transistors; C-DAC on graphene flexible electronics; and IIT Delhi on perovskite displays and conductive nanofibres.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism is that without sovereign compute and sovereign or indigenous AI models, India may become dependent on external AI infrastructure and technologies.
NIELIT's Quantum & AI campus is at
Amaravati
, on 8.5 acres at about Rs 730.70 crore.

rows.title: Big data, cloud computing, edge computing and data centres

secs.t: Big data — definition, the Vs and data terms

x: Big data refers to large volumes of high-velocity, complex and variable data.
The classic three Vs are
Volume, Velocity and Variety
Data mining finds patterns and relationships in large datasets.
A data lake stores raw data in its native format, whether structured or unstructured.
Visibility
is not included in that list.

secs.t: Cloud, fog and edge — models and terms

x: IaaS provides infrastructure such as servers, storage and networks; PaaS provides an application-development platform; SaaS provides ready software over the web.
SaaS delivers ready-to-use software over the web; such software may be accessible on mobile and may allow customisation of the user interface and fields.
In serverless computing, the provider manages and scales the servers, while the developer writes functions and is billed according to usage.

secs.t: Companies → cloud services, providers and investments

x: Google Drive belongs to Google, iCloud to Apple, Dropbox to Dropbox Inc., and S3 to Amazon Web Services.
The proposals in the Visakhapatnam region are associated with Google, Reliance, TCS (HyperVault), CtrlS and GMR.
Google and Andhra Pradesh agreed on an artificial intelligence, cloud and digital-governance task force during a Singapore visit.

secs.t: Policies, platforms and frameworks → body and year — Data governance

x: MeghRaj or GI Cloud is the Government of India's cloud initiative, hosting e-services on the NIC cloud and promoting interoperability and security standards.

All four statements reflect proposals in the draft National Data Centre Policy: a 20-year tax holiday, GST input credit on capital assets, Permanent Establishment status for qualifying foreign firms, and location and renewable-energy incentives.

secs.t: Policies, platforms and frameworks → body and year — Analytics for environment and governance

x: Together, these technologies can analyse large datasets, predict pollution, optimise resource use and support governance decisions.
The Economic Survey 2025–26 refers to
UDISE+, AISHE and ABDM
surveys combined with AI to identify health hotspots.

secs.t: Data centres — capacity data, metrics and resource use

x: India's data-centre capacity rose from 375 MW in 2020 to
in 2026 and is estimated at about 8 GW by 2030.
Mumbai
holds 52% of India's data-centre capacity, followed by Chennai, Delhi NCR and Bengaluru.
Tier I is basic, whereas Tier IV is fully fault-tolerant and is associated with approximately 99.995% availability.

secs.t: AP — Visakhapatnam data-centre and AI hub

x: Nara Lokesh
set a policy for developing multi-gigawatt data-centre capacity along the Vizag–Kapuluppada corridor.
The identified advantages are a submarine cable landing station, sea-breeze cooling, Seismic Zone II and nearness to Southeast Asia.
AP-Transco lists
16 projects with about 9.10 GW of IT load
and plans a 765/400/220 kV grid to carry over 15 GW by 2034.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Economic Survey 2025–26 links rising data-centre capacity with cloud computing, artificial intelligence, IoT and 5G.
Visakhapatnam
is projected to become India’s biggest data-centre hub, with about 6 GW of capacity over ten years.
Hyperscale data centres raise concerns about power and water strain, while India also relies on foreign cloud providers for AI compute.

rows.title: Blockchain and distributed ledger technology; cryptocurrency and CBDC (e-rupee)

secs.t: Blockchain — definition and FIRSTs

x: A blockchain is a time-stamped series of immutable records managed by a cluster of computers rather than a single owner.
Bitcoin was introduced in 2009 by the pseudonymous creator
Satoshi Nakamoto
Cryptocurrency is decentralised and peer-to-peer, uses keys and wallets, and may use mining for validation.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (ledger, crypto, Web 3.0)

x: A
distributed ledger
is a shared ledger replicated across many nodes without a central validator.
Relevant stakeholders can be given visibility while replicated copies and consensus protect the records from unauthorised alteration.
Stablecoins are pegged to fiat, commodities or crypto-assets in an attempt to provide relative price stability.
Tokenisation
converts ownership rights in an asset into a blockchain token.

secs.t: Types — public vs private; PoW vs PoS

x: Bitcoin represents the public/permissionless model, while private/permissioned systems may be controlled by an organisation or consortium; AP DigiVerify is an example cited for the latter.
Proof of Work uses puzzle-solving miners, while Proof of Stake selects validators based on staked coins.
Bitcoin is associated with
Proof of Work
, in which miners solve complex computational puzzles.

secs.t: Regulation, strategies and platforms → body and year

x: Drunix is an open-source private blockchain re-engineered from Hyperledger Fabric.
The National Strategy on Blockchain was published by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology in
December 2021
NeGD
had earlier released an approach paper related to blockchain before the National Strategy was published.
Vishvasya is
MeitY's Blockchain-as-a-Service technology stack
, introduced in 2024.

secs.t: AP blockchain pilots — Mee Bhoomi and AP DigiVerify

x: The Mee Bhoomi-Blockchain pilot was launched by Chief Minister Naidu on 23 July 2026.
AP DigiVerify is a permissioned-blockchain PaaS designed for tamper-proof certificate verification.
Mee Bhoomi-Mee Hakku issues
tamper-proof pattadar passbooks

secs.t: Universal angles

x: However, the reported reduction in Andhra Pradesh land disputes does not constitute the stated reason for the Supreme Court's suggestion.
The identified concerns are scalability, proof-of-work energy use, interoperability and regulatory uncertainty.
Bitcoin, in 2009, was identified as the first cryptocurrency and the first use of blockchain.

rows.title: Telecom technologies - 3G to 5G and 6G roadmap, satellite communication, optical fibre

secs.t: Telecom institutions → role, and milestones (FIRSTs)

x: TEC is DoT’s technical body for telecom standards and equipment testing.
C-DOT was set up in 1984, DoT was created in 1985, MTNL and VSNL were established in 1986, and TRAI was set up in 1997.
The world’s first 5G launch was in South Korea in April 2019.
India's first experimental satellite telecommunication activity was conducted in 1975.

secs.t: Mobile generations 1G to 6G → core technology

x: GPRS is associated with 2.5G and EDGE with 2.75G, both representing faster GSM data developments.
LTE and OFDMA are associated with 4G, and VoLTE denotes voice carried over the LTE data network.
5G applications include eMBB, IoT, AR/VR, remote surgery and autonomous vehicles.
TRAI prefers Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (
C-V2X
) for vehicle communication over the stated 4G/5G alternatives.

secs.t: Terms → meaning (wireless, 5G, satellite, optical)

x: Sub-6 GHz bands provide wider coverage and better penetration, while mmWave bands provide very high data rates but have short range.
Network slicing creates virtual network slices from one physical network, allowing different services to receive suitably configured resources.
FSO communication sends data through laser or light beams without using fibre cables.

secs.t: 5G and 6G — launch, funding, indigenous stack, labs and alliances

x: TTDF was introduced in 2022, receives 5% of Digital Bharat Nidhi collections—about Rs 500 crore annually—and has funded 5G Stack, 6G and quantum-encryption projects.
IIITDM Kurnool
ranked first in DoT’s January–June 2026 gradation in all four categories.
The Bharat 6G Vision document was released in March 2023 and aims for India to lead the design, development and deployment of 6G by 2030.

secs.t: Acts, rulings and rules — spectrum, satcom, EMF

x: TRAI recommended auctioning all available spectrum across nine bands, a uniform 35% spectrum cap, and reducing the new-entrant net-worth requirement from Rs 100 crore to Rs 50 crore per service area.
The Department of Telecommunications rule requires all telecom data and logs of infrastructure providers to be stored
in India

secs.t: Satellite communication — GEO vs LEO and operators

x: GEO satellites are approximately 35,786 km above Earth, remain fixed over one spot and have higher latency.
The
GSAT series
is cited as an example of GEO satellites, and GSAT-7 and GSAT-7A are associated with defence applications.
Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb and Amazon Kuiper
are identified as LEO constellations.
Starlink has more than 8,000 LEO satellites and received its GMPCS licence in India in 2025.

secs.t: Optical fibre — features, undersea cables and national fibre data

x: Exam angle: statement sets on TIR, light signals and single-mode fibre ("All of the above").
Optical fibre
provides faster data transmission than copper cable, radio waves and satellite signals.
NOFN was planned to link all 2,50,000 Gram Panchayats over existing PSU fibre (BSNL, RailTel, Power Grid), uses GPON and was later renamed BharatNet.

secs.t: Wi-Fi vs Li-Fi and alternative access — standards and projects

x: The reported link was the world’s first 2 Tbit/s free-space optical link, using small terminals for satellites and high-altitude platform stations.
WLAN or Wi-Fi uses radio waves for short-range wireless communication.
Wi-Fi 6 corresponds to IEEE 802.11ax and Wi-Fi 7 to IEEE 802.11be.
Project Loon attempted to deliver internet connectivity using
high-altitude balloons

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Chief Minister directed telecom operators to complete new towers within 100 days.
India rose to 49th in the Network Readiness Index 2024 from 60th earlier.

sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-19

secs.t: Fourth Industrial Revolution — origin and stages

x: Artificial intelligence, robotics, the Internet of Things and quantum computing are identified with the Fourth Industrial Revolution.
Smart factories use
cyber-physical systems
that integrate physical production processes with digital technologies.
All three statements correctly describe the principal technological bases of the First, Second and Third Industrial Revolutions.
Klaus Schwab, founder of the World Economic Forum (WEF), coined the term in 2016.

secs.t: Terms and full forms → meaning

x: Exam angle: "What does IoT stand for?" - Internet of Things.
NFT is a Non-Fungible Token (unique blockchain token), DLT is Distributed Ledger Technology, and Web 3.0 is the decentralised, blockchain-based internet.
Li-Fi means Light Fidelity, uses LEDs for data transmission and is noted for better bandwidth and security than Wi-Fi.
Network slicing creates multiple virtual networks over one physical network using Software-Defined Networking and Network Functions Virtualization.

secs.t: IoT — architecture layers and uses

x: The three layers are perception, which uses sensors; network, which transmits data; and application, which provides user services.
Smart grids, logistics tracking and smart buildings
, including HVAC systems, are additional IoT applications.
The four IoT pillars are
device, data, analytics and connectivity
IoT devices are networked to communicate with each other without human intervention.

secs.t: Governance applications → agency (data, crime, blockchain)

x: The AP State Data Lake cross-links RCH health data with POSHAN data and housing data with land pattas to help plug leakages.
I4C's NCAP uses AI and big data to analyse
crime trends
Blockchain governance uses include land records, digital certificates and farm insurance, among others.
DigiVerify is Andhra Pradesh's blockchain governance application: a permissioned-blockchain platform for tamper-proof certificate verification.

secs.t: 5G and 6G — features, labs, alliances

x: 5G can provide latency as low as 1 millisecond, massive device connectivity and high reliability.
Airtel's ‘Priority Postpaid’ offering raised a debate on
net neutrality
6G is expected in the early 2030s.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: IIITDM Kurnool
topped the Department of Telecommunications’ 5G labs ranking in July 2026.
Network slicing has generated a debate concerning its compatibility with
net neutrality
The Andhra Pradesh–Google AI/cloud task force concerns
artificial intelligence and cloud
technologies.

sub: Group-II M2-B-18: Digital India Mission - pillars, key initiatives and impact

secs.t: E-governance — models, pillars, phases, benefits vs challenges

x: NIC solutions serving government departments represent Government-to-Government interaction, or
G2G
Online fraud
is a challenge of e-governance; data costs and funding gaps in some States are also identified challenges.
Gartner's four phases run
Information → Interaction → Transaction → Transformation
(MPPSC 2025).
E-governance lowers the cost of government, increases citizen input (UPPSC 2024) and improves transparency.

secs.t: Implementing bodies → role

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2017 key gave
NITI Aayog
for the drive to make 100% of G2C transactions digital.
The NeGP was drafted by DeitY, now MeitY, with the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (
DARPG
NeGD, or National e-Governance Division, is
MeitY’s programme-management arm under Digital India Corporation
CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. is the special purpose vehicle and implementing agency of CSCs.

secs.t: National e-Governance Plan, 2006 — core infrastructure and MMP categories

x: The three tiers are CSCs at the front end, SWAN as the network, and SDC at the back end.
SWAN provides network links from State headquarters to block or taluka levels.
Land Records and e-District are State MMPs, while eCourts is an Integrated MMP.
e-Panchayat
is a State category MMP.
e-Biz
is an Integrated MMP.

secs.t: Mission Mode Projects → ministry and year

x: MCA21 is the Ministry of Corporate Affairs' online company filing (G2B) project.
e-Procurement uses
online tenders
, which are intended to help prevent collusion.
The e-Panchayat MMP provides
core panchayat software
under the Panchayati Raj domain.
The GS NIRNAY app covers Gram Sabha decisions and is associated with the e-Panchayat initiative.

secs.t: Digital India and e-Kranti — launch, vision areas, nine pillars, principles — Digital India - launch and nature

x: Digital India aims to transform India into a
digitally empowered society and knowledge economy
These measures are components of the vision area called
digital empowerment of citizens
High-speed internet, cradle-to-grave digital identity, Common Service Centre access and cloud locker are examples under digital infrastructure as a core utility.
Digital India was launched on
1 July 2015
(APPSC 2025 key).

secs.t: Digital India and e-Kranti — launch, vision areas, nine pillars, principles — Nine pillars, with latest figures

x: Exam angle: "not a pillar" options are usually initiatives (Aadhaar, DigiLocker, UPI) or look-alike names.
Electronic Governance, National Knowledge Network, Cyber Security and the
IndiaAI Mission
are included among the stated Digital India sub-schemes.
Early Harvest Programmes comprise quick-win projects such as biometric attendance and Wi-Fi in universities; they are not defined as long-term university research grants.

secs.t: Digital India and e-Kranti — launch, vision areas, nine pillars, principles — e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0)

x: E-Kranti is NeGP 2.0, approved in 2015 under Digital India, with the vision 'Transforming e-Governance for Transforming Governance'.
The principles include transformation not translation, integrated not individual services, and cloud by default.
Mobile first, language localisation, process re-engineering in every MMP and cloud by default are all stated principles of e-Kranti.

secs.t: Digital initiatives → launch year (2009 to 2022)

x: Exam angle: chronology Aadhaar → MyGov → PM eVIDYA → ONDC (APPSC 2024 key: 1-2-3-4).
MyGov came in July 2014, UPI and BHIM in 2016, UMANG in 2017.
PM eVIDYA was launched in 2020 in response to the educational requirements arising during
the pandemic
Aadhaar was launched in 2009, MyGov in 2014, PM eVIDYA in 2020 and ONDC in 2022.

secs.t: India Stack, DPI and education platforms → role

x: Bhashini is
an AI language platform integrated with NIC tools such as CollabFiles
, supporting access to services in Indian languages.
India Stack consists of open and interoperable public digital rails, including Aadhaar, UPI, DigiLocker, CoWIN, ONDC and Account Aggregator.
PM eVIDYA uses the One Class, One TV Channel approach through DTH, radio and podcasts, and integrates DIKSHA and SWAYAM.

secs.t: Impact data and the digital divide

x: Rural digital gaps particularly concern Gram Panchayat fibre connectivity through BharatNet and 4G coverage in villages.
UPI transaction volume increased approximately
over the stated period, during which UPI became 10 years old.
PMGDISHA is a rural digital literacy scheme launched in 2017, with the aim of covering one person per household.

x: It was a Singapore delegation that studied AP's RTGS Data Lake and Command Centre (July 2026).
The sequence is NeGP in 2006, Digital India in 2015, and e-Kranti, or NeGP 2.0, in 2015.

DPI was reported to have raised the digital economy's share to approximately
of GDP.
