rows.title: National Policy on Information Technology - objectives and outcomes
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-20

secs.t: IT milestones → year (NIC 1976 to C2S 2022)

x: The milestones occurred in the order NIC in 1976, National Task Force in 1998, IT Act in 2000 and NeGP in 2006.
C-DAC was established at Pune in 1988 to build the
PARAM supercomputer
The IT Act, 2000 gave legal recognition to electronic records and digital signatures, and its 2008 amendment addressed e-signatures and cybercrime-related provisions.

secs.t: Policies → vision, objectives and targets (NPIT 2012, NPE 2019) — NPIT 2012 - vision and objectives

x: The twin goals were universal access to the benefits of ICT and making India a global hub and destination for IT and ITES services by 2020.
The policy sought to spread IT activity to Tier II and Tier III cities because the major established hubs were highly concentrated and nearing saturation.
Digital India, Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet and DigiLocker are all identified as initiatives that put the policy vision into practice.

secs.t: Policies → vision, objectives and targets (NPIT 2012, NPE 2019) — NPIT 2012 targets

x: Exam angle: match target figure to category; "$300 bn by 2020" is the most-asked figure.
IT-ITES revenue was targeted at US$300 billion; IT exports at US$200 billion; skilled manpower at 10 million additional workers; and e-literacy at one e-literate person in every household.
NPE 2019 aimed to establish India as a global hub for Electronics System Design and Manufacturing, including chipsets.

secs.t: Schemes → outlay and support (PLI, SPECS, MPMS, ISM, C2S)

x: MPMS has ₹62,500 crore for FY 2026-27 to 2030-31 and replaces PLI (Large Scale Electronics).
CMOS silicon fabs receive up to 40% capital subsidy, compound and display fabs 35%, advanced packaging 35%, and R&D up to 75% of project cost.
C2S (2022) builds chip-design talent, targeting 85,000 B.Tech/M.Tech/PhD students over five years.

secs.t: Semiconductor units → company → location

x: RRP Electronics is associated with a semiconductor and OSAT facility in Sri Sathya Sai district of Andhra Pradesh.
Tata's (TSAT) OSAT unit is at Jagiroad, Assam.

secs.t: IT institutions → role

x: MeitY handles policy and Digital India coordination; NASSCOM represents IT-BPM firms and partners in IoT CoEs; STPI runs export-oriented parks and CoEs; NIC provides government IT and e-governance services.
MeitY handles policy on IT, electronics, the internet other than ISP licensing, and cyber security, and coordinates Digital India.
C-DAC’s stated roles include R&D involving PARAM supercomputers, implementation of C2S and a centre at Amaravati Quantum Valley.

secs.t: Outcomes data — IT exports, digital economy, electronics output

x: TCS, Infosys and Wipro
are identified as major Indian IT-service companies contributing to India's position as one of the world's largest IT-service exporters.
GCCs perform functions for their parent multinational corporations, whereas outsourcing vendors provide services to other organisations; therefore; .
The digital economy is about 12-14% of GDP now and is projected to reach
about 20%

secs.t: AP IT & GCC Policy 4.0 — incentives, IT hubs and data centres

x: The policy covers 2024-29 and came into force on 12 December 2024 for five years.
The policy promotes
IT parks, co-working spaces and neighbourhood workspaces
The AP Data Centre Policy provides for adding up to
1 GW
of data-centre capacity.
Visakhapatnam is associated with AI data projects with Anakapalli, a cable landing station and an Infosys campus expected to create about 7,000 jobs.

The continuing offline population shows that digital access is not yet universal.
IT and electronics attracted more than
₹18,210 crore
in one Andhra Pradesh Cabinet round.

ICT enhances citizen engagement and improves service delivery, including through transparency and real-time monitoring.

; e-Kranti = 44.

MeghRaj, the GI Cloud, now provides government cloud hosting.

e-Pramaan
; new driving licence =
SARATHI
(not VAHAN).

Aadhaar-based biometric Digital Life Certificates for pensioners
e-Taal 3.0, operated by NIC and MeitY, provides
statistics on e-transactions and e-services

Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
in September 2016.

secs.t: Grievance and sectoral portals → ministry

x: SAMADHAN DIDI is
an AI voice chatbot built with Bhashini
and linked to CPGRAMS.

ABDM was launched in 2021 by the
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
to create a national interoperable digital health ecosystem.
e-Hospital handles
online patient registration, appointments and hospital management

x: Exam angle: APPSC 2022 asked for the wrong pair: "Khajane = land records" is wrong, because Bhoomi does land records.

Project Ganga is described as a digital expressway providing
last-mile rural broadband through local Digital Service Providers
in Uttar Pradesh.

secs.t: AP digital governance — CARD, e-Pragati, RTGS, Mana Mitra

x: Exam angle: "Which app was introduced on 30 Jan 2025 in AP?" -
Mana Mitra
Mana Mitra enabled more than 500 services, used WhatsApp-based conversational governance, and had an Outcome Budget target of up to 1,000 services.
RTGS operates through its
Data Lake, Data Lens and Command & Control Centre
, supported by real-time dashboards.

secs.t: Conferences, awards and schemes → organiser and year

x: The NCeG is organised by DARPG together with MeitY and the host state; the 28th edition (2025) was at Visakhapatnam.
State Collaboration Initiatives is a
DARPG
scheme, revised in 2015-16, that funds replication of PM-awarded and National e-Governance-awarded initiatives.
NeSDA benchmarking of e-governance service delivery began in 2019.

secs.t: Full forms → meaning

x: SDC stands for State Data Centre.
NeGP is the
National e-Governance Plan
MMP stands for Mission Mode Project, not Mission Monitoring Portal.

x: The reported UMANG flaw exposed EPFO Universal Account Numbers (UANs) and Aadhaar numbers in plain text.
Sanjeevani is scheduled for August 2026 and combines ABHA IDs and a wellness app with links to PHCs, 108, 104, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine.
Data security of aggregator portals is a significant criticism, particularly because multiple services and datasets may be brought together on one platform.

secs.t: Digital public infrastructure — India Stack layers, ONDC, Account Aggregator

x: India Stack comprises Aadhaar for identity, eSign and DigiLocker for paperless services, UPI for cashless payments, and DEPA/Account Aggregator for consent-based data sharing.
CoWIN, Aarogya Setu, DigiLocker and DIKSHA
are identified as other open platforms.
ONDC is an open e-commerce network intended to reduce dependence on dominant platforms and break platform monopolies.

secs.t: Aadhaar — FIRSTs, format, biometrics and scale

x: Aadhaar supports DBT under the JAM trinity, Jeevan Pramaan digital life certificates, and bank and mobile KYC.
Ranjana Sonawane
was the first Indian citizen to receive an Aadhaar number.
Tembhli village in Nandurbar district of Maharashtra was the first Aadhaar village and was the place where the first Aadhaar number was issued.
Aadhaar captures ten fingerprints, two irises and a face photograph.

secs.t: Acts, rules and policies → year (Aadhaar, open APIs, payments)

x: Aadhaar's open APIs are authentication, e-KYC and e-Sign (under MeitY's Policy on Open APIs, 2015, via API Setu).
UIDAI became statutory under the Aadhaar Act, 2016, functions under MeitY, and the Act was amended in 2019.
The Aadhaar Act covers enrolment, authentication and targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services.
NUEs are RBI's move to end NPCI's monopoly in retail payments.

secs.t: Payment systems and products → operator

x: UPI allows one application to route payments from several bank accounts through a Virtual Payment Address such as name@bank.
UPI 2.0 includes overdraft-account linking, pre-authorised payments, signed merchant QR codes and a daily limit of Rs 2 lakh.
FASTag (NETC) is operated by NPCI with NHAI and IHMCL, not by RBI alone.
AePS enables cash withdrawal and balance enquiry at micro-ATMs using Aadhaar-based authentication.

secs.t: Data — UPI scale, digital payments growth, DBT and PMJDY

x: UPI accounted for approximately
of digital payments by volume in FY 2025–26.
The cumulative amount transferred through DBT was reported as approximately
Rs 44 lakh crore
by May 2025.
More than half of PMJDY accounts were reported to be held by women.

secs.t: DBT — JAM trinity, routing, mission and AP launch

x: PAHAL, the LPG subsidy scheme, was the first application of JAM.
DBT routing uses CPSMS, now known as PFMS, and NPCI’s Aadhaar Payment Bridge.
The DBT Mission is now located in the
Cabinet Secretariat
DBT was inaugurated at Gollaprolu in East Godavari on 6 January 2013 by Jairam Ramesh along with Chief Minister Kiran Kumar Reddy.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: UPI recorded a FY 2025–26 record and accounted for 49 percent of the world’s real-time payments.
Biometric exclusion, privacy and data-centralisation concerns, and the digital divide are identified criticisms.

x: The Amended BharatNet Programme provides for a PPP model, a greater role for States, revenue sharing, last-mile connectivity and links with 5G.
Digital Bharat Nidhi
runs the Memoranda of Cooperation for the Amended BharatNet Programme.
5% of DBN collections (~Rs 500 crore a year) goes to the
Telecom Technology Development Fund

x: PM-WANI is a public Wi-Fi initiative launched in December 2020, with 3.15 lakh hotspots reported.
India was described as the world’s second-largest mobile maker, while electronics was identified as the third-largest export category.
SPECS is the scheme providing incentives for
electronic components and semiconductors
EMC 2.0 is the modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters scheme, introduced in 2020.

secs.t: AP and village angle — BharatNet MoC and Digital Village pilots → place

x: The MoC (22 Feb 2026, Amaravati) was signed between the Digital Bharat Nidhi Administrator and the AP government for 13,426 village panchayats, with the Centre committing Rs 2,432 crore and the state SPV being Andhra Pradesh BharatNet Infrastructure Ltd.
The AP Samriddhi Kendra offers passport and Aadhaar services, bill payments, soil testing, drone spraying and AI training.

secs.t: MeghRaj GI Cloud — characteristics, models, architecture

x: MeghRaj is the GI Cloud initiative started by the Department of Electronics and Information Technology (DeitY).
The five characteristics are on-demand self-service, ubiquitous network access, metered use, elasticity and resource pooling.
MeitY empanels private Cloud Service Providers for government use.
Public, private, hybrid and community are deployment models, whereas IaaS, PaaS and SaaS are service models.

secs.t: Digital literacy schemes → target and data

x: NDLM and DISHA refer to the digital literacy initiatives that preceded PMGDISHA, with DISHA expanded as Digital Saksharta Abhiyan.
At closure, PMGDISHA had 7.35 crore registered beneficiaries, 6.39 crore trained beneficiaries and 4.78 crore certified beneficiaries.
E&ICT Academy Phase-II (MeitY, 5 years) targets training 1,35,000 faculty through 14 agencies including IITs, NIT, NIELIT and CDAC.

x: BhashaNet was launched to promote digital inclusion by advancing Universal Acceptance, including support for diverse languages and scripts.
Universal Acceptance requires domain names and e-mail addresses in any language or script, including Indian-language domains, to work properly in every application.
The portal unveiled by NIXI and MeitY on UA Day (21 March 2024) is BhashaNet, not Bhashini.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The assessment indicated that about 38% of Indians were still offline.
AP FiberNet reached more than 4,000 tribal hamlets in the
Eastern Ghats
Excessive digital literacy is not a stated challenge.

succeeded e-Seva as a single-window G2C delivery mechanism.
The EDS Department prints MeeSeva certificates, while the Education Department issues migration certificates to passed candidates.
MeeSeva services are delivered through MeeSeva franchise centres as well as the online portal.
MeeSeva also serves as an enrolment channel for schemes such as

, but statutory powers remain with the SROs.

Disha SOS serves women's safety, AP Police Seva provides citizen police services, Sanjeevani provides an ABHA-linked profile, and Pura Seva handles municipal services.

secs.t: RTGS and Mana Mitra — reviews and data

x: Mana Mitra includes services such as
rice card eKYC
, electricity bills, 1-B Adangal, APSRTC tickets and temple darshan services.
The July 2026 directions included redrafting the Business Rules and strengthening
crowd-sourced grievance tracking
Mana Mitra grew from 150 services (Jan 2025) to 865 (2025-26), with a cap of 5 user inputs and 2 documents per service.

secs.t: AP IT policies and institutions

x: The AP Cyber Security Policy was formulated in 2017 to establish a secure cyber ecosystem for citizens, businesses and government.
Kaushalam is an AI-powered platform for employability and skill verification.
Effective Governance and AI-based Public Services
” is one of the pillars of Swarna Andhra @2047.
The monitoring framework tracks KPIs and uses OBD/IVRS calls and bulk WhatsApp for feedback.

was the first State to introduce the paperless e-Cabinet system.
HIMSWAN belongs to Himachal Pradesh; Digital Seva Setu and GSWAN belong to Gujarat; and Seva One is Karnataka's digital citizen-services initiative.

13,426 panchayats
The debate concerns the impact of RSKs on document writers’ livelihoods, while the State has assured that Sub-Registrar Offices are not being privatised.

rows.title: Netiquettes - digital etiquette, digital literacy, misinformation and fake news

secs.t: Terms → meaning (online behaviour and information disorder)

x: Nomophobia is the
irrational fear of being without one's mobile phone
, including situations involving no signal, low battery or insufficient balance.
Misinformation
is false content spread without an intent to deceive, including innocent mistakes and rumours.
Filter bubbles arise because algorithms prioritise content by user preference, isolating users from other viewpoints.

secs.t: Netiquettes and digital citizenship — dos and don'ts

x: Posting others' photos or data without consent is a don't, whether or not the source is credited.
Digital freedom is linked with responsible conduct, including constructive online dialogue and respect for privacy.
A responsible digital citizen identifies misinformation, verifies sources, protects personal data, respects privacy and participates in civil discourse.
Online grievance redressal
, e-consultations and access to open government data are rights-related aspects of digital citizenship.

secs.t: Online safety practices — recommended vs not

x: Exam angle: "which is NOT a safe practice" and odd-one-out questions.
Accepting friend requests from unknown persons without caution
is not a safe online practice.
Passwords, biometrics and multi-factor authentication
are authentication methods used to verify a user's identity.
A friend's account or identity may have been hacked, so the request should be independently verified before payment.

secs.t: Digital literacy — days, schemes and data

x: PMGDISHA promotes digital literacy among rural people, with the aim of having one digitally literate person in every family; it was launched by the Prime Minister at Gandhinagar.

ULLAS covers adults aged 15 years and above during 2022–27 and includes digital and financial literacy under Critical Life Skills; Himachal Pradesh was the fifth State/UT to achieve full functional literacy.

secs.t: Acts, rules, sections and court cases

x: Section 66E of the IT Act concerns privacy violation, Section 67 concerns obscene material, and Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita covers stalking, including monitoring electronic communication.
The April 2023 amendment provided for loss of safe harbour where content concerning the business of the Central Government was flagged as fake by the PIB Fact Check Unit.

secs.t: Fact-check bodies and counter-measures → body — PIB Fact Check Unit

x: WhatsApp
launched a tip line to help curb fake news ahead of the 2019 Lok Sabha election.
SAHYOG Portal is run by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the Ministry of Home Affairs for takedown notices, alongside the Cyber Crime Reporting Portal.
Platforms must remove flagged unlawful content within
three hours
of a court order or reasoned government intimation.

secs.t: Fact-check bodies and counter-measures → body — Deepfakes - responses

x: Measures for responding to deepfakes include the ECI advisory on mandatory labels for AI content in campaigns, DPDP Act penalties and I4C takedowns.
The
EU AI Act
mandates watermarking.
Media literacy, fact-checkers and platform policies to remove or down-rank fake content are counter-measures.
Minors may lack the skills needed to distinguish truth from misinformation.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Doxxing involves the unauthorised exposure of personal information and raises concerns relating to privacy and online safety.
Both statements are true, and the risk of executive overreach explains why regulation intended to curb fake news must also protect free speech.
The WHO lists Gaming Disorder in ICD-11; ICD is WHO's classification of diseases.

rows.title: Cyber security concerns - types of cyber crime, malware, ransomware, phishing, social engineering
sub: Group-II M2-B-21: Cyber security concerns - cyber crime types, threats to critical infrastructure and data breaches

secs.t: Security principles, cryptography terms and tools → function — Principles and cryptography terms

x: Because both sides need the same secret key, key sharing is the main problem of symmetric cryptography.
A digital signature is generated with the sender's private key and verified with the corresponding public key; it helps prove the message's origin and integrity.
Exposure compromises confidentiality, alteration compromises integrity, and denial of access compromises availability; together they cover all elements of the CIA triad.

secs.t: Security principles, cryptography terms and tools → function — Security tools → function

x: A
honeypot
is a decoy system designed to lure attackers and enable security teams to study their behaviour and techniques.
BOSS Linux is associated with C-DAC, Maya OS with Chakravyuh with the Ministry of Defence, M-Kavach with C-DAC Hyderabad, and CERT-In with CVE numbering for products made in India.
Virtual keyboards help protect against
keyloggers
by reducing the usefulness of recording physical keyboard keystrokes.

secs.t: Malware types → mechanism and example

x: Exam angle: "self-replicating without user action" = worm; "no self-replication, disguised" = trojan.
A
Trojan
is disguised as legitimate software, does not self-replicate and may open a backdoor for unauthorised access.
The AIIMS Delhi attack of 2022 is cited as an example of
ransomware
, which encrypts files or systems and demands payment for restoration.
A botnet consists of infected ‘zombie’ devices controlled remotely and may be used for DDoS attacks, spam or crypto-mining.

secs.t: Named malware and attacks → type, origin and FIRSTs

x: Exam angle: "Petya and WannaCry are related to" -
Ransomware
Elk Cloner, created by Rich Skrenta, is regarded as the first virus in the wild and affected Apple II computers in 1982.
Stuxnet was a worm containing rootkit components that sabotaged Siemens PLC-controlled uranium centrifuges at Iran’s Natanz facility.
Pegasus is state-grade zero-click spyware associated with Israel’s NSO Group and can exploit zero-days without requiring user interaction.
Petya and WannaCry are
ransomware
(APPSC-G2 2025): Petya encrypts the master boot record and WannaCry spread as a worm through EternalBlue, demanding ransom.

secs.t: Attack techniques → meaning

x: Spam = unsolicited bulk messages (ii); e-mail bombing = flooding an inbox to crash it (iii); man-in-the-middle = secret interception/alteration (iv); SQL injection = malicious database code via input fields (i).

Phishing = deceptive messages posing as a legitimate source (iii); vishing = phishing by voice calls (i); spoofing = faking a sender identity (ii); SQL injection = malicious database code through input fields (iv).

secs.t: Cyber crimes and frauds → meaning and law

x: Digital arrest is a criminal intimidation technique in which impostors claim that the victim is under arrest and demand money, often while keeping the victim on a video call.
SIM manipulation allows fraudsters to control the victim's mobile connection and divert OTPs, often after posing as bank officials through voice phishing.
Crypto-jacking is the unauthorised and concealed use of a victim's computing device to mine cryptocurrency; botnets may also be used for this purpose.

secs.t: Cyber attacks on India, cases and crime data — Attacks on Indian public systems

x: The e-Nagarpalika portal was attacked as an online civic tax payment system; AIIMS Delhi suffered ransomware; Kudankulam's administrative network was affected by malware; Cosmos Bank faced ATM/SWIFT fraud of about Rs 94 crore.
The e-Nagarpalika portal attack (Dec 2023) hit
Madhya Pradesh
's online civic tax payment portal (APPSC-G1 2024).

secs.t: Cyber attacks on India, cases and crime data — Crime cases and orders

x: The directions covered SOPs by the specified authorities, the use of zero FIRs and restoration of money to victims.
The Telangana case involved trafficking for cyber fraud, scam centres were linked to Myanmar and Laos, and FIU-India flagged Rs 800 crore in cross-border laundering.
APTS
(Andhra Pradesh Technology Services) monitors the State's Critical Government Infrastructure through APCSOC and has audited 270 GoAP applications.

secs.t: Cyber warfare, threat reports and exercises

x: All three statements reflect the framework and threat directions described in the MeitY Digital Threat Report 2025–26 for BFSI and digital payments.
Exercise Cyber Suraksha is a DRDO-led 12-day exercise intended to train the armed forces in cyber security and preparedness.
Cyber espionage is often state-sponsored and may employ spear-phishing and zero-days.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A is correct: AP Police signed an MoU with IIT Tirupati for a Cyber Crime Investigation and Training Academy focused on digital forensics and blockchain tracing.
The Andhra Pradesh Cyber Security Policy was introduced in 2017.
Cyber threats have implications for national security, the economy, public services and public trust in e-governance.

rows.title: Cyber security architecture - IT Act 2000 and amendments, CERT-In, NCIIPC, Cyber Swachhta Kendra, I4C
sub: Group-II M2-B-22: National Cyber Security Policy and institutional framework - CERT-In, NCIIPC, I4C, IT Act

secs.t: IT Act, 2000 — purpose, concepts and framework

x: The
Controller of Certifying Authorities
, or CCA, is the statutory regulator of electronic signatures.

The IT Act, 2000 introduced all three concepts: electronic record (legally recognised under Sec. 4), digital signature (Sec. 3 and 5) and Certifying Authority (licensed by the Controller of Certifying Authorities to issue Digital Signature Certificates).

secs.t: IT Act sections, amendment, case and rules → provision — Sections → subject

x: Exam angle: Section 4 = e-records, Section 5 = e-signatures (CGPSC 2022 match).
Section 4 concerns electronic records, Section 5 electronic signatures, Section 43A protection of sensitive personal data, and Section 66F cyber terrorism.
Sections 66C, 66D and 66E respectively deal with identity theft, cheating by personation using a computer, and violation of privacy.
Section 79 gives intermediaries safe harbour, lost if they fail to act on 'actual knowledge'.

secs.t: IT Act sections, amendment, case and rules → provision — Amendment, case and rules

x: The 2008 amendment added offences relating to sexually explicit material, video voyeurism, data leakage by intermediaries and e-commerce fraud; it did not create the NCCC.
The Supreme Court struck down Section 66A for violating freedom of speech and expression under
Article 19(1)(a)
, and held that it was not saved by Article 19(2).

secs.t: Digital signature and PKI — terms → meaning

x: A digital signature uses asymmetric cryptography together with a hash function to support verification of the signed electronic document.
Digital signatures provide authentication, integrity and non-repudiation, but a signature by itself does not guarantee confidentiality or secrecy of the document.
Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) is the framework of key pairs, Certifying Authorities and digital certificates for digital security: the private key signs and the public key verifies.

secs.t: CERT-In — status, functions and 2022 directions

x: CERT-In collects, analyses and disseminates incident information, issues forecasts and alerts, and coordinates emergency responses; conducting elections is not its function.
CERT-In operates Cyber Swachhta Kendra, serves as a CVE Numbering Authority for Indian products, and has empanelled 200 IT security auditing organisations.
NCCC is associated with
situational awareness of cyber threats

secs.t: Cyber bodies → parent and role (NCIIPC, Cyber Swachhta Kendra, I4C) — NCIIPC

x: NCIIPC was established under
Section 70A
and functions under the National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO).
Cyber Swachhta Kendra is the
Botnet Cleaning and Malware Analysis Centre
, set up and operated by CERT-In.
Cyber Swachhta Kendra was reported to cover about 98% of Indian internet users and 1,415 organisations as of July 2025.

secs.t: Cyber bodies → parent and role (NCIIPC, Cyber Swachhta Kendra, I4C) — I4C

x: The
National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal
, cybercrime.gov.in, is used for reporting cyber crimes, especially those against women and children.
The 1930 helpline is used to report financial fraud, particularly for action during the ‘golden hour’ to freeze funds.
The January 2026 CFCFRMS SOP permits banks to refund frauds below
without a court order.

secs.t: Cyber bodies → parent and role (NCIIPC, Cyber Swachhta Kendra, I4C) — National Cyber Security Coordinator

x: NCIIPC functions under the
National Technical Research Organisation
(NTRO).
NCSC is the National Cyber Security Coordinator associated with the National Security Council Secretariat.
CERT-In
, under MeitY, is the national incident response agency and is also a CVE Numbering Authority.
NCIIPC
(National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre), under NTRO, protects Critical Information Infrastructure.

secs.t: Portals, exercises and awareness days

x: Cyber Surakshit Bharat, associated with MeitY and launched in 2018, focused on training
Chief Information Security Officers
MySecurity.in is a platform for innovation in security-related web applications, launched by the Ministry of Home Affairs, and open to any individual or company (APPSC 2018 PYQ).
The cyber exercise on 'Scenario Building & Response' was held in
New Delhi
(APPSC 2019 PYQ).

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh set-up and international frameworks

x: APTS undertakes capacity building, supports critical-infrastructure security through APCSOC and audits government applications.
APTS
is the first CERT-In-empanelled organisation in Andhra Pradesh and is also identified as the first CERT-In-empanelled auditor in the State.
India, Russia and China
were identified as non-signatories to the Budapest Convention.
India was placed in Tier-1 of the ITU GCI 2024 with a score of 98.49.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court directed the formulation of standard operating procedures concerning digital-arrest scams.
A criticism is that the IT Act lacks specific provisions for AI impersonation and virtual-arrest threats.
The debate concerns surveillance and takedown powers versus free speech, with the wider discussion also linked to Section 66A, Section 69A and VPN regulation.

rows.title: National Cyber Security Policy 2013 and the national cyber crime policy framework

secs.t: National policies and plans → year, objectives, nodal agency — National Cyber Security Policy 2013

x: The policy aimed at resilient cyberspace, trained manpower, research and development, indigenous security technology and an Information Security Assurance Framework.
The target was to develop
5 lakh
cyber security professionals within five years.
The policy promotes public-private partnership, research and development, infrastructure protection and data security.
NCCC supports
situational awareness and timely information-sharing
in the cyber domain.

secs.t: National policies and plans → year, objectives, nodal agency — Draft National Cyber Security Strategy

x: The National Cyber Security Policy 2013 was released by the Information Technology Ministry, now known as MeitY.
CERT-In
is the nodal agency for cyber incident response and crisis management.
CCMP is MeitY's framework against cyber attacks and cyber terrorism.
Every ministry, department and organisation must designate a
Chief Information Security Officer
, or CISO.

secs.t: Sectoral frameworks and fraud recovery → regulator and year

x: Urban Co-operative Banks are required to have a dedicated cyber team, a board-approved policy, MFA, an incident plan and to report all cyber attacks to RBI.
SEBI’s Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework for regulated entities dates to 2024.
The power sector has CERT-Thermal, CERT-Hydro, CERT-Transmission and CERT-Distribution.
The SOP provides for release of frozen funds within
90 days

secs.t: Capacity-building schemes and campaigns → targets

x: The CCPWC scheme has an outlay of Rs 132.93 crore and provides cyber forensic-cum-training laboratories in 33 States and Union Territories.
ISEA is a capacity-building project of the
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
(MeitY).
Cyber Shakti is a programme for
women government officials
, with 305 participants at the beginner level and 53 at the advanced level.

secs.t: International cooperation and the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index

x: India participates in the Quad cyber mechanisms, is a member of the US-led Counter Ransomware Initiative and has been urged to conclude faster CERT-In agreements with foreign counterparts.
India was placed in Tier-1, described as ‘Role Modelling’, and secured a score of 98.49 in the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index 2024.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Supreme Court order concerned standard operating procedures for digital arrests and restoration of victims' losses.
The 2013 policy was criticised for never having been updated, and coordination among CERT-In, the MHA portal and State police was described as weak.
It has four verticals.

rows.title: Data protection and privacy - Puttaswamy judgment, Digital Personal Data Protection Act, data localisation
sub: Group-II M2-B-23: Data protection and privacy - the DPDP Act and related concerns

secs.t: Right to privacy — Puttaswamy and earlier cases

x: In
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
, decided in 2017, the Supreme Court held that privacy is intrinsic to life and personal liberty under Article 21 and protected under Part III.

Kharak Singh is associated with early privacy concerns under Article 21; Gobind recognised privacy as part of personal liberty; Puttaswamy affirmed privacy as a Fundamental Right and informational privacy.

secs.t: Aadhaar judgment and surveillance cases → ruling

x: The Aadhaar judgment was delivered by a five-judge Bench on 26 September 2018 by 4:1, with Justice D.Y. Chandrachud dissenting.
The Court upheld mandatory Aadhaar for welfare benefits (Sec. 7) and PAN/ITR linking (s.139AA).
The challenge concerned Delhi Police use during NEET-UG protests, NAFRS operates without a statute, and surveillance must meet the Puttaswamy tests.

secs.t: Committees and data-protection law history → year

x: The Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee was associated with the
Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
and drafted the Personal Data Protection Bill, 2018.

The A.P. Shah Group dealt with privacy, the Srikrishna Committee with the Personal Data Protection Bill, the Kris Gopalakrishnan Committee with non-personal data and the A.K. Bhargava Committee with net neutrality.

secs.t: DPDP Act, 2023 — scope, terms → meaning, exemptions

x: The Act covers personal data collected in digital form, or collected in non-digital form and digitised subsequently, and certain entities outside India offering goods or services in India.
Notification as a Significant Data Fiduciary is based on factors such as the
volume and sensitivity of data
, along with associated risks.

secs.t: DPDP — rights, duties, Board and penalties

x: The Board is headquartered in New Delhi, its members are appointed by the Central Government, and appeals lie to TDSAT.
Failure of reasonable security safeguards may attract a maximum penalty of
₹250 crore
Children’s data obligations carry ₹200 crore, additional SDF duties ₹150 crore, residual breaches ₹50 crore and false information by Data Principals ₹10,000.

secs.t: DPDP Rules 2025 and the RTI amendment → dates and provisions

x: The final DPDP Rules were notified on
14 November 2025
; 3 January 2025 was the date of release of the draft Rules.
The Rules require clear, specific and informed consent, plain-language notices, purpose limitation, data minimisation and retention controls.
Section 44(3)
of the DPDP Act amended Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act.

secs.t: Data localisation and cross-border transfers

x: The RBI’s April 2018 mandate required all payment-system data to be stored only in India.
The DPDP Act uses a blacklist or negative-list approach, under which transfers are allowed unless the Central Government restricts particular countries.
The standards focus on bias, data sovereignty and privacy and are linked to the DPDP Act.

secs.t: Global frameworks — GDPR, Right to be Forgotten, DPDP vs GDPR

x: The Indian understanding of RTBF does not erase judicial records; it can limit name-based searches in appropriate circumstances.
The GDPR uses ‘Data Controller’, whereas ‘Data Fiduciary’ is the DPDP Act terminology.
The DPDP Act is described as following a blacklist approach, allowing transfers unless restricted.
The DPDP Act provides for the Data Protection Board of India, whereas the GDPR framework has a Data Protection Authority in each member state.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Delhi High Court laid down a framework for de-indexing name-based results concerning persons who had been acquitted.
The AI4AP pilot is associated with
Chittoor, Guntur and Annamayya
, and raises DPDP compliance issues.
The DPDP framework is described as narrower and lighter than the GDPR, with a financial-penalty-based enforcement approach.
The debates include the treatment of journalists as ‘Data Fiduciaries’; journalism does not receive a general exemption.

units.title: Technology in Space and Defence - Indian Space Programme, ISRO, Satellite Programmes, IRNSS, IRS, Defence and Academic Satellites, DRDO

rows.title: Evolution of the Indian space programme - INCOSPAR, Vikram Sarabhai, key milestones

secs.t: Early satellites and experiments → FIRSTs, vehicle and site

x: Exam angle: "Which cosmodrome launched Aryabhata?" -
Soviet
; chronological ordering of Aryabhata-Bhaskara-Rohini-APPLE.
Bhaskara I and II were experimental earth-observation satellites launched during 1979–81 by a Soviet Intercosmos rocket from Baikonur.
SITE was conducted with NASA using ATS-6 and provided educational television to about 2,400 villages, reaching nearly 5 million people.
The American-built
Nike-Apache
, launched from TERLS, Thumba in 1963, was the first sounding rocket of the Indian programme.

secs.t: Key milestones → year (PSLV 1994 to Vikram-1 2026)

x: In 2023, Chandrayaan-3 achieved the first landing near the lunar south pole, while Aditya-L1 was sent to the L1 point.
The correct sequence is Chandrayaan-1 (2008), Mangalyaan (2014), Mission Shakti (2019), and Chandrayaan-3 (2023).
SpaDeX made India the fourth docking nation; LVM3-M6 carried the 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2 on 24 December 2025; and Skyroot's Vikram-1 reached orbit on 18 July 2026.

secs.t: Persons → contributions (Sarabhai and ISRO chairmen)

x: Dr
Vikram Sarabhai
(1919-71) is called the Father of the Indian Space Programme and was the first ISRO Chairman till his death in 1971.
Vikram Sarabhai served from 1969–71, Satish Dhawan from 1972–84, U.R. Rao from 1984–94, and K. Kasturirangan from 1994–2003.
A.S. Kiran Kumar
(2015-18) was ISRO Chairman when a PSLV carried 104 satellites in 2017.

secs.t: International partners → missions

x: Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the International Space Station on Axiom-4 during June-July 2025.
The ISRO-ESA Technical Implementing Plan concerns
ground-tracking support for Gaganyaan
All four pairs are correctly matched.

secs.t: Indian Space Vision 2047 — targets and next missions

x: Gaganyaan plans a 3-member crew to 400 km for 3 days, ending in splashdown in Indian waters.
Chandrayaan-4, Chandrayaan-5 and the Venus Orbiter Mission are identified as next missions in the roadmap.
The stated targets are 50 launches annually, a 44-billion-dollar space economy and more than 440 space start-ups.
A new launch pad is planned at
Kulasekarapattinam

secs.t: Universal angles

x: IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Kumar Goenka stated that ISRO’s role is “by no means diminishing” after privatisation.
India has 56 active space assets, permits up to 100% FDI in non-sensitive segments, and has launched more than 400 foreign satellites on Indian rockets.
SpaDeX is associated with India’s first docking achievement, not the first Indian satellite.

rows.title: ISRO - organisational structure, major centres and their functions
sub: Group-II M2-B-4: Evolution of the Indian space programme and the organisation of ISRO

secs.t: ISRO evolution and governance → year

x: Space research was placed under the Department of Atomic Energy in 1961, INCOSPAR was established in 1962, ISRO was formed in 1969, and the Space Commission and Department of Space were established in 1972.
NSIL was established in 2019 as a CPSE and commercial arm, space-sector reforms including IN-SPACe followed in 2020, and the Indian Space Policy was issued in 2023.

secs.t: Persons → contributions (ISRO chairmen and personalities)

x: Sarabhai chaired INCOSPAR, Kalam directed the SLV-3 project, SHAR honours Satish Dhawan and URSC honours U.R. Rao.
D is the mismatch: Sarabhai was the first ISRO Chairman until his death in 1971, founded PRL and is called the Father of the Indian space programme.
M.G.K. Menon preceded Satish Dhawan, Satish Dhawan preceded U.R. Rao, and K. Kasturirangan preceded G. Madhavan Nair.
U.R. Rao was Chairman 1984-94.

secs.t: ISRO centres and ground network → full form, location, function

x: The Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (
LPSC
), with units at Valiamala and Bengaluru, develops liquid and cryogenic stages.
IPRC at Mahendragiri is responsible for
assembly and testing of liquid and cryogenic engines and stages
MCF operates from Hassan and Bhopal for geostationary-satellite control, while ISTRAC at Bengaluru performs tracking, telemetry and command functions.
VSSC handles launch-vehicle design and development; URSC handles satellite design and building; NRSC handles satellite data; ISTRAC tracks launch vehicles and satellites.

secs.t: Spaceports → location, history and features (Sriharikota, Kulasekarapattinam) — Sriharikota — location and history

x: Exam angle: "Sriharikota is in which district?" - answer by the date of the paper (Nellore earlier, Tirupati now).
Sriharikota lies between Pulicat Lake to the west and the Bay of Bengal to the east.
Sriharikota was selected because of its east-coast location, proximity to the equator, sea corridor for spent stages and relatively thin population.

secs.t: Spaceports → location, history and features (Sriharikota, Kulasekarapattinam) — Sriharikota — facilities and launches

x: The 100th launch from Sriharikota occurred on 29 January 2025 and was the
17th GSLV flight
Kulasekarapattinam allows a direct southward trajectory into polar and sun-synchronous orbits, avoiding the fuel-costly manoeuvre around Sri Lanka required from Sriharikota.
The Kulasekarapattinam complex is mainly for SSLV launches as private players enter the sector, and it is in Thoothukudi (Tuticorin) district of Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: DoS autonomous bodies and training institutes → location, function

x: NARL is located at Gadanki in Tirupati and conducts research on atmospheric radar, lidar and monsoon dynamics.
CSSTEAP is affiliated to the United Nations, was established in 1995 and is hosted at IIRS, Dehradun.
IIRS began in 1966 as the
Indian Photo-interpretation Institute
(IPI) and is located at Dehradun under ISRO/DoS.
IIRS trains in remote sensing, photogrammetry, cartography and geo-informatics/GIS.

secs.t: Outreach programmes and academic network → launch year and number

x: YUVIKA means Yuva Vigyani Karyakram, is a school-student programme launched in 2019, and its second batch was held in 2022.
The six STICs promote space-technology activities in universities, particularly those in tier-2 and tier-3 cities.
The Satish Dhawan Centre for Space Sciences is located at the
Central University of Jammu

secs.t: Universal angles

x: ISRO stated that it would not be privatised, while India is encouraging private participation through space-sector reforms and a growing start-up ecosystem.
The stated plan is to expand the space economy from about $8.4 billion to approximately
$44 billion
by 2033, alongside the growth of more than 450 space start-ups.

rows.title: Launch vehicles - SLV-3, ASLV, PSLV variants, GSLV Mk-II, LVM3/GSLV Mk-III, SSLV
sub: Group-II M2-B-5: Launch vehicles of India - PSLV, GSLV Mk-II, LVM3, SSLV and future vehicles

secs.t: Sounding rockets — TERLS Thumba and Rohini series (FIRSTs)

x: Thumba was selected because the geomagnetic equator passes through the location, making it suitable for sounding-rocket experiments.
M-100 was associated with Russia, Centaure with France, indigenous sounding rockets began in 1965, and the Rohini Sounding Rocket Programme began in 1975.
Rohini sounding rockets carry payloads for atmospheric research and are also used to test and qualify systems intended for larger launch vehicles.

secs.t: Launch vehicles → first flight and first success

x: SLV-3’s successful payload was Rohini RS-1, PSLV’s first successful payload was IRS-P2, and GSLV’s first payload was GSAT-1.
The first flights occurred in the order SLV-3 (1979), ASLV (1987), PSLV (1994) and GSLV (2001).
The ASLV achieved its first success in 1992 with a SROSS-series satellite; its 1987 and 1988 attempts had failed.
CARE was a
suborbital experimental payload
launched by LVM3 on 18 December 2014.

secs.t: Launch vehicles → full form, stages, propellants and payload — Full forms and stages

x: All four statements correctly describe GSLV Mk II: its HTPB solid first stage, Vikas-powered liquid second stage, LH2-LOX cryogenic third stage and four liquid strap-ons.
LVM3 uses two S200 solid strap-ons, an L110 liquid core and a C25 cryogenic stage.
SSLV consists of three solid stages and a liquid Velocity Trimming Module, which provides precise orbit insertion.

secs.t: Launch vehicles → full form, stages, propellants and payload — Payload capacity and orbits served

x: PSLV serves SSO, LEO and GTO missions, including Chandrayaan-1 and the Mars Orbiter Mission.
GSLV Mk II
is designed to place 2–2.5 tonne communication and navigation satellites into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit.
The stated LVM3 capacity is about
4 tonnes to GTO and 8 tonnes to LEO
, although some descriptions cite approximately 10 tonnes to LEO.

secs.t: Orbits and launch physics — terms → meaning

x: Sriharikota’s east-coast position allows launch trajectories to pass over the sea, reducing risk to populated areas.
Polar and Sun-synchronous launches generally follow a
southward
trajectory from Sriharikota; a dog-leg is used to avoid Sri Lanka.
A sun-synchronous orbit is generally near-polar and passes over a given location at approximately the same local solar time, which is useful for consistent imaging conditions.

secs.t: SSLV and cryogenic engines → features

x: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited
(HAL) won the ₹511 crore SSLV Transfer of Technology agreement.
Russia supplied cryogenic engines for early GSLVs; following technology-transfer denial in the 1990s, India developed its own engine, whose first success was GSLV-D5 in 2014.
A semi-cryogenic engine burns refined kerosene with liquid oxygen; SCE-200 is meant for the LVM3 upgrade and NGLV.

secs.t: Satellite → launch vehicle, and record launches

x: EOS-N1 or Anvesha was a DRDO hyperspectral satellite launched with 15 co-passengers by PSLV-C62 on 12 January 2026; the mission failed because of a third-stage anomaly.
PSLV-C61/EOS-09 on 18 May 2025 and PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 on 12 January 2026 both failed in the third stage; ISRO described them as “marginally missed”.

Cartosat-3 (with 13 US nanosatellites) flew on PSLV-C47 in Nov 2019; NVS-01 on GSLV-F12 in May 2023; GISAT-1 on GSLV-F10 (flown Aug 2021, lost after a cryogenic-stage anomaly); NISAR on GSLV-F16 on 30 Jul 2025, the first GSLV launch to a sun-synchronous polar orbit.

secs.t: Reusable and future vehicles — RLV, NGLV, human-rated LVM3

x: RLV-LEX (2 Apr 2023) were autonomous landing tests of RLV-TD, followed by the 'Pushpak' landings in 2024.
NGLV is described as about 90 m tall, with an approximately 1,000-tonne lift-off mass, and is linked to the 2035 space-station and 2040 crewed lunar-landing goals.
The human-rated LVM3, designated
HLVM3
, is intended for the Gaganyaan crew mission to a 400 km LEO orbit for three days.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: GSLV-F17 successfully placed EOS-05, India's first imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit, into a sub-GTO on 4 September 2026.
Rohini RS-1 was launched in 1980, GSLV-D5 succeeded in 2014, PSLV-C61 failed in May 2025, and PSLV-C62 failed in January 2026.
The revised rules allow
automatic FDI in launch vehicles and spaceports.

rows.title: Propulsion and future vehicles - cryogenic engine, semi-cryogenic, reusable launch vehicle, scramjet

secs.t: Rocket propellants — types → example and feature

x: Solid propellants provide high initial thrust but generally cannot be throttled or stopped.
Refined kerosene and LOX are semi-cryogenic, while LH2 and LOX are cryogenic.
Hypergolic propellants
ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring
, although they are highly toxic.
All four pairings are correct examples of the respective propellant categories.

secs.t: Cryogenic technology — propellants, Indian programme, Russian deal

x: Glavkosmos agreed to sell engines and technology in 1991, but US MTCR-based sanctions in 1992 stopped technology transfer; Russia supplied seven engines only.
The sequence is 1991 agreement, 1992 sanctions, 2006 full-stage test and 2014 GSLV Mk II flight with the indigenous stage.
Cryogenic propulsion is used in
rocket upper stages
(and was used on the space shuttle) because of its very high specific impulse (~450 s).

secs.t: Engines → propellants and use (ISRO and private) — ISRO engines

x: CE-7.5 is a 75 kN staged-combustion LOX–LH2 engine used in the GSLV Mk II cryogenic upper stage.
CE-20 is a 200 kN-class gas-generator LOX–LH2 engine for the LVM3 C25 upper stage.
Bootstrap mode starts the engine using its own propellant flow without external gas and is important for in-space restart capability.

secs.t: Engines → propellants and use (ISRO and private) — Private engines → developer

x: Agnilet was flown in 2024 from Dhanush at Sriharikota, described as India’s first private launch pad.
Agnite is described as a single-piece 3D-printed engine made of Inconel for the Agnibaan booster stage.
Astrobase’s EVEREST is described as India’s first private
800 kN full-flow staged combustion LOX-methane engine
Skyroot
’s KALAM 1200 solid motor was static-tested at SDSC-SHAR.

secs.t: Green and electric propulsion — Hall thrusters, LOX-methane, POEM

x: It is a Hall-type xenon thruster with ~6x the specific impulse of chemical systems.
LOX-methane is considered cleaner and cheaper, and methane can be produced from Martian resources.
POEM stands for
PSLV Orbital Experimental Module
POEM reuses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.

secs.t: Scramjet and air-breathing propulsion — ramjet vs scramjet, ATV, HSTDV

x: A ramjet uses forward speed for compression, has subsonic combustion and operates above Mach 2.
A scramjet uses oxygen from the atmosphere, so it need not carry the entire oxidiser required by a rocket.
Maintaining stable combustion in the extremely fast supersonic airflow of a scramjet is likened to trying to keep a candle alight in a hurricane.
ATV flight-tested scramjet engines from Sriharikota in Aug 2016.

secs.t: Reusable launch systems and NGLV "Soorya"

x: Pushpak is ISRO’s reusable winged vehicle and is intended to contribute to a Two-Stage-To-Orbit system.
Soorya is planned as a reusable heavy-lift NGLV using semi-cryogenic propulsion, with a payload of about 20,000 kg to LEO—approximately 2.5 times the LVM3 capacity.
Soorya is intended to support the Bharatiya Antariksh Station planned for 2035 and a crewed lunar landing planned for 2040.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Skyroot's Vikram-1 has three solid stages and one liquid stage and is designed for a 290 kg payload to a 500 km sun-synchronous orbit.
Reusability and advanced propulsion can reduce launch costs, improve commercial competitiveness and support cost-effective human spaceflight.
Cryogenic propellant transfer in orbit
has been identified as a top risk to Starship's Moon-landing plan.

rows.title: Communication satellites - INSAT and GSAT series, applications, transponder capacity

secs.t: Geostationary orbit — terms and features

x: The geostationary orbital height is fixed and does not depend on the satellite’s mass.
A geostationary satellite moves west to east in the equatorial plane and has a 24-hour period, matching Earth’s rotation.
Launch vehicles generally inject satellites into an elliptical geostationary transfer orbit (GTO); the satellite’s own motor raises it to geostationary orbit (GEO).

secs.t: INSAT system — FIRSTs, design, management and operator

x: APPLE stands for Ariane Passenger PayLoad Experiment and was India’s first experimental communication satellite, launched in 1981.
INSAT is a joint venture of DoS, DoT, IMD, AIR and Doordarshan, coordinated by the ICC.
INSAT serves both communication and meteorology from geostationary orbit (JPSC 2021 keyed it as a 'meteorological satellite'), and also carries broadcasting, disaster warning and search-and-rescue.

secs.t: INSAT/GSAT satellites → launch and purpose

x: CMS-03, also designated GSAT-7R, weighed 4,410 kg and was described as the heaviest communication satellite launched from Indian soil for the Navy.
GSAT-30 is a
telecommunication satellite
launched by Ariane from Kourou on 17 Jan 2020 (APPSC 2018 PYQ theme).
INSAT-3A, INSAT-4A, INSAT-4B and GSAT-8
are among the Indian communication satellites launched from Kourou by Ariane.

secs.t: Strategic and regional GSATs → user

x: GSAT-6, launched in 2015, has a large deployable antenna and supports mobile and strategic communication.
GSAT-7 'Rukmini' (2013) is the Navy satellite (later replaced by CMS-03), GSAT-7A 'Angry Bird' (2018) is the dedicated Air Force satellite, and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army.
Pakistan
opted out of the South Asia Satellite (GSAT-9, GSLV-F09, May 2017).

secs.t: Transponder bands → use

x: C/extended C is used for telecom and TV distribution (iii), Ku for DTH and VSAT (ii), Ka for high-throughput broadband such as GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2 (i), and S for mobile satellite services and the DWS downlink (iv).
GSAT-19, GSAT-29, GSAT-11 and GSAT-N2
are identified with high-throughput broadband services for underserved areas, in-flight links and defence, complementing BharatNet.

secs.t: Communication applications → services

x: Starlink’s India launch was imminent in 2025 and its stated advantage was broadband access for remote, disaster-hit and mobile areas.
INSAT/GSAT applications include DSNG, mobile satellite services and satellite-aided search and rescue, but satellites do not directly extract petroleum from underground reservoirs.
DTH means Direct-to-Home broadcasting, VSAT supports business networks, DSNG means satellite news gathering, and MSS means mobile satellite services.

secs.t: Disaster management applications — DWS, search and rescue, APSDMA

x: The warning signal goes up on C-band and comes down on S-band to selectively addressable DWS receivers along the coast.
SDSC-SHAR supplies Bay of Bengal cyclone-track data to the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (
APSDMA
INSAT carries search-and-rescue transponders under the international
COSPAS-SARSAT
programme.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: CMS-03/GSAT-7R is associated with encrypted, anti-jam naval links extending up to 2,000 km from the coast and was launched using LVM3-M5.
INSAT-3D and INSAT-3DR early warnings sharply reduced cyclone deaths along the east coast, including Andhra Pradesh.
KALPANA-1 was India's
first exclusive weather satellite

rows.title: Navigation satellites - IRNSS/NavIC constellation and GAGAN; applications and limitations

secs.t: Satellite navigation — GPS basics, NavIC full form, constellation and services

x: A one-microsecond clock error can produce an approximate position error of
300 metres
, illustrating the importance of atomic clocks in navigation.
NavIC’s planned constellation has seven satellites: three in geostationary orbit and four in inclined geosynchronous orbit at about 29° to the equator.
The NVS series adds
a civilian L1 signal
compatible with other GNSS systems, helping mobile-phone adoption.

secs.t: IRNSS and NVS satellites → launch and clock failures

x: The IRNSS satellites were launched from Sriharikota, and the IRNSS-1 series was launched using PSLV vehicles.
First-generation IRNSS satellites used rubidium clocks supplied by Swiss firm SpectraTime, which repeatedly failed; ISRO switched to indigenous clocks in 2018.
After the last clock on IRNSS-1F failed, only IRNSS-1B, IRNSS-1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable—three satellites, below the four needed.

secs.t: NavIC applications and adoption — devices, chipsets, timing

x: Elena Geo Systems
developed India’s first NavIC-based device for precise directions on infrastructure projects.
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways’ AIS-140 rule made NavIC-enabled location trackers compulsory in public transport vehicles.
The Government urged electronics makers to use NavIC for Indian Standard Time (Mar 2026), reflecting NavIC's precise-timing capability.

secs.t: GAGAN and other SBAS → developer and region

x: An SBAS broadcasts real-time corrections for orbit, clock and ionospheric delay, improving accuracy, integrity and availability.
The GAGAN ground segment includes Indian Reference Stations (INRES), the Indian Master Control Centre (INMCC) and uplink stations (INLUS).
GAGAN supports
precision approach and landing for civil aviation
by providing augmented navigation information over the Indian Flight Information Region.

secs.t: Limitations of NavIC — issues

x: NavIC is a regional system, while GPS is global.
Receiver adoption was constrained because L5 and S bands were not commonly supported in phone chipsets; the newer civilian L1 signal helps address this limitation.
Repeated atomic-clock failures and the NVS-02 launch failure
reduced the effective constellation, preventing NavIC from fully replacing GPS over India.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Reduced dependence on foreign navigation systems during conflict directly explains NavIC’s importance for strategic autonomy.
GPS jamming near the Strait of Hormuz illustrates the operational risk of relying on foreign navigation systems in a conflict situation.
NavIC-based fishermen alerts can support the large fishing community along Andhra Pradesh’s long coastline during cyclones.

rows.title: Earth observation - IRS series, Cartosat, Resourcesat, Oceansat, RISAT, EOS series and applications
sub: Group-II M2-B-7: Communication, navigation and earth observation satellites - INSAT/GSAT, NavIC, IRS/Cartosat

secs.t: Remote sensing — definition, components, sensor types

x: Remote sensing obtains information about the Earth without physical contact by detecting reflected or emitted electromagnetic radiation.
Passive sensors detect natural sunlight or emitted heat; active sensors transmit their own signal.
Hyperspectral sensing uses hundreds of narrow spectral bands, enabling identification of materials and their chemical characteristics.
LiDAR sends its own laser pulse and reads the echo, so it is active (APPSC 2023: laser is active).

secs.t: Resolution types and remote-sensing techniques → what they map

x: InSAR
maps ground deformation, including subsidence, earthquake-related movement and volcanic uplift.
LiDAR uses laser ranging to derive elevation, three-dimensional terrain and forest canopy height.
Thermal infrared sensing
records emitted heat and is therefore useful for volcanic eruptions, forest fires and urban heat mapping.
The four resolution types are spatial, spectral, temporal and radiometric. '
Chemical resolution
' does not exist (APPSC 2025 trap).

secs.t: Orbits for Earth observation → altitude and use

x: A satellite appears permanently fixed over one equatorial point only in the geostationary special case, not in every geosynchronous orbit.
Sun-synchronous polar imaging orbits generally operate at approximately
EOS-05 images priority targets every five minutes and the whole Indian landmass every
30 minutes
GEO is at 35,786 km over the Equator, and GEO and GSO share a period of one sidereal day (~23 h 56 min).

secs.t: IRS programme — origins and FIRSTs

x: Bhaskara I, launched in 1979, was the first experimental Earth-observation satellite.
IRS-1A was launched on 17 March 1988 using a
Soviet Vostok launcher
and was India's first operational IRS satellite.
India's IRS programme began with IRS-1A in 1988 and is regarded as the largest civilian remote-sensing constellation in the world.

secs.t: Satellite series → type and application

x: Exam angle: "match series with function" and "which satellite uses SAR / serves fishermen".
Oceansat observations support PFZ advisories, which help fishermen identify areas likely to have higher fish availability.
RISAT-1, RISAT-2 and RISAT-2B use
Synthetic Aperture Radar
(SAR), enabling all-weather, day-and-night imaging through clouds.
SCATSAT-1 uses a scatterometer to measure
ocean-surface wind vectors
, supporting cyclone forecasting.
SARAL is an ISRO-CNES altimetry mission using the AltiKa Ka-band altimeter to measure sea-surface height; hyperspectral agricultural imaging is associated with HySIS.

secs.t: Cartosat series → year, resolution and uses

x: Cartosat-1, launched in 2005, was intended for topographic mapping and supplied stereo images for 3D maps and elevation models.
The Cartosat-2 series, operational from 2007 onward, provides sub-metre resolution imagery for Smart Cities, transport, border management and infrastructure corridors.
Cartosat-3 imagery supports Smart Cities, PM Gati Shakti, border surveillance and heritage applications including KASTURI and Bharat Darshan.

secs.t: Geo-imaging and recent EO missions — EOS-03, EOS-05, NISAR, losses

x: EOS-05 sensors span visible, near-infrared, short-wave infrared and long-wave infrared portions of the electromagnetic spectrum.
NISAR was launched on GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025 and carries NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band radars, making it the first dual-frequency radar satellite of its kind.
NISAR scans nearly the whole Earth every 12 days and carries a 12-metre antenna reflector deployed in orbit.

secs.t: INSAT system — services, bands, FIRSTs

x: INSAT-3DS
is a weather satellite fully funded by the Ministry of Earth Sciences and was launched by GSLV-F14 on 17 February 2024.
INSAT supports telecommunication, television, meteorology, telemedicine and tele-education.
The INSAT system carries
C, extended-C, Ku, Ka and S bands
EDUSAT (2004) delivered the INSAT system's tele-education service, giving schools and colleges two-way satellite links to virtual classrooms.

secs.t: Navigation systems → owner and scope (NavIC status)

x: NavIC is the operational Indian regional navigation system, with a seven-satellite constellation of three GEO and four GSO satellites and coverage extending up to 1,500 km beyond India.

After IRNSS-1F's last clock stopped (3 days after its 10-year design life), only IRNSS-1B, 1I and NVS-01 remained PNT-capable: three, below the minimum four needed. 'Five' and 'all seven lost' are wrong counts, and NVS-02 never reached its circular orbit (Jan 2025).

secs.t: NRSC data platforms, national uses and EO in news (incl. AP)

x: Bhuvan
is the ISRO geoportal through which Earth-observation data are made openly accessible along with NRSC data services.
Bhoonidhi, VEDAS and MOSDAC are hosted by ISRO as data platforms, while Yuktdhara supports gram panchayats in planning MGNREGA assets.
CROP stands for Comprehensive Remote Sensing Observation on Crop Progress and uses EOS-04 SAR to track sowing, growth and harvest near real time.
Bhuvan uses
RISAT and INSAT-3DS
data to provide flood-inundation maps and cyclone tracks.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: EOS-05 is intended for applications such as floods, cyclones, forest fires, crops and security.
The INSAT-3D series represented India's earlier geostationary weather satellites, while EOS-05 is India's first geosynchronous land-imaging satellite.
IIRS and CSSTEAP are both in Dehradun.
SDSC-SHAR is located at Sriharikota in
Tirupati district
, Andhra Pradesh.

rows.title: Recent Indian satellite launches and their applications
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-36

secs.t: Recent launches → vehicle, date, purpose

x: EOS-07 was an Earth-observation and technology-demonstration mission launched by SSLV-D2.
NVS-02
, launched by GSLV-F15 in January 2025, was intended for NavIC navigation but missed its intended orbit.
NISAR is an Earth-observation mission with NASA and was placed in a sun-synchronous polar orbit.
EOS-05 is a geo-platform imaging satellite intended for agriculture, environmental monitoring and disaster applications.

secs.t: Mission FIRSTs and records — SpaDeX, most satellites, heaviest payload

x: The
United States, Russia and China
had achieved space docking before India, making India the fourth country through SpaDeX.
Space docking capability demonstrated by SpaDeX is needed for the
Bharatiya Antariksh Station
LVM3-M6
launched the 6,100 kg BlueBird Block-2 (223 sq m phased array, direct-to-smartphone broadband) on 24 Dec 2025.

secs.t: Foreign customer satellites → country and vehicle

x: Duchifat-3 was an
Israel
i satellite launched by PSLV-C48.
Proba-3 was an
ESA
satellite mission launched by PSLV-C59 in December 2024.
ISRO had launched 433 foreign satellites from more than 34 countries; more than half were from the United States.

secs.t: Launch failures, re-entry experiments and POEM platforms

x: On 12 January 2026, PSLV-C62 failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of its third stage and lost EOS-N1 ‘Anvesha’ along with 15 co-passengers.
AayulSAT was identified as the first on-orbit refuelling demonstrator and MOI-1 as an AI image laboratory among the PSLV-C62 co-passengers.
POEM platforms use the spent PS4 stage as an orbital laboratory.

secs.t: Satellites by application domain

x: GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7A, known as the ‘Angry Bird’, serves the IAF, and GSAT-7B has been proposed for the Army.
Kalpana-1 was India’s first exclusive meteorological satellite and was launched by PSLV in 2002.
NVS/NavIC are navigation systems, while XPoSat and Aditya-L1 are science missions.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The GSLV-F17/EOS-05 mission ended an eight-month launch pause that followed two PSLV failures.
Starlink obtained a GMPCS licence from the Department of Telecommunications in 2025.
India had
86 satellites in orbit, of which 27 were operational

rows.title: Space science missions - Chandrayaan-1, 2 and 3; Mangalyaan; AstroSat; Aditya-L1; XPoSat
sub: Group-II M2-B-8: Indian space science missions - Chandrayaan series, Mangalyaan, AstroSat, Aditya-L1, XPoSat

secs.t: Space history — early milestones and Space Shuttle FIRSTs

x: The sequence is Columbia’s first flight in 1981, Solar Maximum Mission repair in 1984, Challenger’s loss in 1986, and Columbia’s loss during re-entry in 2003.
NASA’s
Solar Maximum Mission
satellite was repaired by the crew of Space Shuttle Challenger in April 1984 during mission STS-41C.
SLV-3 launched Rohini
, making India the 6th nation with indigenous satellite launch capability.

secs.t: Space science terms → meaning

x: Lagrange points
are five points, L1 to L5, in a two-body system where a small object can remain in balance.
Earth’s escape velocity is approximately
A Hohmann transfer uses an elliptical transfer orbit and two engine burns to move between two orbits efficiently.

secs.t: Indian science missions → launch date and vehicle

x: Exam angle: match mission-month-year (Ch-2 July 2019, Ch-3 July 2023, Aditya-L1 Sept 2023, SpaDeX Dec 2024).
Chandrayaan-1 used PSLV-C11, Mangalyaan PSLV-C25, AstroSat PSLV-C30 and Chandrayaan-2 GSLV Mk III-M1.
The correct order is Chandrayaan-3 (14 July 2023), Aditya-L1 (2 September 2023), XPoSat (1 January 2024) and SpaDeX (30 December 2024).
LVM3 flew two OneWeb missions carrying 72 satellites in total.

secs.t: Chandrayaan-1 and Chandrayaan-2 — payloads, findings, outcome

x: Chandrayaan-1 comprised an orbiter and MIP, carried 11 instruments including M3, and confirmed water molecules on the lunar surface.
India was the fourth nation to place its flag on the Moon through an impact probe, after the USSR, the USA and Japan.
Vikram's soft landing failed in September 2019, although the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter continued operating with its payloads active.
The Chandrayaan-2 crash spot was named
Tiranga Point
, whereas Chandrayaan-3's landing site was named Shiv Shakti Point.

secs.t: Chandrayaan-3 — modules, launch, specs and payloads

x: ChaSTE, ILSA and the Langmuir Probe perform the functions stated.
The
Propulsion Module
carried the SHAPE payload, which studies Earth from lunar orbit.
Chandrayaan-3 had a Propulsion Module plus lander Vikram and rover Pragyan (names kept from Chandrayaan-2, APPSC 2022), and it soft-landed on 23 Aug 2023.

secs.t: Chandrayaan-3 — landing site, India's rank and findings

x: Exam angle: "Vikram = lander, Pragyan = rover"; element confirmed (sulphur); landing point names; India's rank (4th).
India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon, after the
United States, Russia and China
Pragyan confirmed
sulphur
near the south pole; its LIBS also detected Al, Ca, Fe, Cr, Ti, Mn, Si and O. Helium-3, uranium and nitrogen are not among the elements Pragyan confirmed.

secs.t: Mangalyaan (2013) — FIRST-attempt record, rank, orbit, payloads

x: Mangalyaan was India’s first interplanetary mission and was also known as the
Mars Orbiter Mission
India reached Mars orbit on its maiden attempt through Mangalyaan.
ISRO was the fourth space agency to orbit Mars, after
NASA, Roscosmos and ESA
Mangalyaan carried the Methane Sensor for Mars, Mars Colour Camera, MENCA, Lyman Alpha Photometer and Thermal Infrared Imaging Spectrometer.

secs.t: Aditya-L1 (2023) — L1 point, payloads, results

x: SUIT performs near-ultraviolet imaging, SoLEXS performs soft X-ray spectroscopy, HEL1OS performs hard X-ray spectroscopy, and the Magnetometer measures the magnetic field.
The Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (
VELC
) was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.
VELC recorded the first-ever spectroscopic observations of coronal mass ejections in
visible wavelengths
during the 2025 solar maximum.
Aditya-L1
(PSLV-C57, 2 Sep 2023), stationed in a halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1, is India's first space-based solar observatory.

secs.t: AstroSat (2015) and XPoSat (2024) — bands, partner, payloads, FIRST

x: Exam angle: "India's first polarimetry mission with RRI" = XPoSat (a PYQ wrongly dated it May 2023; it flew on 1 Jan 2024).
AstroSat observes in the
visible, ultraviolet and X-ray bands
XPoSat is India's first and the world's second X-ray polarimetry mission, after NASA's IXPE, and studies black holes and neutron stars.

secs.t: Upcoming Indian missions → target and partner

x: Shukrayaan, or the
Venus
Orbiter Mission, targets Venus.
Chandrayaan-4 is a sample-return mission (regolith and ice) with a site near Mons Mouton.
NISAR is a NASA–ISRO Earth-observation mission using L- and S-band synthetic aperture radar to study climate and hazards.
The vision envisages the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035 and placing an Indian on the Moon by 2040.

secs.t: Foreign missions and vehicles → agency and target

x: Exo
Mars
is an ESA mission undertaken with Roscosmos involvement to search for signs of life on Mars.
Chang'e-6 was a far-side sample-return mission.
Artemis I was an uncrewed SLS-Orion test conducted in 2022.
Europa Clipper targets Europa, Psyche targets asteroid 16 Psyche, SuperView provides commercial high-resolution Earth observation, and Nuri is South Korea’s indigenous launch vehicle.
SLIM (2024) made Japan the 5th country to soft-land on the Moon with its 'Moon sniper' precision landing.
India signed the Artemis Accords in 2023.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India is targeting a capacity of
50 launches
a year while focusing on Chandrayaan-4, BAS, and missions to Venus and Mars.
The missions were launched from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre SHAR at Sriharikota, located in Tirupati district of Andhra Pradesh.

Chandrayaan-3 achieved the first near-south-pole landing; Mangalyaan achieved a Mars orbit on India’s maiden attempt; Aditya-L1 is India’s first solar observatory; and XPoSat is India’s first polarimetry mission.

rows.title: Human spaceflight - Gaganyaan programme, Bharatiya Antariksh Station roadmap
sub: Group-II M2-B-9: Human spaceflight - Gaganyaan and the Bharatiya Antariksh Station roadmap

secs.t: Gaganyaan — definitions, modules and FIRSTs

x: The Orbital Module consists of the Crew and Service Modules; the Crew Module houses the crew and survives re-entry; the Service Module provides on-orbit support and de-orbits the vehicle; and HLVM3 injects it into orbit.
The Service Module separates from the Orbital Module after the de-orbit operation and burns up; therefore; .
Both Soyuz and Shenzhou use a three-module configuration: orbital, descent and service modules.

secs.t: HLVM3 launch vehicle and Gaganyaan flights → target dates

x: The planned sequence is two or more uncrewed missions, G1 followed by G2 and G3, before the crewed H1 mission.
The current target is H1 during
the first quarter of 2027
, although later assessments have indicated that it could slip beyond 2027.
The 2018 announcement set
December 2021
for the first crewed flight (PYQ 2018); it later slipped to 2023 and now H1 is targeted for Q1 2027.

secs.t: Gaganyaan tests → date → what they proved; Vyommitra

x: TV-D1 demonstrated an in-flight abort of the Crew Escape System at Mach 1.2, followed by crew-module separation and sea recovery.
IADT-01 involved the 4.8-tonne dummy module, IADT-02 the 5.7-tonne module and ten parachutes, CARE tested re-entry, and SOLVE tested the solid motor.
Vyommitra is an AI-enabled, female-form semi-humanoid robot intended to fly on the uncrewed G1 and G2 missions before the crewed flight.

secs.t: Persons → Gaganyatris and Indians in space

x: Exam angle: "which name is NOT a Gaganyatri" (e.g., Pankaj M. Sinha is not).
Kalpana Chawla was the first Indian-born woman in space, died in the 2003 Columbia disaster, and Sunita Williams is an Indian-origin NASA astronaut associated with long ISS stays.
Anil Menon, an Indian-origin NASA astronaut, is associated with
Soyuz MS-29 to the ISS for an eight-month mission
involving Expeditions 74–75.

secs.t: Axiom-4 mission → crew, dates and experiments

x: Axiom-4 was launched on 25 June 2025 aboard a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft carried by a Falcon 9 rocket.
Shubhanshu Shukla spent
18 days
aboard the ISS during the Axiom-4 mission and returned on 15 July 2025.
The experiments included muscle regeneration, crop viability and cognitive performance, among other biological and life-science themes.

secs.t: Institutions → role in crew training and human spaceflight

x: The basic training sequence included the Yuri Gagarin Cosmonaut Training Centre in Russia followed by ISRO's Astronaut Training Facility in Bengaluru.
The IAF Institute of Aerospace Medicine in Bengaluru conducted the selection and aeromedical testing of the astronaut candidates.
The ISRO Human Spaceflight Expo was held at the
Jawaharlal Nehru Planetarium, Bengaluru
, on 22-24 July 2022 (PYQ).

secs.t: Places → launch pads and analogue mission sites — Launch pads

x: The Third Launch Pad costs about ₹4,000 crore and is planned for the NGLV and future human spaceflight; the NGLV is about 90 metres tall and has about 1,000 tonnes of lift-off mass.
The mission simulates life in an interplanetary habitat and generates data for astronaut selection and training, ECLSS design, work-rest schedules and ground-crew protocols.

secs.t: Places → launch pads and analogue mission sites — Related sites and studies

x: HOPE, or Himalayan Outpost for Planetary Exploration, was located in Ladakh because of early-Mars-like conditions such as high UV flux, low air pressure, cold extremes and saline permafrost.
Mission MITRA is a behavioural study at Leh conducted with the IAF’s Institute of Aerospace Medicine, testing crew under hypoxia, cold and isolation.

secs.t: Terms → microgravity effects on the human body

x: Spaceflight osteopenia can cause approximately 1–1.5% loss of bone mass per month without mechanical loading.
Muscle atrophy weakens postural muscles.
Microgravity causes body fluids to shift towards the head, producing a puffy face and comparatively thinner-looking legs.
Space medicine is also studied through ground analogues such as Leh and HOPE.

secs.t: Space stations — ISS, Tiangong and Bharatiya Antariksh Station

x: The ISS is operated by NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
Zarya was the first ISS module, Zvezda is Russian, Destiny is the US module and Kibo is the Japanese module.
SpaDeX, Axiom-4 and Gaganyaan are identified as precursor missions for the BAS roadmap.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: TV-D1, both air-drop tests, all Gaganyaan launches and the Third Launch Pad are associated with Sriharikota.
IADT-01 was conducted at SDSC-SHAR, and IADT-02 was associated with April 2026.
The sequence cited is 2021, followed by 2023 and then 2027, illustrating repeated slippage.

rows.title: Satellites for defence and for academic purposes - GSAT-7 series, EDUSAT, RISAT for surveillance

secs.t: Defence satellites → user and nickname

x: GSAT-7A serves the Indian Air Force and supports network-centric warfare and drone operations.
GSAT-7 serves the Navy, GSAT-7R/CMS-03 is its naval replacement, and GSAT-7B is proposed for the Army.
GSAT-7R, or CMS-03, was launched on
LVM3-M5 on 2 November 2025
as a replacement for GSAT-7 in naval service.
EMISAT is associated with DRDO and performs electronic intelligence (ELINT).

secs.t: RISAT series → band, launcher and key fact

x: Exam angle: launcher-satellite pairs (RISAT-1/PSLV-C19; RISAT-2BR1/PSLV-C48) and the band (C vs X).
RISAT-2 used X-band radar, RISAT-1 used C-band SAR at 5.35 GHz, and RISAT-2B was an X-band surveillance satellite.
RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre against a defunct US satellite using
NETRA
data.
RISAT-1, carrying a C-band (5.35 GHz) SAR, was launched by
PSLV-C19

secs.t: Programmes and organisations → defence space (SBS-3, DSA, DSRO)

x: SBS-3 comprises 52 satellites, including 21 by ISRO and 31 by private industry.
The DSA is a tri-service agency established at Bengaluru in 2019.
DSRO is the R&D arm associated with the Defence Space Agency and develops space-warfare systems and technologies for it.

secs.t: Education and student-built satellites → builder and FIRSTs — EDUSAT (GSAT-3)

x: GSAT-3, popularly known as EDUSAT, was India's first satellite dedicated to education and provided two-way satellite communication to classrooms.
EDUSAT was launched on
20 September 2004 by GSLV-F01
from Sriharikota.

secs.t: Education and student-built satellites → builder and FIRSTs — Student, university and women-built satellites

x: WESAT
, built by the LBS Institute of Technology for Women in Kerala, was the first Indian satellite fully built by women students.
Jugnu was built by IIT Kanpur, SRMSAT by SRM University, SATYABAMASAT by Sathyabama University and Kalamsat-V2 by Space Kidz India.
Kalamsat-V2, built by Space Kidz India and launched on PSLV-C44 in January 2019, was the first to use the PS4 stage as an orbital platform and was the lightest.

secs.t: Programmes → ISRO capacity-building for students

x: UNNATI (UNispace Nanosatellite Assembly and Training by ISRO) trains developing countries in nanosatellites and was launched in 2019 for 50 years of UNISPACE-I. Statement 3 is wrong: the Class 9 summer programme is YUVIKA.
Student CubeSats may fly on PSLV POEM, the PS4 orbital platform, or as rideshare payloads.
The ATL Space Challenge is an initiative involving the
Atal Innovation Mission, ISRO and CBSE
for school students.

secs.t: Launch records → foreign co-passenger and academic satellites on PSLV

x: The foreign nanosatellites on PSLV-C37 came from the United States, Israel, Kazakhstan, the Netherlands, Switzerland and the UAE.
PSLV-C37 launched 104 satellites on 15 February 2017, including Cartosat-2 series, two ISRO nanosatellites and 101 foreign nanosatellites.
PSLV-C62/EOS-N1 failed after a roll-rate disturbance at the end of the third stage.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: EOS-05 is intended for geosynchronous orbit at approximately 36,000 km and supports observation of floods, cyclones, fires and security-related events.
The reported relevance referred to two consecutive PSLV failures: C61 in 2025 and C62 in January 2026, which affected surveillance satellites.
RISAT-1 was the first indigenous radar satellite, EDUSAT the first education satellite, ANUSAT the first university satellite and WESAT the first all-women-student satellite.
