rows.title: Space policy and commercialisation - Indian Space Policy 2023, IN-SPACe, NSIL, private launch sector
sub: Group-II M2-B-10: Space sector reforms - Indian Space Policy 2023, IN-SPACe, NSIL and private participation

secs.t: Space sector reforms 2020 → FDI limits by segment

x: The automatic route permits 74% in satellite manufacturing, operations and data products, 49% in launch vehicles and spaceports, and investment above the applicable limits requires government approval.
FDI up to
is allowed overall in non-sensitive space segments, with segment-wise automatic-route limits of 100%, 74% and 49% and the government route beyond those limits.

secs.t: Indian Space Policy 2023 → roles of ISRO, IN-SPACe, NSIL, DoS and NGEs

x: NSIL commercialises mature ISRO technology; the Department of Space handles policy and cooperation; non-governmental entities undertake end-to-end activities; and ISRO focuses on advanced research and strategic missions.
ISRO is to focus on advanced research, deep space and human spaceflight while gradually moving away from routine operational and commercial production.
Nine ISRO employee associations sought clarity on outsourcing and ISRO’s future role.

secs.t: Organisations → IN-SPACe and NSIL (vs Antrix)

x: IN-SPACe authorised Vikram-S, operates a Seed Fund Scheme, approved the Pixxel-led EOS constellation and enabled SSLV technology transfer to private consortia.

Antrix was set up in September 1992 as a private limited company and became a Miniratna in 2008; its supply-driven model covered marketing ISRO products, transponder leasing, remote-sensing data and consultancy; NSIL follows the demand-driven model of owning satellites against committed demand.

secs.t: NSIL → demand-driven missions, DTH leasing, launches and technology transfer

x: Under the demand-driven model, NSIL builds, owns and operates satellites against assured or committed customer demand, unlike the earlier supply-driven approach.
Ten satellites were transferred in 2022, taking NSIL’s operating fleet to 11 communication satellites, about 300 transponders and more than 150 lease agreements.
GSAT-N2 is also designated GSAT-20, supports Ka-band broadband and in-flight connectivity, and was launched on SpaceX’s Falcon-9 in November 2024.

secs.t: Acts, Bills and conventions → space legislation and gaps

x: India does not yet have a Space Activities Act; the space sector operates through policies and guidelines.
The draft Space Activities Bill first issued in 2017 proposed
licensing of private space activity
The legislative gap concerns liability, dispute resolution, risk-sharing and the absence of sovereign-backed insurance arrangements.
The Liability Convention of 1972 makes the
launching State
liable for damage caused by a space object.

secs.t: Data → space economy size, targets, funds and start-ups

x: The ₹1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund for space start-ups is to be managed through
SIDBI
over a period of five years.
Downstream data services are expected to generate approximately
of future space-sector revenues.
The Minister said India now has more than 440 space start-ups, up from single digits in 2014 (some older sources give 300+).

secs.t: Private launch and propulsion firms → product and FIRSTs

x: Vikram-1, developed by Skyroot, is a four-stage private orbital rocket with a payload capacity of up to 350 kg to LEO.
Vikram-1 carried the
SOLARAS nanosatellite with VIT-AP University's VISWA-M solar-spectrum payload, built with Grahaa Space
All four statements correctly describe Bellatrix Aerospace, its Bengaluru base, green propulsion and electric-thruster work, the POEM-3 demonstration, and Technology Development Fund support.

secs.t: Private satellite firms → company, base and FIRST

x: TSAT-1A was a sub-metre optical surveillance satellite built by Tata Advanced Systems with Satellogic and launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in 2024.
IN-SPACe approved a public-private partnership Earth-observation constellation led by Pixxel, with Dhruva Space, SatSure Analytics India and Piersight Space.

Ananth Technologies is associated with the first private satellite integration facility; Azista with the first commercial small-satellite launch from Indian soil; GalaxEye with Drishti; and Digantara with space surveillance.

secs.t: Places → AP space policy and space cities

x: Andhra Pradesh has announced Space Policy 4.0 and is developing dedicated space cities to promote space manufacturing and related activities.
The Tirupati Space City is planned over approximately
3,000 acres
near Sriharikota.
The proposed investment in the Tirupati Space City is approximately
US$4 billion
The AP Space Tech Summit-2026 was held at Vignan’s University in Vadlamudi, Guntur.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: All three statements describe concerns associated with India's space-sector ecosystem: the absence of a Space Activities Act, dependence on imported space-grade chips exceeding 90%, and the lack of sovereign-backed insurance for long-gestation ventures.
Eighteen collision-avoidance manoeuvres were carried out in low Earth orbit in 2025, reflecting the growing problem of LEO congestion.

rows.title: Applications of space technology - agriculture, disaster management, telemedicine, tele-education, navigation
sub: Group-II M2-B-11: Applications of space technology in agriculture, disaster management, navigation and governance

secs.t: Remote sensing — definitions, types and what it measures

x: Passive remote sensing uses naturally available radiation such as solar radiation, while active systems transmit their own signal.
Microwave/SAR systems can observe through cloud cover and in darkness, making them useful for flood mapping during cloudy conditions.
InSAR can map ground deformation associated with earthquakes, land subsidence, landslides, volcanoes and glacier movement.

secs.t: Terms → meaning: spectral indices and GIS

x: Healthy vegetation reflects strongly in the near-infrared band
, which is why NIR is used in vegetation indices such as NDVI.
GIS data includes spatial data such as vector points, lines and polygons and raster satellite images, along with attribute tables.
Situational awareness uses real-time layers for disaster response, including flood alerts and mineral-vehicle tracking, as well as shoreline mapping.

secs.t: Organisations → remote sensing agencies and role

x: The
National Remote Sensing Centre
(NRSC), Hyderabad, receives, processes and supplies satellite data, runs Bhuvan and supports States in disaster management.
IIRS provides training and education; NESAC serves the North-East; SAC works on sensors and applications; and the five RRSCs undertake regional projects for States.
NESAC is at Umiam (Shillong), Meghalaya.

secs.t: Platforms and apps → developer and use — Bhuvan and geoportals

x: Bhoonidhi provides access to an archive of Indian and foreign Earth-observation data dating from 1988.
Bhuvan Panchayat supports Gram Panchayat planning; Yuktdhara concerns MGNREGA assets; SVAMITVA uses drone mapping and provides property cards; PM Gati Shakti is the National Master Plan GIS platform.
Srishti is used for watershed monitoring under the Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP).

secs.t: Platforms and apps → developer and use — Weather and lightning alert apps

x: City Flood Alert was built by RTGS with APSDMA and IIT Gandhinagar, is an AI-based urban flood-forecasting platform, and gives 48-hour rainfall and 6-hour flash-flood warnings (first in Vijayawada).
The system was first implemented in
Vijayawada
, using satellite digital elevation models and Budameru flood data.
The APSDMA-NRSC MoU aims to prevent
lightning deaths
in rural Andhra Pradesh.

secs.t: Disaster monitoring from space → can / cannot, satellites, fire hotspots

x: Exam angle: "which CANNOT be monitored" - answer is always the human-health event.
Bhuvan combines RISAT/SAR flood-related imagery and INSAT-3DS cyclone-track information to support flood-inundation mapping and cyclone warnings.
Thermal-infrared sensors on MODIS and VIIRS detect fire hotspots.
Floods, cyclones, drought, forest fires, tsunami inundation, landslides and post-quake ground deformation can all be monitored from space.

secs.t: Programmes → Disaster Management Support, NDEM and warning systems

x: The DMS Programme uses INSAT and IRS, is recognised as an INSAT application, and provides satellite imaging and communication support for floods, cyclones, droughts, fires, landslides and earthquakes.
ISRO assumed the lead role in the International Charter Space and Major Disasters for six months from
April 2025
The system follows the chain: Cyclone Warning Centre at Chennai, C-band uplink, S-band downlink and reception by coastal disaster-warning receivers.

secs.t: Agriculture programmes → full form and purpose

x: FASAL
provides pre-harvest crop acreage and production forecasts using space, agro-meteorological and land-based observations.
YES-TECH estimates crop yield using satellite technology for crop insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana.
The SAC drought geoportal tracks
rainfall, temperature and soil moisture
for drought-related assessment.
Microwave and SAR sensors are particularly suitable for soil-moisture measurement; NISAR uses L-band and S-band radar for such applications.

secs.t: Fisheries and maritime safety → devices, developer and advisories

x: PFZ advisories identify fish-rich areas using satellite observations of
chlorophyll and sea-surface temperature
Nabhmitra is a satellite-based fishermen safety device developed by ISRO’s Space Applications Centre, Ahmedabad, and tested at Neendakara in August 2023.
The RTGS hub at Vijayawada provides satellite-based alerts to coastal fishermen about
cyclones, high waves and fish shoals

secs.t: Applications → telemedicine, tele-education and navigation

x: Village Resource Centres are single-window centres combining tele-education, telemedicine, weather information and remote-sensing-based land and water advisories.
INSAT and GSAT
satellite communication systems have enabled tele-education, telemedicine and Village Resource Centres.
The ISRO Telemedicine Network links
border posts and rural clinics
through satellite-enabled medical services.
The Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Tracking System fitted 50,000
mineral vehicles
with AIS-140 tracking devices.

secs.t: AP Space Applications Centre (APSAC) → drought, yield, APSSDI and shoreline data

x: APSSDI standardises GIS layers and supports spatial mapping; the satellite-based lightning alert application is not its stated function.
APSAC undertakes YES-TECH yield estimation in
Nandyal and Kakinada
with ISRO and the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
APSAC mapping of Andhra Pradesh’s 1,053-kilometre coast recorded 26% erosion, 54% accretion and 20% stable coastline.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: NVS-02 was stranded in the wrong orbit, limiting its intended use in the NavIC system.
GAGAN (ISRO-AAI) payloads fly on GSAT-8, 10 and 15.
India proposed both a BRICS Space Economy and a stronger BRICS remote-sensing constellation, representing expanded cooperation in space applications.

rows.title: Space debris, space situational awareness and international space law

secs.t: Space debris — definition, sources, terms and FIRSTs

x: Space debris consists of non-functional man-made objects, including fragments, that are in orbit or re-entering the atmosphere.
The ESA Space Environment Report 2025 estimated more than
1.2 million
objects larger than 1 cm.
Mission Shakti was a DRDO kinetic-kill anti-satellite test that destroyed the Indian satellite Microsat-R at approximately 300 km altitude, raising debris concerns.

secs.t: SSA systems and trackers → agency and aim

x: Exam angle: "NETRA - which agency / what aim" → ISRO / safeguard Indian space assets.
Project NETRA aims to provide indigenous space situational awareness and
safeguard Indian space assets from debris and collisions
The policy push encourages private LiDAR satellites and expansion of NETRA with radars and telescopes; it does not restrict debris tracking exclusively to government agencies.

secs.t: Data → ISSAR 2025 and collision avoidance manoeuvres

x: ISSAR 2025 recorded 1,911 catalogued re-entries.
Indian satellites logged over
1.5 lakh
close-approach alerts in 2025.
RISAT-2B performed a collision avoidance manoeuvre to avoid
a defunct US satellite
Regular CAMs involved Cartosat, Resourcesat and GSAT during 2021–25, 18 CAMs were recorded in 2025, and their purpose is collision avoidance and satellite safeguarding.

secs.t: Rules and mitigation → re-entry rules, DFSM 2030, POEM, ADR

x: Inflatable sails add drag so POEM re-enters within months.
PSLV-C62 was planned to restart PS4 and de-boost it into a re-entry trajectory after payload injection.
The planned ADR mission involves a servicer craft equipped with a robotic arm or net to capture a defunct Indian rocket body; it is being tested at URSC.

secs.t: Treaties → year, core rule and India's status

x: The Outer Space Treaty provides that space is free for all and does not recognise national sovereignty or appropriation.
The Liability Convention (1972), to which India is a party, makes the launching State absolutely liable for damage on the Earth's surface and liable only for fault for damage caused in outer space.

secs.t: Organisations and accords → UNCOPUOS, IADC, Zero Debris Charter, Artemis

x: The UN Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space was established in 1959, and India is a founding member.
UNCOPUOS guidelines on long-term sustainability and debris mitigation guide India's
Department of Space
The Artemis Accords were launched by the United States in 2020 and set out non-binding principles for peaceful and transparent exploration.

secs.t: Debates → weaponisation of space, PAROS and India's stance

x: The United States
declared the moratorium on destructive direct-ascent ASAT tests in April 2022, and the issue was subsequently taken up in a UNGA resolution.
1 is a proposed measure: strengthen the Outer Space Treaty with clear limits on destructive ASAT tests and deliberate debris creation.
The stated approach was '
cooperation over confrontation
', with the aim of a safe, secure, peaceful and sustainable space domain anchored in international law.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India does not have a Space Activities Act specifically addressing liability, which is identified as a significant legal gap.
Space debris threatens Gaganyaan, BAS and India's approximately 50 satellites currently in orbit.
Treaties dating from the 1960s–70s do not adequately address cumulative harm or mega-constellations.

rows.title: DRDO - vision, mission, structure, major laboratories and technology clusters
sub: Group-II M2-B-12: DRDO - structure, vision and mission

secs.t: DRDO — formation, predecessors, motto, vision and mission

x: Exam angle: motto-matching questions. Tejasvinavadhitamastu is not DRDO's motto; Balasya Mulam Vigyanam is.
All four statements describe elements of DRDO's mission, including production-oriented development, indigenous capability, combat effectiveness, troop well-being and Aatmanirbharta.
DRDO's motto is '
Balasya Mulam Vigyanam
' ('the source of strength is science'), the answer asked in RPSC 2021.

secs.t: DRDO leadership → parent department, Chairman–Secretary and hierarchy

x: The hierarchy is Ministry of Defence, Department of Defence R&D, Secretary DD R&D who is also Chairman DRDO, Director Generals and then laboratory directors.
All three statements correctly describe the three-level DRDO hierarchy: Secretary DDR&D and Chairman at Level I, the two DGs at Level II, and lab directors and corporate directorates at Level III.

secs.t: Technology clusters → focus and constituent labs

x: Aeronautics includes ADE, GTRE, CABS and ADRDE; Missiles and Strategic Systems includes DRDL, RCI and ASL; Naval Systems and Materials includes NSTL, NPOL and NMRL; Combat Vehicles includes CVRDE and VRDE.
LRDE, DLRL, DEAL and CAIR belong to the Electronics and Communication cluster.
Each technology cluster is headed by a Director General, to whom the directors of laboratories in that cluster report.

secs.t: DRDO laboratories → full form, location and field — Key labs

x: Exam angle: "RCI, Hyderabad stands for?" (Research Centre Imarat) and "DFRL is at?" (Mysuru). Hyderabad is the missile hub: DRDL, RCI, ASL, DMRL and DLRL are all there.
The
Aeronautical Development Establishment
(ADE), Bengaluru works on UAVs such as Rustom/TAPAS BH-201, Nishant and the Lakshya target drone.
Research Centre Imarat (
RCI
), Hyderabad specialises in missile guidance and avionics, including IIR seekers, Ku-band RF seekers and navigation systems.

secs.t: DRDO laboratories → full form, location and field — Other labs often asked together

x: LRDE, Bengaluru works on radars.
ADA is an autonomous society under the Ministry of Defence that designs LCA Tejas with DRDO, but it is not itself a DRDO laboratory.

secs.t: Institutes → DRDO–academia centres, new labs and research cells

x: DIA-CoEs are a network of 15 DRDO Industry Academia Centres of Excellence at premier institutions such as IITs, IISc and central universities.
The figures referred to were five newly established laboratories and fifteen new DRDO centres working on underwater and space awareness.
Agnishodh is the Indian Army's research cell at IIT Madras and links Army requirements with academic research and development.

secs.t: Spin-off products → use and lab

x: Lukoskin is a polyherbal product used for leucoderma or white patches and was developed by DIBER at Haldwani.
Bio-toilets or bio-digesters for human-waste treatment in railway coaches were developed by
DRDE, Gwalior and DRL, Tezpur
NETRA or Netra V2 is a mini-UAV intended for police and disaster-management applications.
Nocdurna
is a commercial drug and is not a DRDO product.

secs.t: Schemes → Technology Development Fund and technology transfer

x: The new TDF policies focus on
deep-tech and cutting-edge technologies
and seek greater participation of private firms in co-development.
Since 2020, Indian industry has received royalty-free access to DRDO patents through technology transfer, and DRDO test facilities are open to the private sector.
DRDO helped ISRO test the Gaganyaan
crew-escape parachute recovery system

secs.t: Places → DRDO facilities in Andhra Pradesh

x: NSTL, Visakhapatnam
develops the Multi-Influence Ground Mine and SMART, or Supersonic Missile Assisted Release of Torpedo.
Nagayalanka in coastal Krishna district is the site of DRDO's planned missile test range for flight trials of tactical missiles.
The ADA Aircraft Integration and Flight Testing Complex in Sri Sathya Sai district had its groundbreaking in 2026 and involves an investment of ₹15,803 crore.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The centre was established under INMAS to train personnel of the Ministry of Defence, Ministry of Home Affairs and National Disaster Management Authority in CBRN-related preparedness.
DRDO designed or contributed to systems including
Agni, Prithvi, Tejas, Pinaka and Akash
, forming part of the foundation of Aatmanirbharta in defence.
The AP defence-infrastructure locations highlighted are NSTL at Visakhapatnam, the Kurnool test range, the planned Nagayalanka range and the ADA complex in Sri Sathya Sai district.

rows.title: Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme - Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul, Nag
sub: Group-II M2-B-14: Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme - Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Trishul and Nag

secs.t: IGMDP — launch, phases, completion and FIRSTs

x: The phases were Prithvi and Trishul during 1984–89, Nag and Akash during 1989–92, and Agni during 1992–2008.
The IGMDP was launched in 1983 under
Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
, popularly known as the Missile Man of India.
Long-range tracking systems, composites, ring laser gyros and radomes were identified as IGMDP spin-offs.

secs.t: Persons → role and title in the missile programme

x: Kalam was project director of SLV-III (Rohini).
Dr Tessy Thomas is known as the “Missile Woman of India”, played a key role in Agni-V and is called “Agniputri”.
Dr V.K. Saraswat was a former DRDO chief and led the Prithvi and ballistic missile defence programmes.

secs.t: IGMDP missiles → type, range class and service

x: Exam angle: "Which is a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile?" The answer is Nag (Prithvi, Akash and Trishul are not).
Prithvi is a surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile with a range of 150–350 km and uses liquid fuel.
Akash is a medium-range surface-to-air missile with a range of about 25–30 km, a speed of approximately Mach 2.5 and an altitude capability of 18 km.

secs.t: Prithvi → variants, Dhanush and the PAD interceptor

x: Prithvi-II has a range of 350 km and a payload capacity of 500–1,000 kg.
Prithvi-II was first tested in 1996 and inducted in 2003.
The first two statements are correct.
Dhanush (Prithvi-III) is the Navy's ship-launched Prithvi (UPSC).

secs.t: Agni series → range, propellant, tests and ICBM status — Range and propellant

x: Agni-I is a single-stage solid-fuel missile with a range of about 700–800 km and is approximately 15 metres long.
Agni-IV uses RINS and MINGS navigation systems and has a circular error probable (CEP) of less than 100 metres.
Agni-V is a three-stage solid-fuel, canister-launched missile with a stated range of 5,000 km or more, and MIRV capability has been tested with it.

secs.t: Agni series → range, propellant, tests and ICBM status — ICBM status (sources differ)

x: Exam angle: "not correct about Agni-5" → "not exclusively indigenous".
Mission Divyastra, conducted in 2024, involved Agni-V with Multiple Independently targetable Re-entry Vehicles (MIRVs).
The advanced Agni MIRV test occurred on 8 May 2026, Agni-1 was tested from ITR Balasore on 22 May 2026, and Agni-4 from ITR Chandipur on 6 August 2026.

secs.t: SAMs → Akash and Trishul variants, outcome and successors

x: Akash Prime is an upgraded Akash Mk-I fitted with an indigenous active Radio Frequency seeker.
Akash-NG is canister-launched, has an approximate range of 70 km, and was cleared for induction in 2023 by both the Army and the IAF.
Trishul was closed on 27 February 2008 after failing to meet operational requirements and suffering delays and cost overruns.
QRSAM
, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, is the later indigenous short-range successor to Trishul.

secs.t: Nag family → variants and features

x: Nag Mk-2 (NAMIS) is the tracked fire-and-forget 'tank killer' approved for Army procurement.
Akash Prime is a surface-to-air missile (upgraded Akash Mk-I with an active RF seeker), not one of the fire-and-forget ATGMs.
Nag carries an 8 kg HEAT tandem warhead; NAMICA can carry up to six missiles; and the Nag Missile Carrier is a tracked amphibious vehicle.

secs.t: Terms → guidance features, missile names and non-missiles

x: SANT is an air-launched stand-off anti-tank guided missile employing
Lock-On After Launch
guidance.
Nag uses an Imaging Infra-Red seeker, whereas Akash Prime uses an active RF seeker and SANT uses Lock-On After Launch.
Pinaka is a multi-barrel rocket launcher, Tejas is an aircraft, Lakshya is a target drone, and Nishant is a UAV; none is a missile.

secs.t: Places and regimes → missile test ranges and MTCR

x: Coastal ranges in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha support sea-skimming missile trials; Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island is off the Odisha coast, and LRAShM is cited as an example.
The MTCR concerns missiles and UAVs able to carry a 500 kg payload over a range of 300 km.
India's MTCR membership facilitated BrahMos exports and high-technology imports.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The IGMDP transformed India from a missile importer into a missile-exporting power and provided the foundation for Agni-V MIRV, ballistic missile defence and BrahMos-era programmes.
The approval provides for transfer of technology of conventional missiles, including Nag, to private industry, while Agni remains in state production.
Trishul
is the IGMDP missile that was never inducted; its programme was shut in 2008.

rows.title: Missiles beyond IGMDP - BrahMos, Nirbhay, Astra, Pralay, hypersonic technology, Mission Shakti (ASAT)
sub: Group-II M2-B-15: Missiles beyond IGMDP - BrahMos, Astra, Nirbhay, hypersonic systems and Mission Shakti

secs.t: Missile classes — definitions, types and terms

x: SFDR uses atmospheric air for combustion and was demonstrated from ITR Chandipur for application in
long-range air-to-air missiles
Mission Divyastra (11 Mar 2024) was the first MIRV test, carried out on
Agni-V
. Prithvi-II is a short-range ballistic missile, BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile, and K-4 is a submarine-launched missile; none was the Divyastra MIRV platform.

secs.t: Hypersonic technology → Indian systems and FIRSTs

x: India's HSTDV flew at above Mach 6 and validated scramjet combustion and thermal protection at temperatures exceeding 2,000°C.
India's first reported flight-trial of the long-range hypersonic missile took place on
16 November 2024
The missile is reported to use skipping manoeuvres, with a peak speed of about Mach 10 and an average speed of about Mach 5.

secs.t: BrahMos → partnership, features, variants and combat use — Partnership and name

x: Exam angle: "BrahMos is developed by India and ___" (Russia). This was asked in APPSC G2 2025.
BrahMos uses a solid booster and liquid ramjet, combines inertial and satellite navigation, and can be fired from a Transport Launch Canister in fire-and-forget mode.
BrahMos combines the names of the Brahmaputra (India) and Moskva (Russia) rivers, reflecting the India-Russia joint venture.

secs.t: BrahMos → partnership, features, variants and combat use — Variants and launch platforms

x: The base system has land, ship, submarine and air-launched versions; BrahMos-NG is a lighter version for platforms including Tejas; and BrahMos-II is planned as a hypersonic missile.
The BrahMos Integration and Testing Facility at
Lucknow
(in the UP defence corridor) was inaugurated on 11 May 2025, with the first batch flagged off within five months.

secs.t: Cruise and air-to-air missiles → Nirbhay, ITCM and Astra

x: Nirbhay has an approximate range of 1,000 km, uses a turbojet, can carry conventional or nuclear warheads, and has a payload of about 200–300 kg.
Nirbhay hugs the terrain at low altitude, which helps it evade or reduce radar detection.
ITCM is the successor to Nirbhay and is powered by the indigenous
Manik small turbofan engine
developed by GTRE.
Astra is a DRDO-developed family of beyond-visual-range air-to-air missiles using an active radar seeker.

secs.t: Other new missiles → type and role

x: Pralay is a quasi-ballistic short-range tactical surface-to-surface missile with a 150–500 km range, conventional warhead and manoeuvrable re-entry capability.
Shaurya
is a canister-launched hypersonic surface-to-surface tactical missile with a range of about 700–1,900 km and nuclear capability.
QRSAM, or Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile, forms
the mid-range layer of the Integrated Air Defence Weapon System
MPATGM is a man-portable, third-generation fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile; its procurement was approved by the DAC in July 2026.

secs.t: Air-defence shields → Sudarshan Chakra, Project Kusha and BMD layers

x: Project Kusha is associated with three interceptors: M1 of about 150 km, M2 of about 250 km and M3 of about 350–400 km range.
Phase-I exo-atmospheric interception uses PAD/Pradyumna; Phase-I endo-atmospheric interception uses AAD/Ashwin; Phase-II uses AD-1 for exo-atmospheric and AD-2 for endo-atmospheric interception.
Prithvi Air Defence or Pradyumna is an exo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 50–80 km altitude, while AAD or Ashwin is an endo-atmospheric interceptor operating at 15–30 km.

secs.t: Mission Shakti (2019) → India's ASAT test

x: Exam angle: PYQ statement pairs. "Destroyed a live satellite in LEO" is correct. "Done in the upper atmosphere so there is no debris" is wrong.
A DRDO PDV Mk-II interceptor destroyed the live satellite Microsat-R during Mission Shakti.
The interception was conducted at a low LEO altitude so that the resulting debris would decay relatively quickly.

secs.t: Countries → partners, buyers and foreign missiles

x: BrahMos is a joint venture with Russia, while R-73 Archer and S-400 are Russian systems.
The Philippines
became India's first BrahMos export customer through a 2022 deal valued at $375 million.
The Philippines was the first BrahMos buyer (2022 deal, deliveries from 2024).
Fattah is associated with Iran, Hwasong with North Korea, and Zircon with Russia.
Minuteman III is a United States intercontinental ballistic missile and forms the land leg of the US nuclear triad.
Kinzhal is a Russian air-launched hypersonic missile.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Ranges along the Andhra Pradesh coast were used for LRAShM validation rounds.
The assessment states that the systems are not yet fully integrated and that the rocket force remains only a concept.
Mission Shakti (2019) made India the 4th ASAT nation after the USA, Russia and China.

rows.title: Missile defence and strategic forces - BMD programme, nuclear triad, SSBN, no-first-use policy

secs.t: Nuclear weapon technology — types and terms

x: A neutron striking U-235 can split it into two smaller nuclei, such as barium and krypton, while releasing two or three neutrons that sustain the chain reaction.

Fission (atomic) weapons split heavy nuclei (U-235/Pu-239) in a neutron chain reaction, as in Pokhran-I. Fusion (hydrogen) weapons fuse light hydrogen isotopes, with a fission 'primary' supplying the heat to trigger fusion, as tested in Pokhran-II.

secs.t: Nuclear tests → date, code name and leaders

x: Pokhran-I took place on 18 May 1974 under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and was officially described as a peaceful nuclear explosion.
Pokhran-II was conducted under A.B. Vajpayee, involved A.P.J. Abdul Kalam and R. Chidambaram, and included fission as well as fusion devices.
Pokhran-II, known as Operation Shakti, was conducted on
11 and 13 May 1998
under Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee.

secs.t: Nuclear doctrine (1999–2003) → tenets, Nuclear Command Authority, SFC

x: The Political Council is headed by the Prime Minister, the Executive Council by the National Security Adviser, the Strategic Forces Command manages nuclear forces, and civilian political control is supervised by the CCS.
India’s nuclear policy includes a continued testing moratorium, strict export controls and support for disarmament and the FMCT.
Agni user trials are conducted under the aegis of the
Strategic Forces Command

secs.t: Nuclear triad → land, air and sea platforms

x: Dhanush was fired from ships, including INS Subhadra and INS Rajput; it is distinct from the K-15 and K-4 SLBMs deployed on SSBNs.
SSBNs are difficult to detect and destroy, thereby supporting a reliable second-strike capability that underpins India’s No First Use posture.
Continuous at-sea deterrence
is identified as the next step in strengthening India’s SSBN-based nuclear deterrence.

secs.t: Nuclear submarines → commissioning, features and K-series SLBMs

x: The Advanced Technology Vessel project was initiated more than three decades ago by DRDO and private firms, with Russian assistance, to build SSBNs.
INS Aridhaman (S4), commissioned at Visakhapatnam in April 2026, is larger than INS Arihant (about 6,000 t, 4 VLS): about 7,000 t with 8 VLS for 24 K-15 or 8 K-4/K-5.

secs.t: Ballistic Missile Defence → tiers and interceptors

x: AD-1 and AD-2 are Phase II BMD interceptors intended to address longer-range threats, including those in approximately the 5,000-km class.
The Long-Range Tracking Radar, known as Swordfish, tracks ballistic missiles and space objects at distances of more than 1,500 km.
In June 2026, DRDO demonstrated a multi-layered BMD system with interceptors destroying targets, placing India among the few countries capable of engaging threats up to ICBM class.

secs.t: Air defence systems → origin and operators; Mission Sudarshan Chakra

x: Project Kusha is reported as a long-range air-defence project with M1, M2 and M3 interceptors of about
ranges, respectively.
UPSC 2026 keyed as correct only that Mission Sudarshan Chakra aims to enhance air defence, BMD and aerial offensive capabilities; it is a networked national shield (Vision 2035).

secs.t: Regimes → non-proliferation, India's status and reasons

x: India considers the NPT discriminatory because it creates an unequal division between recognised nuclear-weapon states and other states, a position often described as opposition to nuclear apartheid.
India has not signed the CTBT because it seeks a link between the treaty and
time-bound global nuclear disarmament
; it nevertheless observes a voluntary test moratorium.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The cited deployment was linked to
SSBN deterrence patrols and canisterised Agni missiles
INS Aridhaman (S4), the third Arihant-class SSBN (about 7,000 t, 8 VLS), was commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 3
April 2026
The US triad consists of Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missiles, strategic bombers and Ohio/Columbia-class SSBNs.
India is described as having a fully operational triad alongside
the United States, Russia and China

rows.title: Defence platforms and systems - Tejas LCA, Arjun MBT, radar and EW systems, naval platforms
sub: Group-II M2-B-13: Technologies developed by DRDO - platforms, sensors, materials and spin-off technologies

secs.t: Defence platforms — FIRSTs and LASTs

x: INS Vikrant is India’s first indigenous aircraft carrier, designated IAC-1, and was built by Cochin Shipyard.
INS Arihant is India’s first SSBN, or nuclear ballistic-missile submarine, commissioned in 2016.
GRSE was the first Indian shipyard to export a warship; the export to Mauritius took place in 2014.
Adamya-class FPVs (eight by Goa Shipyard) are a separate class; H-561 is a hovercraft.

secs.t: Aircraft and UAVs → developer, origin and role — Military aircraft

x: The Tejas LCA was designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency and built by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited.
The C-130J is used for tactical transport and special operations; the C-17 for strategic heavy lift; the IL-76 for heavy transport; and the IL-78 as a mid-air refuelling tanker.
The C-295 is an Airbus (Spain) aircraft built with Tata.

secs.t: Aircraft and UAVs → developer, origin and role — UAVs and drones → class

x: Lakshya is a pilotless target drone developed by DRDO-ADE for weapon testing.
Rustom-II or TAPAS-BH-201 is a Medium Altitude Long Endurance UAV.
Nishant is a tactical UAV intended for battlefield reconnaissance.
Ghatak is a stealth UCAV with a flying-wing configuration; its demonstrator is a high-speed flying-wing UAV.

secs.t: Land systems → type and developer

x: Exam angle: "What is PINAKA?" → Indian multi-barrel rocket system.
ATAGS is
a 155 mm towed gun developed by DRDO's ARDE with Indian industry
Dhanush is a 155 mm gun based on the Bofors design and was associated with the Ordnance Factory Board at Jabalpur.
Pinaka is a multi-barrel rocket launcher (MBRL) developed by DRDO (ARDE Pune with HEMRL), as keyed in APPSC 2018.

secs.t: Warships and submarines → class, project and builder

x: Project 17A consists of seven multi-mission stealth frigates with CODOG propulsion, speeds above 28 knots, and systems including BrahMos and MRSAM/Barak-8.
The Kalvari class belongs to Project 75, comprises six French-design Scorpene diesel-electric submarines, and INS Vaghsheer is the last boat.
Project-75(I) concerns next-generation conventional submarines with air-independent propulsion, with Navantia of Spain and L&T signing a teaming agreement in July 2023.

secs.t: Underwater weapons and systems → type and lab

x: TAL is a lightweight torpedo, Maareech is an anti-torpedo decoy, USHUS is an integrated submarine sonar, and ERASR is an anti-submarine rocket.
The AIP system was developed by DRDO-NMRL using fuel-cell technology and has been cleared for retrofit in diesel-electric submarines.
INS Astradharini is an indigenous torpedo launch and recovery vessel used for trials of DRDO underwater weapons; it was commissioned in 2024 at Visakhapatnam.

secs.t: Orders, commissionings and decommissionings → dates and numbers

x: 97 aircraft (68 fighters + 29 twin-seaters), Rs 62,370 crore, signed 25 Sep 2025.
INS Tamal was commissioned on 1 July 2025 at Yantar Shipyard in Kaliningrad, Russia.
The 2026 inductions included ASW shallow-water craft Agray, Malwan and Anjadip, survey vessel Sanshodhak, and NGOPVs Sanghmitra and Shachi.
INS Cheetah, Guldar and Kumbhir were decommissioned on 12 January 2024 at
Port Blair

secs.t: Shipyards and naval bases → location and feature

x: Hindustan Shipyard Limited at Visakhapatnam was founded in 1941 by Scindia Steam Navigation and built Jala Usha, the first Indian-built ship, in 1948.
Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is located in Mumbai and builds destroyers, Project 17A frigates and Scorpene submarines.
Goa Shipyard is located at Vasco da Gama in Goa, is a defence PSU, and builds Adamya-class fast patrol vessels for the Coast Guard.
The SAGAR and MAHASAGAR visions guide India's maritime and naval capabilities.

secs.t: Indian Coast Guard → roles, vessel classes and data

x: The Adamya-class vessels are being built by Goa Shipyard and perform surveillance, anti-smuggling and SAR roles.
The Coast Guard performs coastal security, anti-poaching, anti-smuggling and search-and-rescue roles.
The Indian Coast Guard's 84 radar stations form a coastal surveillance network established after 26/11.

secs.t: Radar and early-warning terms → meaning

x: Active Electronically Scanned Array radar has a transmit/receive module on each element and steers its beam electronically without a moving antenna.
Over-the-horizon radar uses high-frequency waves reflected by the ionosphere, enabling observation beyond the geometric horizon.
AWACS is the larger, longer-range platform with full air-battle control, while Netra is a smaller jet offering early warning and command-and-control over a shorter range.

secs.t: Indigenous radars and Netra → role and developer

x: Swordfish is the long-range tracking radar of the BMD shield (1,500+ km); Swathi (BEL, exported to Armenia) is the weapon-locating radar; Rajendra is the phased-array fire-control radar of Akash (80 km); Surya is the VHF radar for tracking stealth aircraft.
Netra AEW&C (DRDO-CABS, AESA radar on Embraer EMB-145) received Final Operational Clearance, handed to the IAF on 27
June 2026

secs.t: Counter-drone, loitering munitions and EW → developer and role

x: Indrajaal is
an AI-powered anti-drone grid developed by a Hyderabad start-up
Bhargavastra
is an indigenous counter-drone system that fires 64 micro-rockets at drone swarms.
Akash Tarang is an indigenous anti-UAV EW system using soft-kill jamming, approved for procurement in July 2026 and included in the Sudarshan Chakra layered air shield.
Vayu Astra is
an indigenous loitering munition developed by NIBE Ltd

secs.t: Stealth terms and defence materials → meaning and lab

x: TBRL is associated with ultra-fine beta-HMX and fine RDX, Kanchan is composite armour for the Arjun tank, and carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites serve high-temperature aerospace applications.

Kanchan armour is used on the Arjun tank; carbon-carbon/C-SiC composites are used for re-entry heat shields and hot-gas nozzles; super-alloys and tungsten heavy alloys serve engines and penetrator rods; maraging steel is used in rocket motor casings and submarine hulls.

secs.t: Spin-off and life-science products → use and lab

x: Lukoskin is a polyherbal ointment used for leucoderma, also called vitiligo.
Bio-toilets treat waste in high-altitude environments and have been adopted by the Railways.
The Bukhari space heater and Cognobar are DIPAS (high-altitude physiology); DIHAR, Leh works on high-altitude agriculture and herbal products.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Mahendragiri, the 7th Project 17A (Nilgiri-class) frigate and the 6th to be commissioned, joined the
Eastern Fleet
at Visakhapatnam on 18 July 2026.
A DRDO test range near
Kurnool
(21 May 2026) is part of AP's defence ecosystem; Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command, NSTL and HSL, and Sri Sathya Sai district has BEL Palasamudram and the ADA complex.

rows.title: Defence indigenisation - Make in India in defence, DAP 2020, iDEX, defence corridors, FDI in defence
sub: Group-II M2-B-16: Defence indigenisation - Make in India in defence, iDEX, defence corridors and exports

secs.t: FDI in defence → year and cap

x: The defence sector was opened to 100 per cent Indian private participation in
May 2001
, with FDI up to 26 per cent under the licensing route.
The current provision allows 74 per cent FDI through the automatic route.
Cumulative defence-sector FDI from May 2001 to June 2025 amounted to

secs.t: Policies, committees and reforms → year and provision

x: The seven DPSUs included Munitions India, AVNL, AWEIL, Troop Comforts, Yantra India, India Optel and Gliders India.
DPM 2025 (released 23 Oct 2025, effective 1 Nov 2025) covers
revenue procurement of about Rs 1 lakh crore
The four segments are fighter aircraft, helicopters, submarines and armoured vehicles or main battle tanks.

secs.t: DAP 2020 categories → priority order

x: The EoI for 600 indigenous 1,000-kg aerial bombs was issued under
Buy (Indian-IDDM)

secs.t: Schemes, portals and funds → objective and run by — Indigenisation lists and portal

x: SRIJAN is the indigenisation portal through which DPSUs and the Services list import items that Indian industry can manufacture.
ADITI funds deep-tech start-ups in
artificial intelligence, quantum technologies, hypersonics and directed energy
, with emphasis on critical and strategic defence technologies.
DISC comprises iDEX challenge rounds in which the Services set problem statements for start-ups to solve.

secs.t: Schemes, portals and funds → objective and run by — Technology Development Fund and VIMARSH

x: The Technology Development Fund is a Ministry of Defence scheme executed by
DRDO
TDF provides grants to industry, with particular emphasis on MSMEs and start-ups, to support indigenous defence technology development.
VIMARSH 2026 provides direct funding, incubation and access to test facilities for MSMEs and start-ups, and includes source-code sharing.

secs.t: Industry partnerships and MoUs → partner and outcome

x: L&T and Spain's Navantia signed the agreement in New Delhi in July 2023 to bid for the P-75(I) submarine programme.
The K9 Vajra-T self-propelled gun emerged from India–
South Korea
cooperation under the 2020 Roadmap for Defence Industries Cooperation.
Bharat Forge is setting up India's first private marine gas turbine MRO facility at
Visakhapatnam

secs.t: Defence corridors and AP defence units → place and purpose

x: The two corridors are in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, and they support decentralised manufacturing and connected supply chains; the BrahMos unit at Lucknow is linked with the Uttar Pradesh corridor.
The naval base at Rambilli, near Visakhapatnam, is intended as a new Eastern Naval Command base for submarines, including nuclear boats.

secs.t: Data → defence production, exports and contracts

x: Production reached ₹1,51,339 crore in FY 2024–25 and ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY 2025–26, while exports rose from ₹686 crore to ₹23,622 crore over the stated period.
Despite record exports, India remains outside the top 25 arms exporters and imports jet engines and defence chips.
The Philippines is associated with BrahMos, Indonesia with Astra, and the UAE was in talks with India.

secs.t: Expos, conferences and roadmaps → venue and theme

x: DefExpo 2020 was held at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, with the theme 'India: The Emerging Defence Manufacturing Hub'.
Aero India is a biennial air show held at Yelahanka in Bengaluru.
The conference is held twice a year.
RAKSHA is a 10-year roadmap.
DefExpo 2022 was held at Gandhinagar, Gujarat, with the theme 'Path to Pride'.

secs.t: Platforms → licence-built vs indigenous design

x: Exam angle: UPSC 2026 keyed only "Su-30 MKI" as made in India from {Su-30 MKI, T-90 Mk-III, Akula}. BPSC 2025 keyed both Arjun and ATAGS as Make in India platforms.
ATAGS, Arjun, Tejas, Akash and Pinaka
are identified as indigenous designs.
Swathi Weapon Locating Radar and Akash control centres are associated with
Bharat Electronics Limited

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Palasamudram, the Sri Sathya Sai ADA complex, the Kurnool range, and Visakhapatnam with NSTL, MGT MRO and Rambilli are all associated with Andhra Pradesh’s defence-manufacturing role.
Visakhapatnam is the home port of the Eastern Fleet, is associated with the commissioning of P-17A frigates, and includes important defence-related facilities such as NSTL, MGT MRO and Rambilli.

rows.title: India's energy needs and deficit - primary energy demand, per-capita consumption, peak deficit
sub: Group-II M2-B-30: Energy demand projections and the demand-supply gap in India

secs.t: Energy terms → meaning

x: D is right: energy intensity is energy used per unit of GDP, and a falling value means growth is decoupling from energy use.
Peak demand is the highest power drawn from the grid during a 15-minute interval.
Energy shortage refers to unmet energy requirement and is expressed in MU or percentage terms.

secs.t: Reports and publishers → coverage and projections — Energy Statistics India

x: Energy Statistics was published by the Central Statistics Office (CSO), now the National Statistics Office (NSO) under MoSPI.
The publication also covers imports and exports.

secs.t: Reports and publishers → coverage and projections — Projection reports → publisher

x: The NITI study projects renewables' share of generation rising from about 20% in 2024-25 to about 80% in 2070, coal falling from about 74% to 6-10% and nuclear rising from 3% to 5-8%.
NGAP (May 2026) puts the storage need at 174 GW/888 GWh, made up of 94 GW pumped storage and 80 GW BESS.

secs.t: India's energy demand → global rank and fuel mix

x: Coal
supplies about 55% of the energy mix and more than 74% of power generation.
After coal, the order was solar, wind, large hydro, and oil and gas.
Energy crisis refers to the danger of exhaustion of fossil fuels such as coal and petroleum.
India is the world’s second-largest coal consumer, and its energy demand is expected to triple by 2047.

secs.t: Data → per-capita energy and electricity

x: Per-capita energy consumption rose from 15,296 MJ in 2016 to
Per-capita electricity consumption rose from 957 kWh in FY 2014 to
in FY 2025.
Per-capita electricity consumption acts as a proxy for energy use, and a certain minimum level is required to ensure a minimally acceptable level of well-being.

secs.t: Sector-wise consumption and drivers of demand → cause and effect

x: Cooking demand is expected to fall as clean fuels replace biomass, while industry remains the largest sector with 8,764 TWh under business as usual in 2040.
Electric vehicles, farm pumps, appliances, cooling demand, data centres and telecom operations all contribute to rising electricity demand.
Data centres and telecom networks require continuous and reliable power, thereby increasing the need for dependable generation and grid management.

secs.t: Energy intensity and NDC targets → year and target

x: The 2031-35 NDC sets 47% by 2035 with a 60% non-fossil capacity target.
The non-fossil capacity share increased from 32% in 2014 to 51% in 2025, reaching the 50% target five years ahead of schedule.
The Bureau of Energy Efficiency and the National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency under NAPCC work through Energy Service Companies under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.

secs.t: Data → peak demand met and deficit trend

x: Exam angle: "near-zero peak deficit" questions; the evening non-solar peak is the new gap.
The grid had no shortage during solar hours, whereas non-solar hours had a 2% deficit, equal to 4,243 MW.
Although solar-hour supply has improved, the non-solar evening peak still creates a deficit, making storage important for meeting that period’s demand.

secs.t: Seasonal and regional shortages → cause and effect

x: C is right: the 6-11 p.m. evening peak comes from cooling demand after solar output drops, and Delhi responds with time-of-day tariffs and smart meters.
The rainfall deficit associated with El Niño affected renewable generation, including wind and hydropower.
Poor storage and slow transmission
can strand renewable power in some regions, while heatwaves can place additional stress on grids.

secs.t: Fuel demand-supply gap → import dependence and reserves

x: India's crude-oil import dependence is approximately
, with one cited estimate placing it at 88.6%.
All four statements correctly describe the reported natural-gas and LPG supply situation.

Coal remains a major component of primary energy, while FY26 output and the decline in thermal-coal imports are recorded figures; India now has the fifth-largest coal reserves (older sources said fourth).

secs.t: Plans, schemes and measures → targets

x: AT&C losses fell from 22.62% in FY14 to
in FY25, alongside measures such as RDSS, IPDS, smart meters and time-of-day tariffs.
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 is from the Ministry of Power and targets 100 GW of pumped storage by 2047; it is intended to replace the 2005 policy.

secs.t: AP power demand → plan, approval and roadmap

x: The plan is part of the CEA's resource adequacy process, recommends about 5,588 MW of thermal capacity, and APERC cleared the first 1,600 MW.
APERC approved DISCOM procurement of
of coal-based power on 6 August 2026.
APGENCO
has been allowed to import coal under the Andhra Pradesh energy roadmap.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Long-duration storage in the cited policy context refers to storage lasting more than eight hours.
India's per-capita electricity consumption is about one-fifth of China's and one-ninth of the USA's.
Nuclear power provides round-the-clock baseload electricity and can reduce dependence on fossil-fuel imports.
The “35 by 35” goal seeks to raise electricity's share to
of final energy by 2035.

rows.title: India's energy resources and import dependence - crude oil, coal, gas import share; energy security
sub: Group-II M2-B-32: Energy security of India - import dependence and diversification strategies

secs.t: Data → domestic reserves and import dependence

x: The current estimate identifies India as the world’s
fifth
-largest holder of coal reserves; an older estimate had placed it fourth.
India’s LPG supply depends mainly on stocks held by oil marketing companies.
Crude oil has the highest import share at about 88%, followed by natural gas/LNG at about 47–51%, and coal at about 26%.

secs.t: Supplier countries → share

x: Russia accounted for about 35%, Iraq about 20%, Saudi Arabia about 15% and the United States about 8% of India’s crude imports in 2025.
Russia was the largest supplier in recent years; Iraq and Saudi Arabia were major suppliers; and West Asia and Africa together accounted for approximately 65% of supplies.

secs.t: Issues → oil challenges, 2026 Hormuz shock and import bill — Core challenge & India's position

x: India’s core oil-related challenge is the combination of
supply-chain disruptions and fluctuating global oil prices
Higher oil prices increase import costs, thereby widening the trade deficit and contributing to inflation.
Strategic petroleum reserves, ethanol and electric vehicles are responses used to manage oil dependence and external-balance pressure; increasing imported crude dependence is not such a response.

secs.t: Issues → oil challenges, 2026 Hormuz shock and import bill — 2026 supply shock & prices

x: The strait lies between Iran and Oman.
The crude import volume was 21.4 MMT, representing a year-on-year increase of 13.3 per cent.
PPAC reported that the crude import bill of $13.7 billion in July 2026 was up
year-on-year.
Petroleum product exports rose 10% to
5.5 MMT
in July 2026.

secs.t: Organisations → role (OPEC+, OVL, PNGRB, SCI)

x: OPEC’s share of India’s imports has fallen below 50%, although older figures referred to a much higher share.
The 2026 proposal involved refiners and SCI, 59 ships and $1.5–2 billion, while IOC pursued Algeria deals and more US crude for 2027.
PNGRB authorised approximately
of LPG pipelines in six States in the reported August 2026 development.

secs.t: Policies and plans → year and focus

x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 aimed at energy security through higher domestic output and equity oil abroad, strategic and buffer stocks, appraisal of basins, competitive refining, free markets and better fuel quality; exams link it to storage of petroleum products.
HELP provides a unified licence for hydrocarbons; OALP concerns upstream exploration; ONGC Videsh is ONGC’s overseas arm; and overseas acreages help augment supply.

secs.t: Strategic Petroleum Reserves → site, state and capacity

x: Phase I reserves are underground rock caverns at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, with a total capacity of 5.33 MMT and about 9.5 days of cover at full capacity.
The IEA norm referred to for strategic oil reserves is
90 days of cover
, compared with about 9.5 days at India’s Phase I full capacity.

secs.t: Import-substitution fuels → terms and benefits

x: Methanol can be produced from biomass, natural gas, high-ash coal, agricultural residue and carbon dioxide captured from thermal power plants.
Methanol can replace petrol and diesel in transport, and it can also be used in diesel generator sets, boilers and partly in LPG and kerosene applications for cooking.
M15 is expected to cut gasoline/crude imports by at least 15% and reduce PM, NOx and SOx emissions by about 20%.

secs.t: Programmes → year and target (EBP, CBO, EVs)

x: Pilots began in 2001; 5 per cent blending was resolved from 1 January 2003 in nine States and four Union Territories; and blending was about 1.53 per cent in 2013–14.
The CBO is intended to promote compressed biogas and substitute LNG imports.
The sequence is EBP pilot in 2001, FAME in 2015, PM E-DRIVE in 2024 and the India Electric Mobility Index in 2025.

secs.t: Places → AP hydrocarbons

x: The KG Basin is an offshore East Coast zone, is among India’s most prolific hydrocarbon zones, and Andhra Pradesh produces gas and crude oil in the Godavari Basin.
IIPE Visakhapatnam was established in 2016, became an Institution of National Importance in 2017, and signed the stated shale-modelling pact with OIL India in April 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The disruption was linked to a 41% jump in the July crude bill, an LPG crunch and a proposed 41 MT strategic fuel system.
Both statements are true, and the time required for renewable capacity to become firm power helps explain why it has not immediately displaced fossil-fuel imports during sudden shocks.

sub: Group-II M2-B-31: National Energy Policy and the Integrated Energy Policy - objectives and projections

secs.t: Ministries and bodies → mandate

x: MNRE's missions include energy security, a larger share of clean power, energy availability and access, affordability and equity.
MoPNG handles exploration, production, refining and marketing of oil and gas.
The NITI Aayog energy vertical is associated with IESS 2047, the Draft National Energy Policy, the Methanol Economy and IEMI.
MNRE, the nodal ministry for all new and renewable energy, notified the National Policy on Geothermal Energy on 15 September 2025.

secs.t: Reports and indices → publisher

x: Exam angle: distractors are World Energy Council, OPEC, IRENA.
The first in-depth review of India's energy policies was published by the
International Energy Agency
in 2020, in association with NITI Aayog.
The IEA standard requires strategic oil stocks equivalent to
90 days
of net imports.
Renewables Integration in India 2021 was prepared by NITI Aayog with the IEA (APPSC-G1 2022 key).

secs.t: Policy documents → year and drafting body

x: The Integrated Energy Policy was prepared in 2006 by an expert committee of the Planning Commission under Kirit Parikh.
India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 was prepared by NITI Aayog in 2014–15.
The Draft National Energy Policy (2017) was prepared by
NITI Aayog
, which had earlier also produced the India Energy Security Scenarios 2047.

secs.t: Integrated Energy Policy 2006 and pricing reforms → provisions

x: The report was prepared in 2006, approved in December 2008, and aimed to meet energy needs reliably, sustainably and at least cost up to 2031-32.
The Integrated Energy Policy was drafted by the Planning Commission's Expert Committee chaired by
Kirit Parikh
, reported in 2006 and was approved by the Cabinet in December 2008.

secs.t: IESS 2047 and Draft National Energy Policy 2017 → scenarios and objectives

x: The figures are 582 Mtce in 2012, 1190 Mtce under 2040 BAU and 1385 Mtce under 2040 Ambitious; hence
A, C, B
Fossil fuels constitute nearly 90% of commercial primary energy supply and are increasingly imported.
The projection placed primary energy import dependence at 31% in 2012 and

secs.t: Acts and electricity policies → year and provision

x: Greenhouse-gas emission-intensity targets for 208 industrial units under the Energy Conservation Act 2001 feed into
the domestic carbon market
The Draft National Electricity Policy 2026 of the Ministry of Power covers hybrid RE, BESS, smart grids and Time-of-Day tariffs.
The Electricity Act 2003 enables
State Electricity Regulatory Commissions
to fix Renewable Purchase Obligations.

secs.t: Energy transition targets → year and target

x: As of 30 November 2025, total installed capacity was 509.64 GW and non-fossil capacity was 262.74 GW, or 51.55%.
The new NDC for 2031–35 proposes 60% non-fossil capacity and a 47% cut in emissions intensity by 2035.
The Updated NDC set a target of reducing GDP emissions intensity by
by 2030 from the 2005 level.

secs.t: Data → non-fossil share vs Panchamrit / NDC

x: 30 Nov 2025 break-up:
Thermal
Emission intensity:
Already down

secs.t: Terms → meaning (RPO, DER, green bonds)

x: Battery storage, biomass generators, fuel cells and rooftop solar PV
all qualify as distributed energy resources.
RPO requires
DISCOMs and open-access or captive users
to purchase a prescribed share of power from renewable energy sources.
Sovereign and municipal green bonds are growing, but the greenium is modest and access to global climate finance remains limited.

secs.t: Programmes and schemes → launch and aim

x: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana focuses on rooftop solar for one crore households.
The Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (
DDUGJY
) was launched in 2014 for rural feeder separation and village electrification.
DDUGJY is associated with feeder separation and village electrification, PMUY with LPG connections to BPL women, and Saubhagya with household electrification.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The Entropy Effect describes the possibility that rapid decarbonisation without sufficient buffers can raise grid volatility, as observed in the Netherlands and Spain.
The highlighted challenges include approximately 25 GW of stranded gas capacity and net-zero investment requirements exceeding $20 trillion.
ICEP-2024 targets 160 GW+ of clean energy, Rs 10 lakh crore of investment and 7.5 lakh jobs, with net zero by 2047 (APSES 2024-25).

secs.t: MNRE and clean energy → history and FIRSTs

x: India was the first country in the world to set up a ministry for
non-conventional energy sources
CASE was established in 1981, DNES in 1982, MNES in 1992 and the Ministry was renamed MNRE in 2006.
The first solar ferry, Aditya, was introduced in 2017 on the
Vaikom–Thavanakkadavu route in Kerala
VITO's two-year biodiesel project (April 2023) is at Ayodhya, UP (APPSC 2023).

secs.t: Institutions under MNRE → location and role

x: NIBE (Kapurthala) is for bio-energy and SECI is the implementing arm for the National Solar Mission and wind projects.
IREDA is a PSU and non-banking financial company that provides term loans for renewable-energy and energy-efficiency projects.
IREDA's MoU for innovation and research in renewable energy was with
IIT Bhubaneswar
(APPSC 2024).

secs.t: Funds → National Clean Energy Fund (NCEF)

x: The NCEF was intended to fund
research and innovative projects in clean energy technologies
, promote renewable energy technologies and reduce carbon emissions.
The NCEF was financed through a clean energy cess imposed on coal, including lignite and peat, from 2010-11.
The clean energy cess started at ₹50 per tonne and was subsequently raised to
₹400 per tonne

secs.t: Distributed energy programmes → scheme and feature

x: Phase-II of the Grid-Connected Rooftop Solar Programme had a target of
and was subsumed in PM Surya Ghar.
PM Surya Sarovar projects must add BESS with a minimum storage duration of two hours.
Family biogas plants come under the National Biogas and Manure Management Programme, and biomass power and bagasse co-generation under its own programme.

secs.t: Global initiatives and events → partners and host

x: OSOWOG is
a transnational solar grid under the International Solar Alliance
; its roadmap was operationalised at the 8th ISA Assembly in New Delhi.

ISA was launched by India and France (COP21, 2015); GGI-OSOWOG by India and the UK (COP26, 2021); the Global Biofuels Alliance by India, USA and Brazil (G20 New Delhi, 2023); and LeadIT by India and Sweden (UN Climate Action Summit, 2019).

secs.t: Reports and indices → publisher; India's global rank

x: The Renewable Energy Country Attractiveness Index is published by EY, formerly
Ernst & Young
The 2021 report on Renewables Integration in India was issued by the International Energy Agency with NITI Aayog.
IRENA reported that more than
of new utility-scale renewable-energy capacity was cheaper than the cheapest fossil-fuel alternative.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India has a 500 GW non-fossil capacity target for 2030; the 50% Panchamrit capacity goal was reported as achieved five years early, and the share was 51.93% by December 2025.
The reported wind-energy targets are
100 GW by 2030 and 155 GW by 2035
Tata Renewable's 800 MW hybrid project (₹5,750 crore) and the solar Centre of Excellence with IIT Tirupati and UNSW.

rows.title: Coal sector - reserves, production, washing, commercial mining, coal gasification

secs.t: Coal — types by carbon and age

x: Lignite resources are estimated at 47.295 billion tonnes, with Tamil Nadu leading through the Neyveli region, followed by Rajasthan and Gujarat.
Bituminous
coal is the most widely used type and includes the coking grade.
Bokaro and Giridih are in Jharkhand, Raigarh is in Chhattisgarh and Neyveli lignite field is in Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Coalfields → state and valley

x: Jharia in Jharkhand is
the largest coking-coal field
and is situated in the Damodar Valley.
Mawlong is located in Meghalaya and is associated with Tertiary coal.
The Satpura coalfield, including Pench-Kanhan and Pathakhera, is located in
Madhya Pradesh
and belongs to the Satpura Basin.
Talcher and Deogarh, including the IB Valley, are coalfields of Odisha.

secs.t: Data → reserves, production and imports

x: GSI put resources at 389.421 BT (1 April 2024) and Jharkhand leads.
India recorded
of coal production in 2024–25, the first time production crossed one billion tonnes.

secs.t: Producers, policies and Acts → year and provision

x: Central Mine Planning and Design Institute, abbreviated as
CMPDI
, functions as Coal India Limited’s planning arm.
The seven producing subsidiaries are
ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL and MCL
Coal India Limited
is the world's largest coal producer, working through seven producing subsidiaries with CMPDI as planning arm.
Coking coal
was declared a Critical and Strategic Mineral, allowing the Centre to auction its leases.

secs.t: Coal sector problems → cause and effect

x: The identified problems include poor quality, movement bottlenecks, low washery use, rising coking-coal imports and administrative issues.
Rail and logistics delays create
movement and evacuation bottlenecks
, which can disrupt thermal power generation.
APGENCO buys washed coal from
MCL's IB Valley Washery
, posts engineers at mines to stop grade slippage and seeks better coal from SCCL.

secs.t: Coal gasification, CBM and UCG → terms and products

x: Coal is partly oxidised with
oxygen and steam
at high temperature and pressure to produce syngas.
Coal gasification can produce synthetic natural gas, methanol, ammonia for fertilisers, hydrogen, dimethyl ether, ammonium nitrate and petrochemicals.
CBM is methane held in coal seams (free in joints, adsorbed in micropores) and is released by drilling wells and pumping out water.

secs.t: Coal gasification → mission, schemes and projects

x: The National Coal Gasification Mission has a target of gasifying
100 million tonnes
of coal by 2030.
BCGCL is a BHEL-CIL joint venture formed on 21 May 2024, and it is constructing the plant at Lakhanpur, Jharsuguda, Odisha.
Commercial blocks get a 50% rebate on revenue share if at least 10% of their output is used for gasification.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The West Asia conflict
increased the policy emphasis on coal gasification.
The 100 MT goal is considered doubtful because few coal-gasification projects have reached an advanced stage.
All three have been called for in the debate on coal gasification: CFB gasifiers for high-ash coal, zero liquid discharge and mandatory CCUS.

rows.title: Oil and natural gas - basins, refineries, strategic petroleum reserves, gas grid, city gas distribution
sub: Group-II M2-B-35: Non-renewable energy sources in India - coal, lignite, petroleum and natural gas

secs.t: Petroleum geology → terms and meaning

x: The Tertiary period is the period of oil formation, and anticlines and fault traps are the principal settings of most reserves.
Oil forms in organic-rich shale, the source rock.
Commercial oil commonly accumulates at the crests of
anticlines
Gas rich in hydrogen sulphide is called sour gas.
Petroleum is composed of approximately
90–95 per cent
hydrocarbons.

secs.t: Sedimentary basins and fields → state and FIRSTs

x: Ankleshwar is in the Cambay Basin (Gujarat), Bombay High in the Mumbai Offshore Basin and Naharkatiya (with Digboi and Moran) in the Assam-Arakan/Assam Shelf.
Mumbai Offshore, Krishna-Godavari, Assam and Cambay are all identified as major gas basins.
Digboi
(1889) in the Assam-Arakan/Assam Shelf basin marks the start of India's oil industry.

secs.t: Unconventional hydrocarbons → where held and basins

x: Shale hydrocarbons occur in fine-grained shale and require fracking and horizontal drilling.
CBM is held (adsorbed) in coal seams and released by pumping water.
Gas hydrates are associated with the Krishna-Godavari, Mahanadi and Andaman offshore areas.
The
Cambay Basin
(Gujarat) has the largest shale gas reserves (APPSC-G1 2017 key).

secs.t: Petroleum fuels and products → composition and use

x: PNG contains approximately 85–95 per cent methane and is supplied through City Gas Distribution networks on a continuous basis.
LPG is mainly used for household cooking, CNG for vehicles, naphtha for petrochemicals and fertilisers, and furnace oil in industrial boilers and furnaces.
LNG is methane-rich natural gas cooled below −160°C, CNG is compressed to about 200–250 kg/cm², and LPG mainly consists of propane and butane from refining.

secs.t: Exploration policies → year and provision

x: OALP allows companies to select blocks and bid year-round, using data available through the National Data Repository.
Under the Discovered Small Fields policy of 2015, small fields held by
ONGC and OIL
are auctioned to increase domestic output.
Samudra Manthan is the National Offshore Exploration Scheme, with an outlay of ₹84,084 crore up to 2030-31 and 100 per cent central funding.

secs.t: Natural gas grid → pipelines and states

x: The HVJ pipeline of GAIL connects
Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh
; Maharashtra is not on this route.
All four statements correctly describe Pradhan Mantri Urja Ganga, including its JHBDPL identity, authorised and operating lengths, and regional linkage function.
PNGRB had authorised 34,223 km of pipelines, of which 25,429 km were operating.

secs.t: PNGRB and city gas distribution → regulation

x: PNGRB is a statutory body under the 2006 Act, authorises CGD geographical areas and sets pipeline tariffs.
The two regulated activities specified are refining, storage and distribution of petroleum, and marketing and sale of petroleum products.
Oil marketing companies had established 799 Energy Stations by 1 August 2025.

secs.t: Strategic Petroleum Reserves → sites, operator and new plan

x: Phase I of India's Strategic Petroleum Reserves comprises
Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur
in Karnataka.
Phase I (Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru, Padur) gives about 9.5 days of import cover.
The proposed reserve covers about two months of crude and LNG and about six weeks of LPG, with funding through levies on LPG and gas.

secs.t: AP hydrocarbons → KG basin fields and city gas

x: APGIC holds a
10 per cent
share in the consortium involving ONGC, OIL, NTPC and British Gas for four KG-basin blocks.
Ravva is an offshore KG field associated with Cairn-ONGC, whereas KG-D6 is associated with Reliance-BP.
The target is 83.61 lakh PNG connections by March 2032.

secs.t: Coal → history, nationalisation and institutions

x: The cancellation of 204 coal blocks in 2014 led to the
Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act, 2015
, which enabled auction-based allocation.
The Coal Controller’s Organisation performs all three functions: maintaining coal statistics, monitoring captive blocks and hearing objections concerning acquisition of coal-bearing land.
Coking coal was nationalised in 1971-72, non-coking coal in 1973, and Coal India Ltd was established in 1975.

secs.t: Coal → output, gasification and problems

x: Coal gasification produces syngas containing
carbon monoxide, hydrogen, methane and carbon dioxide
Coal gasification can support production of SNG, methanol, ethanol, ammonia or urea, hydrogen and petrochemicals.
The mission target is 100 MT by 2030.
Output was 1,040.08 MT in FY 2025-26.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: IUCN Motion 042 (2025) calls fossil-fuel production
a direct threat to nature
Samudra Manthan, the strategic reserve levy plan and the Dandewala find were all presented as current developments driven by West Asia supply shocks.
The Hormuz closure led India to lean on domestic coal and gas and accelerate LNG and LPG imports.

rows.title: Electricity sector - installed capacity mix, generation, transmission, discom finances, Electricity Act 2003
sub: Group-II M2-B-29: India's energy scenario - installed capacity, generation mix and energy demand
Group-II M2-B-45: Electricity distribution reform - UDAY, discom finances and smart metering

secs.t: Data → installed capacity and source-wise mix — Total capacity and non-fossil share

x: The 50 per cent non-fossil share was reached about
five years before 2030
A record 44.6 GW of solar capacity was added during 2025-26.
In April 2023, the private sector accounted for 50.6 per cent, the State sector 25.4 per cent and the Centre 24 per cent.

secs.t: Data → installed capacity and source-wise mix — Source-wise mix

x: The descending order is coal including lignite at 42.43 per cent, solar at 28.96 per cent, wind at 10.47 per cent and large hydro at 9.58 per cent.
The plan projects all four figures: 1,121 GW capacity, 70 per cent non-fossil share, 459 GW peak demand and 174 GW/888 GWh storage.

secs.t: Data → generation, global rank and plant load factor — Generation mix

x: Thermal sources contributed about 75% and renewable-energy sources about 22% of generation in 2024-25.
All four are correct.
Coal generation fell by 3.69% in 2025-26, and its share fell for the first time in 50 years.
Electricity generation rose from 1,020.2 BU in 2013–14 to 1,830 BU in 2024–25.

secs.t: Data → generation, global rank and plant load factor — Global rank

x: The latest cited ranking places India third in renewable and solar capacity and fourth in wind capacity.
The stated ranges are coal 60–85%, nuclear above 84% or roughly 85–90%, wind 20–35% and solar 20–25%.
The
Southern Region
was identified as having the highest plant load factor.
India is the
third
-largest electricity producer in the world.

secs.t: Transmission → national grid, Green Energy Corridor, peak demand

x: The PGCIL study was conducted in 2012, the Southern Grid was synchronised in December 2013, the Green Energy Corridor was implemented from 2015, and the APERC approval came in 2026.
Intra-State GEC-I covers 8 States including Andhra Pradesh, with about 9,700 ckm of lines and 24 GW of RE, costing Rs 10,141.68 crore and funded MNRE 40%, KfW 40% and STU 20%.

secs.t: Electricity Act 2003 and regulators → year and role

x: APERC was set up under the AP Electricity Reform Act, 1998, which came before the Electricity Act 2003.
CERC handles central tariffs and inter-State matters; SERCs handle State retail tariffs and licensing; APTEL hears appeals; CEA publishes technical power-sector reports.
CERC was set up in 1998, the Electricity Act was notified in 2003, APTEL was established in 2004, and the Consumer Rules were issued in 2020.

secs.t: Electricity Rules and power markets → year and provision

x: The 2022 Rules permit discoms to clear old dues in instalments and provide for cutting power-exchange access for defaulters.
The payment cycle declined from 178 days in FY21 to
113 days
in FY25.
Automatic pass-through of fuel-cost changes is intended to prevent new deficits caused by delays in recovering such costs.

secs.t: DISCOM finances → causes, terms and data — Why SEBs went sick

x: Commercial losses, project delays and below-cost sale of power were all identified as sector problems or causes of financial weakness.
States spend about ₹2.4 lakh crore a year on farm and domestic power subsidies.
Discoms with fixed long-term PPAs buy shortfalls on power exchanges, where prices can be volatile during peak demand.

secs.t: DISCOM finances → causes, terms and data — Loss metrics → meaning

x: The ACS-ARR gap fell to
₹0.06 per kWh
in FY25 from ₹0.78 per kWh in FY14.
DISCOMs posted a profit of ₹2,701 crore in FY25, compared with a loss of ₹67,962 crore in 2013-14.
PFC annually grades DISCOMs on their
financial and operational performance
through its Integrated Rating and Ranking exercise.

secs.t: UDAY and RDSS → purpose and features

x: Distribution of energy-efficient LED bulbs
(UJALA) is a demand-side intervention under UDAY.
RDSS is reform-based and results-linked, has been extended to FY 2027-28, and uses REC and PFC as nodal agencies.
RDSS smart metering follows the TOTEX model under PPP, with priority for government offices and commercial and C&I consumers.

secs.t: DDUGJY and Saubhagya → components and milestones

x: DDUGJY was conveyed on 3 December 2014, subsumed the Rajiv Gandhi Grameen Vidyutikaran Yojana and aimed at providing 24x7 power in rural India.
Feeder separation continues under RDSS, while separated agricultural feeders can subsequently be solarised under PM-KUSUM.
The milestone occurred on 28 April 2018; 18,374 inhabited census villages were electrified; the last village was Leisang in Manipur.

secs.t: DISCOM privatisation, franchise and 16th Finance Commission

x: Repayment of the warehoused discom debt qualifies for
the Special Incentive Scheme for Capital Investment
All four pairs are correctly matched.
The input-based franchisee model was first implemented at Bhiwandi by
Torrent in 2007

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh → capacity, thermal plants and planning — Capacity mix

x: Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own and draws coal from Singareni and MCL.
Andhra Pradesh had an installed and contracted capacity of
Simhadri is in Visakhapatnam, Dr NTTPS is at Ibrahimpatnam, RTPP is at Muddanur, and Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS is at Krishnapatnam.
Hinduja National Power in Visakhapatnam is owned by the Hinduja group, not APGENCO.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh → capacity, thermal plants and planning — Coal power procurement and planning

x: APERC approved in principle the purchase of
1,600 MW of coal power through tariff-based bidding under Section 63 on the DBFOO model
The projected demand CAGR is 6.90%, and peak demand is expected to reach 30,927 MW by 2035–36.
AP's T&D losses are
, with 376 EHT substations and 33,379.72 ckm of transmission lines.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh → DISCOMs, smart metering and free farm power

x: Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy
introduced free electricity for farmers after becoming Chief Minister on 14 May 2004.
PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh aims to solarise
2.93 lakh
farm pump sets.
At bifurcation under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, APSPDCL took over Anantapur and Kurnool from APCPDCL.
About 20.79 lakh BPL SC/ST households get free power up to
200 units
a month.

secs.t: Energy data publications → publisher

x: The World Energy Outlook is published by the International Energy Agency in Paris.
NITI Aayog is associated with India Energy Security Scenarios 2047 and the 2026 Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat and Net Zero.
Energy Statistics is published by the CSO, now the NSO under MoSPI (UPSC 2009; APPSC-GS 2019).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Non-fossil sources constitute more than half of installed capacity, but their share in actual output is only about 22%, demonstrating the capacity-generation gap.
BESS is highlighted as a means of managing the evening peak in electricity demand, especially alongside variable renewable generation.

UDAY is associated with debt takeover, RDSS with results-linked infrastructure and reform grants, ICEP-2024 with the 160 GW renewable-energy target, and PM JANMAN with electrification of 24,691 tribal households.
