rows.title: Hydropower and pumped storage; large dams and their trade-offs
sub: Group-II M2-B-36: Thermal and hydro power in India - capacity, issues and reforms

secs.t: Hydropower — energy conversion, types and classification

x: Stored water has potential energy; falling water gains kinetic energy, turns the turbine through mechanical energy, and the generator produces electricity by electromagnetic induction.
Pumped storage uses surplus electricity to pump water to an upper reservoir and releases it during peak demand; it is regarded as a grid battery and a fast large-scale storage option.

secs.t: Data — hydro potential, installed capacity and dams

x: India’s hydro potential is estimated at more than 145 GW, about 36% is developed, and small-hydro potential is 21,133 MW across 7,133 sites.
Arunachal Pradesh is identified as having large untapped hydropower potential, and Subansiri Lower is cited as a 2,000 MW project.
Waterfalls support hydropower generation in peninsular rivers, whereas east-flowing rivers are generally more suitable for irrigation than power generation.

secs.t: Persons and movements → large dams

x: Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed the Sardar Sarovar project on the Narmada.
Rally for the Valley was an NBA campaign that highlighted the resettlement concerns of people displaced by the Narmada project.
Jawaharlal Nehru
used the expression “temples of modern India” for large dams such as Bhakra Nangal.
Medha Patkar
led the Narmada Bachao Andolan (MPPSC 2004).

secs.t: Large dams — sustainability and trade-offs

x: Large hydropower projects can provide flexible power generation, which helps maintain grid stability.
Hydroelectricity is regarded as cheap and clean once the project has been built, although large projects can still involve displacement and ecological trade-offs.
Hydropower is renewable, clean in operation and flexible, but its output can be affected by drought and variability in snowpack.

secs.t: Acts, policies, schemes and commissions on hydro and thermal power — Hydro policy

x: The March 2019 package included renewable-energy status, tariff rationalisation and budgetary support; abolition of all renewable purchase obligations was not included.
The SHP scheme has an outlay of
Rs 2,584.60 crore for about 1,500 MW
, with support of Rs 3.6 crore/MW or 30% in NE and border areas and Rs 2.4 crore/MW or 20% elsewhere.

secs.t: Acts, policies, schemes and commissions on hydro and thermal power — Storage policy

x: ISTS charges for BESS and PSP are waived until 2028 as a policy support measure.
Off-stream closed-loop pumped-storage projects
are exempted from CEA concurrence.
Feasibility reports were prepared for 29 locations, representing a potential of 33,240 MW.
Window-I uses the notified price, whereas Window-II involves bidding at a premium; therefore; .

secs.t: Places — major hydro projects in India

x: The Subansiri Lower project is associated with
Arunachal Pradesh and Assam
and has a capacity of 2,000 MW.
The capacities are Koyna 1,960 MW, Nathpa Jhakri 1,500 MW, Tehri 1,000 MW and Srisailam right bank 770 MW.

secs.t: Pumped storage — principle, grid role and projects outside AP

x: Pumped storage is described as the fastest-responding large-scale storage, making it useful for balancing variable renewable generation and peak demand.
Surplus electricity first pumps water upward, the water is stored in the upper reservoir, and it is later released through turbines during peak demand.
Pumped-storage hydropower is
long-duration energy storage
: it stores surplus solar and wind power as water in an upper reservoir and releases it over the peak hours.

secs.t: AP power projects — hydro, pumped storage and thermal — AP hydro projects

x: Exam angle: direct recall - "Polavaram installed capacity" (APPSC 2019:
960 MW
The Polavaram hydro project is located on the Godavari and has an installed capacity of 12 × 80 MW, or 960 MW.
Upper Sileru has 240 MW, Lower Sileru 460 MW and Machkund 114.75 MW.
Nagarjuna Sagar
on the Krishna is one of the world's largest masonry dams and serves irrigation, power and drinking water.

secs.t: AP power projects — hydro, pumped storage and thermal — AP pumped storage projects

x: Pinnapuram in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh, has a capacity of 1,680 MW and is described as the world’s first integrated renewable energy storage project.
Guntawada is the upper reservoir and Donkarayi is the lower reservoir of the Upper Sileru PSP.
The Gandikota pumped storage project is located in
YSR Kadapa district

secs.t: AP power projects — hydro, pumped storage and thermal — AP thermal plants

x: APGenco plans two 3,200 MW ultra mega supercritical plants: one at Srikakulam and one at a pithead site at Talcher (Odisha), likely as a JV with Coal India.
Dr NTTPS near Vijayawada commissioned its Stage V 800 MW unit in December 2023 (total 2,560 MW).
The resource plan approved by APERC in 2024-25 provides for
of additional capacity over five years.

secs.t: Thermal power — largest plants, capacity data and UMPPs

x: Adani's Mundra plant has a capacity of 4,620 MW, and the Tata Mundra UMPP has a capacity of 4,000 MW.
The cited past ranking placed Maharashtra first, Gujarat second, West Bengal third and Uttar Pradesh fourth.
A UMPP is a
4,000 MW supercritical coal plant awarded through tariff-based bidding
Sasan, Krishnapatnam and Tilaiya were associated with Reliance Power, whereas Mundra was developed by Tata Power.

secs.t: Thermal power — issues and flexible operation

x: Peak electricity demand reached approximately
256 GW
in April 2026.
FGD scrubbers trap sulphur dioxide in the stacks of thermal power plants.
The projected thermal capacity requirement for 2023–2035 is approximately
307 GW
Flexible operation includes pumped storage, batteries, cyclical operation of gas plants and optimisation of hydro generation alongside coal.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Pumped storage is described as the grid battery supporting India’s 500 GW non-fossil target by providing storage and flexibility.
The projected storage comprises 94 GW of pumped-storage projects and 80 GW of battery energy storage systems.
Approximately 40 GW of renewable-energy projects were reported to be stuck because they lacked power-purchase contracts.

rows.title: Nuclear energy - three-stage programme, types of reactors, PHWR/FBR/AHWR, thorium strategy
sub: Group-II M2-B-24: Nuclear technology - fission, fusion and types of nuclear reactors
Group-II M2-B-25: India's three-stage nuclear programme and the thorium strategy

secs.t: Nuclear fuels — fissile vs fertile isotopes, enrichment, non-fuels

x: is fissile and forms approximately 0.72% of natural uranium.
Pu-239 is not natural in significant quantities; it is produced from U-238 by neutron absorption and requires reprocessing.
U-235 is the naturally occurring fissile isotope, U-238 is fertile, Pu-239 is bred from U-238, and U-233 is used as the Stage III and KAMINI fuel.
Enrichment raises the share of U-235, the fissile isotope, by isotope separation; it does not increase U-238.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — fission, fusion, bombs and radioactivity

x: Exam angle: "Breaking apart of a nucleus is called fusion" is the
incorrect
statement - that is fission.
The simplified U-235 fission reaction produces barium, krypton and approximately 2–3 neutrons, along with energy.
Critical mass
is the minimum quantity of fissile material needed to sustain a chain reaction.
Fusion needs extremely high temperature and pressure, whereas fission needs a neutron hit and critical mass.

secs.t: Terms → meaning — fission, fusion, bombs and radioactivity — Atomic vs hydrogen bomb

x: An atomic bomb is based on an uncontrolled fission reaction.
The Hiroshima bomb, Little Boy, used U-235.
Beta radiation can generally be stopped by a few millimetres of aluminium.
The neptunium series is artificial.
Henri Becquerel
discovered radioactivity in 1896; its emissions are alpha, beta and gamma.

secs.t: Reactor components and reactor types

x: Moderator (heavy water, light water, graphite) slows neutrons (ii); coolant (heavy water, light water, liquid sodium) carries heat to make steam (iii); control rods (boron, cadmium) absorb neutrons and control the rate (i).
PWRs and VVERs use low-enriched uranium fuel, light water as moderator and
pressurised light water
as coolant.
Control rods restrain the chain reaction, so their absence can cause a runaway reaction and meltdown risk.

secs.t: Homi Bhabha and the three-stage programme — PHWR → FBR → AHWR — Homi Bhabha

x: India's programme begins with PHWRs using natural uranium, proceeds to FBRs using plutonium-based fuel, and culminates in thorium-based AHWRs or other thorium reactors.
Fast Breeder Reactors use liquid sodium as coolant and do not require a moderator.
Thorium-232 in the blanket is converted into uranium-233, an important fuel for the third stage.

secs.t: Homi Bhabha and the three-stage programme — PHWR → FBR → AHWR — Advanced Heavy Water Reactor (Stage III)

x: The AHWR is a 300 MW thorium reactor designed by BARC, using a heavy-water moderator, boiling light-water coolant and a Th-232 plus U-233 fuel combination.
AHWR is intended for large-scale thorium use, not large-scale utilisation of plutonium-bearing spent fuel.
The AHWR is intended to bridge Stage I and Stage III by advancing thorium utilisation without requiring the conventional passage through Stage II.

secs.t: Places — nuclear minerals, thorium reserves and uranium mines

x: The estimated quantities are approximately
3,60,000 tonnes of thorium and 70,000 tonnes of natural uranium
Monazite is a source of thorium and rare earths; it also yields phosphate and a small amount of uranium.
Thorium is more abundant, provides greater energy per unit mass of mined mineral and leaves less harmful waste compared with uranium.

secs.t: Fast breeder reactors — breeding principle, PFBR Kalpakkam, FBTR — Breeding principle

x: Fuel use is about 1% in PHWRs and about 10% or more in FBRs.
Fast neutrons turn the U-238 blanket into Pu-239.

secs.t: Fast breeder reactors — breeding principle, PFBR Kalpakkam, FBTR — PFBR, Kalpakkam

x: BHAVINI
built and commissioned the 500 MWe PFBR at Kalpakkam.
The PFBR is sodium-cooled and pool-type, with a capacity of 500 MWe and 1,250 MWt.
India is expected to become the second country after
Russia
to operate a commercial-scale fast breeder reactor.
The
Atomic Energy Regulatory Board
(AERB) must clear the PFBR’s low-power tests before commercial operation begins.
IGCAR’s 2005 milestone was the reprocessing of the mixed-carbide fuel used in the Fast Breeder Test Reactor.

secs.t: Research reactors → site and features

x: Exam angle: "Dhruva is India's largest research reactor" is TRUE.
AHWR is a BARC design for a 300 MW thorium reactor; it is not described as an already built and operating reactor at Trombay.
APSARA was Asia’s first research reactor; CIRUS used natural uranium and heavy-water moderation; KAMINI is the 30 kW U-233 reactor; Dhruva is India’s largest research reactor.

secs.t: Fusion research — ITER, Indian tokamaks, ignition

x: ITER (Cadarache, southern France) is a tokamak fusion device, the world's largest magnetic confinement experiment.
The ITER members are the European Union, India, China, Japan, South Korea, Russia and the United States.
The National Ignition Facility at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory in the United States achieved fusion ignition and net energy gain in December 2022 using lasers.

secs.t: Acts, missions and data — nuclear power expansion — Present fleet (data)

x: All four figures describe India's nuclear electricity share, NPCIL's reactor fleet and capacity, and the stated capacity target for 2031–32.
The stated deployment target is at least
five
indigenous SMRs by 2033.
The SHANTI Act 2025 repealed the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the CLNDA, 2010, allowing licensed private companies and joint ventures to build, own and operate nuclear plants.

secs.t: Acts, missions and data — nuclear power expansion — Small modular reactors

x: An SMR has a capacity of up to 300 MWe per unit and is generally about one-third the size of a conventional reactor.
SMRs generally have a longer, not shorter, refuelling interval than conventional reactors.
NPCIL floated a request for proposals for 220 MW PHWR-based Bharat Small Reactors to be used as captive plants for industry.
CODENE, the Centre of Design Excellence in Nuclear Engineering, has been established at
IIT Hyderabad

secs.t: Nuclear institutions → seat and role

x: The Atomic Energy Commission is headquartered in Mumbai and functions as the main policy body for nuclear energy.
DAE (Mumbai) was set up in 1954 for all nuclear activities.
BARC undertakes research and development in PHWR, AHWR, FBR, fuel cycle and radioisotopes.
BHAVINI is the PSU associated with building and running fast breeder reactors, with NPCIL holding equity.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The policy direction has been framed as thorium-led, involving private participation, with an associated goal of 100 GW by 2047.
The programme is significant for utilising India's abundant thorium resources and supporting the Net Zero 2070 objective.
The identified bottlenecks include a thin fissile inventory for Stage III, 10–12-year construction periods and local protests.

rows.title: Nuclear power plants in India, NPCIL, civil nuclear agreements, nuclear liability law and safety (AERB)
sub: Group-II M2-B-26: Indian nuclear reactors and nuclear power plants - locations, capacity and status
Group-II M2-B-28: Nuclear safety, regulation and international nuclear agreements

secs.t: Places — nuclear power plants → state and reactor type

x: Kalpakkam’s MAPS units are PHWRs representing the first fully indigenous PHWR design, and the site is also associated with a Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR).
Narora Atomic Power Station (NAPS) is in Uttar Pradesh and has two 220 MW PHWR units.
Kaiga has achieved a world-leading capacity factor, exceeding 90 percent according to the plant profile.
Kudankulam’s two operating 1,000 MW VVER units provide 2,000 MW, making it the largest operating station in the profile.
Rawatbhata (RAPS/RAPP) is in
Rajasthan
; its Canada-assisted RAPS-1 began in 1972 and RAPP-7 (700 MW) now operates.

secs.t: Nuclear power — FIRSTs and largest

x: Tarapur began operation with two boiling water reactors (BWRs).
Rajasthan-1 was India's first PHWR, developed with AECL of Canada, modelled on Douglas Point, and started in 1972.
Jaitapur
is the largest planned nuclear power project with a stated capacity of 9,900 MW.
Kashiwazaki-Kariwa in Japan is
the world's largest nuclear power plant by capacity

secs.t: PHWR programme — design lineage, fleet mode, NPCIL and PFBR

x: Mahi Banswara is being developed by Anushakti Vidhyut Nigam Limited (ASHVINI), an NPCIL–NTPC joint venture.
The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) is a public sector enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy and was registered in September 1987.
The 2017 fleet-mode sanction covered
ten 700 MW PHWRs
(Kaiga 5-6, Gorakhpur 3-4, Chutka 1-2 and Mahi Banswara 1-4).
PFBR is developed by
BHAVINI
(APPSC-G1 2024 key) and designed by IGCAR; NPCIL holds equity in BHAVINI.

secs.t: Data — installed capacity and targets

x: Nuclear power accounted for
of electricity generation in 2024–25.
The construction and implementation figures are 6,100 MW and 13,100 MW respectively, and the 2031–32 target is 22.38 GW.
NPCIL is expected to add
54 GW
as part of the effort to reach the 100 GW target by 2047.
Installed nuclear capacity is about
(8,780 MW) from 24 NPCIL reactors.

secs.t: Heavy water plants → place and commissioning order

x: Nangal
in Punjab was the first heavy water plant and was commissioned in 1962.
Nangal is in Punjab, Tuticorin in Tamil Nadu and Talcher in Odisha.
Kota (Rawatbhata) in Rajasthan was commissioned in 1985, whereas Thal in Maharashtra was commissioned in 1987.
The heavy water plants function under the
Heavy Water Board, Mumbai
, which comes under the Department of Atomic Energy.

secs.t: Foreign partners → projects and civil nuclear agreements — Foreign-assisted projects

x: Jaitapur is located in Maharashtra and is associated with France's EDF and six EPR units.
NPCIL and France's EDF signed the Industrial Way Forward Agreement for Jaitapur in
March 2018
NPCIL stated that the leaked files concerned balance-of-plant facilities and not nuclear safety systems.
Kovvada is planned with US AP1000 PWR technology, but its capacity and number of units were still to be finalised.

secs.t: Foreign partners → projects and civil nuclear agreements — AP nuclear project - Kovvada (Srikakulam)

x: France
was the first country to conclude a post-waiver civil nuclear agreement with India, on 30 September 2008.
The September 2008 NSG waiver ended India's 34-year exclusion from international nuclear trade; it did not make India an NSG member.
Kovvada is proposed to use
AP1000 reactors from the United States
; its capacity and unit details remain to be finalised.

secs.t: Foreign partners → projects and civil nuclear agreements — Partner-wise agreements

x: The DAE–Rosatom Strategic Vision of December 2014 set out plans for 12 or more units associated with the Russian cooperation framework.
Australia signed the agreement in 2014, it entered into force in 2015, and Australian uranium is supplied under IAEA safeguards.
The 10,000-tonne Canadian uranium arrangement is intended for safeguarded pressurised heavy water reactors.

secs.t: Organisations — IAEA, safeguards, NSG and export-control regimes — IAEA

x: The IAEA undertakes safeguards, verification, safety standards, nuclear security and technical cooperation, but it does not command member states’ military forces.
The Incident and Trafficking Database (ITDB) is associated with
nuclear security information
In 2006 India separated civil and military facilities and put its civil reactors under IAEA safeguards so that NSG members could supply fuel.

secs.t: Organisations — IAEA, safeguards, NSG and export-control regimes — Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG)

x: The NSG was formed in 1975, in response to
India’s 1974 Pokhran-I nuclear test
NSG membership could provide access to advanced technology and a say in rule-making, but it would not make India an NPT member.
India joined the MTCR in 2016, the Wassenaar Arrangement in 2017 and the Australia Group in 2018.

secs.t: Treaties → content and India's stand

x: Since India did not sign the NPT and its post-1970 weapons capability was treated as outside the treaty framework, it pursued
full fuel-cycle independence
India has not signed the NPT and considers it discriminatory because it creates unequal categories of nuclear-weapon states.
India has not signed the CTBT because it does not provide for time-bound nuclear disarmament and still permits subcritical tests.

secs.t: Acts — nuclear liability, CLNDA 2010 to the SHANTI Act 2025

x: No-fault operator liability capped at Rs 1,500 crore, with the Centre paying beyond the cap.
The Indian Nuclear Insurance Pool was created to help cover the supplier-liability risks arising under the CLNDA framework.
The graded caps are ₹3,000 crore for large facilities, ₹1,500 crore for medium facilities and ₹100 crore for small modular reactors.
The SHANTI Act caps total liability at 300 million SDR (~Rs 3,900 crore) and meets the excess through a Nuclear Liability Fund.

secs.t: Nuclear safety — AERB, zones around a reactor, safety terms — AERB - origin, status, powers

x: The AERB was set up on 15 Nov 1983 by executive order under the Atomic Energy Act 1962 and worked under the DAE.
The earlier arrangement raised an independence concern because the AERB functioned under the DAE, while the DAE was also the promoter of nuclear development.
Defence in Depth
is the nuclear-safety design approach based on multiple successive and independent protective layers.

secs.t: Nuclear safety — AERB, zones around a reactor, safety terms — Safety practice

x: ALARA
is the radiation-protection principle requiring exposure to be kept As Low As Reasonably Achievable.
The stated limits are 20 mSv per year averaged over five years, a maximum of 30 mSv in a year, and 100 mSv cumulative.
The Safe Disposal of Radioactive Wastes Rules were issued in 1987.
Emergency preparedness needs both on-site and off-site plans.

secs.t: Nuclear accidents → country, year and INES level

x: The Chernobyl accident occurred in 1986 in the then USSR, in present-day Ukraine.
The Fukushima Daiichi accident occurred in Japan in 2011, following an earthquake and tsunami.
Chernobyl and Fukushima Daiichi
were both rated Level 7 on the INES scale.
Three Mile Island (1979, INES level 5) was in Pennsylvania, USA (APPSC 2019).

secs.t: Nuclear security — dirty bombs, Nuclear Security Summits, ICONS

x: A dirty bomb, or radiological dispersal device, uses a conventional explosion to spread radioactive material.
Caesium-137 and Cobalt-60, commonly associated with medical or industrial sources, are mentioned as typical materials.
A dirty bomb does not produce a nuclear chain reaction or a city-flattening blast; its principal effects are contamination and panic.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A three-judge Bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notice in a petition challenging the liability caps under SHANTI.
The criticisms concern supplier indemnity and the omission of CLNDA Clause 46, which relates to remedies under other laws and therefore affects accountability and victims’ compensation.
Criticism has included delays in Kudankulam and PFBR, the Kudankulam data or ransomware file leak, and concerns over the independence of the AERB.

rows.title: Applications of radioisotopes in agriculture, medicine and industry
sub: Group-II M2-B-27: Applications of radioisotopes in agriculture, medicine and industry

secs.t: Radiation units, terms → meaning and safety limits

x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and damage to genetic material explains the occurrence of cancer, leukaemia and genetic mutations after ionising exposure.
Radioimmunoassay uses radioisotopes to measure minute quantities of
hormones, enzymes and drugs
in blood.
Gamma-sterilised males are released so that mating with wild females reduces successful reproduction and causes pest populations to decline.

secs.t: Institutions and facilities → role — BRIT

x: BRIT, or the Board of Radiation and Isotope Technology, is an industrial unit of the Department of Atomic Energy involved in radioisotopes, radiopharmaceuticals and isotope technology.
BRIT supplies radioimmunoassay kits, radiography cameras and gamma chambers, besides radioisotopes, radiopharmaceuticals and radiation-processing services.
India produces isotopes in Trombay research reactors, at the Kolkata accelerator and in NPCIL power plants.

secs.t: Institutions and facilities → role — Cancer-care institutions

x: The 30 MeV Medical Cyclotron at Kolkata produces
F-18 FDG
commercially for PET applications and delivers doses to hospitals.
Tata Memorial Centre is the Anchor Centre for the International Atomic Energy Agency’s ‘
Rays of Hope
’ initiative.
Food irradiation can stop sprouting, delay ripening and kill insects, parasites and pathogens.
ISOMED 2.0 is
a high-intensity gamma irradiator for sterilising healthcare products
and was completed in May 2025.

secs.t: Medical radioisotopes → radiation and use — Isotope → use

x: Iodine-131
emits beta and gamma radiation and is supplied by BRIT as sodium iodide for thyroid diagnosis and treatment.
Sodium-24 emits gamma radiation and is used in blood-flow and circulation studies; it can also help detect pipeline leaks.
Phosphorus-32
, a beta emitter, treats leukaemia and polycythaemia; exam keys (UPPSC 2012) also accept Cobalt-60.

secs.t: Medical radioisotopes → radiation and use — Disease-isotope keys

x: Exam angle: match isotope with organ/disease; "diagnosis vs therapy" pairs.
PET mainly uses the positron emitter
F-18 FDG
SPECT uses single gamma emitters, particularly Technetium-99m.
Radiotherapy can use gamma rays, X-rays or beta emitters, and gamma rays also underpin nuclear medicine.
Radon
is the radioactive noble gas used to treat cancer (APPSC-G1 2018).

secs.t: Radiometric dating and RTG — isotope → application

x: Potassium-40 to Argon-40 dating is used for volcanic rocks and layers containing fossils or hominid remains, with a range extending from thousands to billions of years.
RTGs use heat from radioactive decay and are therefore useful for spacecraft and planetary rovers operating far from the Sun, where solar energy is weak.

secs.t: Agriculture — mutation breeding, pest control and tracers

x: L. J. Stadler
first demonstrated mutation breeding using X-rays in 1930.
Mutation breeding uses radiation to produce genetic changes in seeds or plant material, after which desirable traits are selected.
P-32-labelled fertiliser traces nutrient uptake, nuclear moisture gauges help determine irrigation requirements, and BARC applies tissue culture to banana and pineapple.

secs.t: Food irradiation — process, sources and exports

x: Sources:
Gamma (Co-60), X-rays, electron beams
Uses:
Stops sprouting, delays ripening, kills insects, parasites and pathogens
→ extends shelf life.
Exports:
Irradiated
mangoes exported to USA, Australia, Malaysia, South Africa.

secs.t: Industry — radiography, gauging and radiotracers

x: Radiotracers are used for pipeline leak detection, dam seepage studies, port sediment transport, and flow measurement.
Radiation-based gauging is used for thickness measurement of plates and pipes, fill-level measurement and some automotive sensor applications.
Gamma radiography of welds and castings uses radiography cameras with sources such as
Iridium-192 and Cobalt-60

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Non-power applications in health, agriculture and industry provide the wider ‘atoms for peace’ dividend and justify the nuclear programme beyond electricity.
Technetium-99m is the most used diagnostic isotope (imaging of heart, brain, bones and lungs).
72 crop varieties have been developed by Trombay (BARC), a non-power use of nuclear technology that supports food security.

rows.title: Renewable energy sources and installed capacities in India - overall targets
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-58

secs.t: Renewable energy — definitions, classification and exam keys

x: Exam angle: "Which is NOT renewable / NOT green / NOT from the Sun" - nuclear, natural gas, geothermal are the usual answers.
Natural gas
is a fossil fuel and is not classified as green energy in this comparison; sunlight, wind and algae-based sources are treated as green sources.
Tidal energy
is generated mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon, rather than directly from solar radiation.

secs.t: Data — installed capacity, milestones, potential and rankings — Source-wise share

x: Nuclear capacity was 8.78 GW, accounting for about 1.6–1.7% of capacity.
Solar
, at 164.59 GW (Aug 2026), is the largest RE component.

secs.t: Data — installed capacity, milestones, potential and rankings — Cumulative solar and wind milestones

x: India's solar potential was estimated at 748 GW, while only about 4.5% had been utilised.
Rajasthan accounts for 23.70% and Andhra Pradesh for 9.10% of the stated potential ranking data.
Cumulative solar capacity stood at
on 31 December 2022.
In 2025, about 48 GW of renewable capacity was added, comprising approximately 38 GW solar and 6.3 GW wind.

secs.t: Data — installed capacity, milestones, potential and rankings — Rankings - India and top states

x: India ranked
third
in renewable-energy capacity after China and the United States.
Gujarat
was the leading renewable-energy State in June 2026, with 42.58 GW and 16.5% of India's renewable capacity.
India ranks 4th in the world in wind power, while it is 3rd in total renewable capacity after China and the USA.

secs.t: Capacity targets — 175 GW to Net Zero 2070

x: The 175 GW target comprised
100 GW solar, 60 GW wind, 10 GW bio-power and 5 GW small hydro
India's stated commitments include 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030 and achieving Net Zero by 2070.
The 2030 target includes approximately 292 GW of solar capacity, and around 300 GW of non-fossil capacity had been reached in 2026.

secs.t: Obligations and programmes — RPO, RCO, Green Energy Corridors

x: RPO requires
DISCOMs and large or designated consumers
to procure a prescribed share of their power from renewable sources.
Inter-State GEC lines are built by Power Grid Corporation of India Limited (PGCIL) to evacuate renewable energy from renewable-rich zones to load centres.
GEC-I covered eight States and involved about 9,700 ckm of transmission lines, 22,600 MVA of substations and approximately 24 GW of renewable-energy integration.

secs.t: Organisations — IREDA

x: IREDA is
an NBFC under the administrative control of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
(MNRE).
IREDA undertakes project financing, appraisal, consultancy and provides term, bridge and working-capital loans.
IREDA was established in 1987 and entered the stock exchanges through an initial public offering in
November 2023

secs.t: Universal angles

x: India curtailed 8,133 GWh of solar power during
April–June 2026
due to a mismatch in transmission capacity.
Approximately 40 GW of renewable-energy projects were reported to lack power-purchase agreements, creating uncertainty about the sale of generated power.
The curtailment arose from a transmission mismatch; strengthening and synchronising transmission infrastructure directly addresses that constraint.

rows.title: Solar energy - PV vs thermal technologies, National Solar Mission, solar parks, rooftop solar, ISA
sub: Group-II M2-B-38: Solar energy - technologies, National Solar Mission, solar parks, rooftop solar and the ISA

secs.t: Solar technologies — PV vs thermal, types and applications

x: Crystalline silicon cells, including mono- and polycrystalline types, use the photovoltaic effect and remain dominant in the market.
The IIT Bombay project under MNRE achieved 26% efficiency for a perovskite cell, and the perovskite-silicon tandem achieved 30.2% efficiency.
In PV cells the photovoltaic effect frees electrons and produces direct current (DC); an inverter converts it to alternating current (AC).

secs.t: Data — solar potential, installed capacity and rankings — Solar resource

x: All three statements describe the stated solar-resource conditions in India: 4–7 kWh/m²/day irradiation, 250–300 clear sunny days and about 5,000 trillion kWh of annual incident energy.
NISE estimates about 748 GW, assuming 3% of wasteland.

secs.t: Data — solar potential, installed capacity and rankings — Installed capacity

x: The reported installed solar capacity was 157.05 GW, constituting about 29 per cent of total capacity.
A record
of solar capacity was added in FY 2025-26.

secs.t: Data — solar potential, installed capacity and rankings — Rankings

x: Rajasthan
leads with about 23.70%.
The Energy Survey 2025-26 places India
third
globally in solar energy and total renewable energy.
India was the 2nd-largest solar growth market in 2025, and its ~38 GW addition in 2025 beat the US for the first time (Ember).

secs.t: Solar FIRSTs → place

x: Diu
became the first Union Territory to run 100 per cent on solar power during the day.
Modhera, the Sun Temple town in Mehsana district, became India's first
24x7 solar-powered village
Bancha is India's first all-solar-kitchen village and is located in Betul, Madhya Pradesh; it is not a Union Territory.

secs.t: Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission — launch, targets, phases

x: Exam angle: "NSM target" without a year = 100 GW by 2022 (historic); the live commitment is 500 GW non-fossil by 2030 (~292 GW solar).
The National Solar Mission is one of the eight missions of the
National Action Plan on Climate Change
, adopted in 2008.
Renewable Purchase Obligations, preferential tariffs, solar parks and research and development were associated with the Mission.
India’s successor goal is
500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030
, associated with its COP26 pledge.

secs.t: Solar schemes → year and key feature — Chronology

x: The Solar Park Scheme facilitates land, transmission and clearances for solar parks and runs up to 2025-26.
VGF schemes, including JNNSM Phase-II arrangements through SECI, provide viability gap funding to grid-scale solar developers.
CPSU Scheme Phase-II supports government producers through viability gap funding and domestic cells and modules.
The
Rooftop Solar Programme Phase-II
, launched in 2019, was subsumed into PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana.
Floating solar saves land, reduces evaporation, benefits from water cooling and has an upfront cost approximately 25% higher than comparable land-based installations.

secs.t: Solar schemes → year and key feature — PM-KUSUM progress

x: SRISTI is associated with rooftop incentives, the ARUN application and Suryamitra skill development.
The scheme includes a mandatory two-hour storage requirement amounting to 10,000 MWh.
The scheme involves ₹5,070 crore and targets 5,000 MW of floating solar capacity by 2030–31.
The scheme gives CFA of up to Rs 1 crore/MW and the 5,000 MW target is to be delivered via SECI.

secs.t: Solar schemes → year and key feature — New schemes → objective

x: GTAM is
a renewable-energy-only trading segment on the Indian Energy Exchange
(IEX), launched in 2020.
IEX was established in 2008, is regulated by CERC, and trades DAM, TAM, renewable energy and ESCerts.
The Rules were issued by the Ministry of Power.

secs.t: Places — solar parks and floating solar plants — Ultra mega solar parks

x: The capacities are Bhadla 2,245 MW, Pavagada 2,050 MW, Kurnool 1,000 MW and Rewa 750 MW.
Khavda Renewable Energy Park in Gujarat's Kutch region is projected to have approximately 30 GW of solar-wind capacity when complete and is described as the world's largest renewable-energy park.
Ramagiri hosts a
hybrid solar-wind park

secs.t: Places — solar parks and floating solar plants — Floating solar - potential and status

x: The stated national floating-solar potential is 102.18 GW, with Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh leading at about 16 GW and 14 GW, while installed capacity is only about 0.7 GW.
The first national assessment of floating solar PV potential was undertaken by the
National Institute of Solar Energy
(NISE).
Omkareshwar floating solar project is on the Narmada in Khandwa district of Madhya Pradesh.

secs.t: Solar manufacturing — ALMM, PLI, duties

x: The requirement also covers government-linked projects such as PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM and SECI tenders.
ALMM is the approved list maintained under the
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
(MNRE).
DCR requires domestic cells and modules in CPSU projects, PM-KUSUM and rooftop subsidy projects.
The sequence is PLI in 2021, BCD from April 2022, GST reduction on 22 September 2025 and REEIMS from 1 November 2025.

secs.t: Organisations — International Solar Alliance and NISE — NISE

x: NISE is an autonomous body of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy located at Gurugram and acts as a technical focal point for solar research and development.
The foundation stone was laid at the National Institute of Solar Energy campus at Gwal Pahari, Gurugram, on 25 January 2016.
The ISA Framework Agreement entered into force on
6 December 2017
, giving the organisation its treaty-based character.

secs.t: Organisations — International Solar Alliance and NISE — ISA initiatives - OSOWOG, Global Solar Facility, STAR-C

x: The
Global SIDS Initiative
, ISA Academy, Global Capability Centre and SUNRISE were launched at the 8th ISA Assembly in New Delhi.
OSOWOG
, or One Sun One World One Grid, is the transnational grid concept for sharing solar power across time zones.
The Global Solar Facility is an ISA fund designed to
de-risk solar investment in underserved regions
through instruments such as payment guarantees and insurance.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Kurnool, NP Kunta and Kadapa are the three Andhra Pradesh ultra mega solar park locations.
The Cabinet approved PM Surya Sarovar Yojana for floating solar projects.
Both statements are true, and curtailment and transmission constraints directly explain why increasing installed capacity may not translate into fully utilised generation.
AP had 4,11,915 rooftop systems (4 Aug 2026), placing it
among the top four States

rows.title: Wind energy - potential, installed capacity, offshore wind policy, hybrid wind-solar policy
sub: Group-II M2-B-39: Wind energy - potential, installed capacity, offshore wind and hybrid policy

secs.t: Wind energy terms → meaning — conversion, HAWT vs VAWT, CUF, onshore vs offshore

x: Offshore projects do not eliminate risks; they may involve corrosion, undersea cables, navigation issues and marine-ecology concerns.
IEC turbine classes are determined by site wind speed: Class I is for high-wind sites and Class III for low-wind sites.
Wind’s kinetic energy rotates the blades and rotor; the generator then converts the mechanical energy into electricity.

secs.t: Data — wind potential, installed capacity and targets — Potential

x: The assessed potential is 695.5 GW at a 120-metre hub height and 1,163.9 GW at a 150-metre hub height.

secs.t: Data — wind potential, installed capacity and targets — Installed capacity

x: Capacity rose from 21.04 GW in March 2014, crossed 50 GW in March 2025 and reached 56.09 GW on 31 March 2026.
The latest stated wind capacity of 56.81 GW represented
of the total 542 GW capacity.
Solar power
, at 157.05 GW, was the largest renewable source in the comparison, followed by wind at 56.81 GW and large hydro at 51.96 GW.

secs.t: Data — wind potential, installed capacity and targets — Climate targets

x: The wind-turbine manufacturing base has a capacity of about 24 GW per year, with 70–80% indigenisation.
The 2015 goal was 175 GW of RE by 2022, including
60 GW
of wind.
The 50% non-fossil capacity goal was met early, at 51.93% by December 2025.

secs.t: Rankings — India's global rank and state ranking

x: The 2026 Global Wind Day conference was hosted in
Goa
with the theme ‘Wind Energy: From Ambition to Acceleration’.
Gujarat is stated to lead installed renewable energy with 42.58 GW and a 16.5% share.
India is 4th in the world in installed wind capacity, after China, the USA and Germany.
Gujarat
leads with about 12,314 MW, roughly a fifth of India's wind capacity (APPSC keys).

secs.t: Places and organisations — windy states, offshore zones, NIWE, partners

x: NIWE is located in
Chennai
and functions as an autonomous body under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
All four statements correctly describe NIWE’s institutional status and functions, including resource assessment, site identification, atlas preparation, testing and certification support.
The United Kingdom is associated with the Offshore Wind Taskforce, Denmark with the 2019 agreement renewed in May 2025, and Belgium with the WEF 2026 reaffirmation.

secs.t: Policies and schemes → year and provision — offshore, hybrid, repowering — Offshore wind

x: The policy promotes co-location of wind turbines and solar PV at the same point of grid connection.
RTC renewable-energy tenders bundle wind, solar and storage to provide a firm supply of electricity.
The GEC dates from 2015 and Intra-State GEC-I covers AP, Gujarat, HP, Karnataka, MP, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu.

secs.t: Policies and schemes → year and provision — offshore, hybrid, repowering — Repowering and incentives

x: Repowering replaces ageing, less efficient turbines with more powerful modern units at the same windy site to increase generation.
The 2016 policy was revised as the
Repowering and Life Extension Policy, 2023
A universal waiver after 2030 is not stated as a support measure.

secs.t: AP wind energy — zones, capacity, Suzlon

x: Wind farms are concentrated in Rayalaseema, especially in Ananthapuramu, Kurnool and YSR Kadapa districts.
Ramagiri hosts a
hybrid solar-wind park
Suzlon
is identified as Andhra Pradesh's largest wind developer, with more than 1,700 MW.
The stated 2025–26 installed wind capacity of Andhra Pradesh is
, making wind its second-largest renewable-energy source after solar.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: El Niño and a weak monsoon were expected to dent wind and hydro output.
An oscillation originating from renewable-energy variability in Rajasthan was reportedly felt at
Kudankulam
The industry has sought a Production Linked Incentive for large forgings and export incentives.

rows.title: Other renewables - biomass, biofuels (National Policy on Biofuels, ethanol blending), small hydro, geothermal, tidal, waste-to-energy
sub: Group-II M2-B-33: National Policy on Biofuels - categories, ethanol blending targets and progress
Group-II M2-B-40: Bio-energy, small hydro, geothermal, tidal and waste-to-energy

secs.t: Other renewables — definitions, classification and types — MNRE classification

x: Biogas is produced through anaerobic digestion of organic matter and mainly contains methane and carbon dioxide, along with small quantities of other gases.
Methanogenic archaea
, also called methanogens, carry out the final methane-forming step during anaerobic digestion.
Gobar gas
is a form of biomass energy because it is produced from organic biological material, especially cattle dung.

secs.t: Other renewables — definitions, classification and types — Biofuel generations (1G to 4G)

x: Second-generation biofuels use non-food lignocellulosic residues such as
rice straw
, straw, husk, wood chips and bamboo.
Second-generation biofuels use non-food lignocellulosic residues and therefore avoid the food-fuel conflict, although their conversion is technically complex.
Both statements are true, and the enhanced carbon-dioxide capture by genetically engineered algae or microbes explains the potential carbon-negative character of fourth-generation fuels.
Geothermal energy originates from the internal heat of the Earth, much of which is generated by radioactive decay in its interior.

secs.t: FIRSTs and pioneers — India and world

x: Exam angle: match site → state; "first geothermal project" = Ladakh (Puga).
The IOCL Panipat plant, described as the first commercial 2G plant in 2022, used
rice straw
as feedstock.
India’s first biojet-fuelled flight was SpiceJet’s Dehradun–Delhi flight in August 2018, using jatropha fuel developed from CSIR-IIP sources.
IOCL Panipat became India's first ISCC CORSIA-certified SAF producer in August 2025.

secs.t: Terms and technologies → meaning — Fuels and processes

x: Bagasse, the residue of sugarcane processing, is burned in sugar mills to generate steam and electricity together.
Biodiesel is produced by transesterifying vegetable oils or animal fats with methanol or ethanol, producing fatty-acid methyl or ethyl esters.
Power alcohol refers to fuel-grade ethanol, which in India is made mainly from molasses, a by-product of the sugar industry.
Saccharomyces cerevisiae
, a yeast, ferments sugars or starch-derived sugars to produce bioethanol.

secs.t: Terms and technologies → meaning — Waste-to-energy routes

x: Incineration directly burns MSW; pyrolysis heats it without oxygen; gasification uses partial oxidation; RDF is the dry combustible fraction of segregated MSW.
Proper source segregation is essential for both gasification and anaerobic digestion because the feedstock must be suitably separated and relatively free from incompatible materials.
In a microbial fuel cell,
bacteria oxidise organic matter and transfer electrons to an electrode
, producing electricity while treating wastewater.

secs.t: Terms and technologies → meaning — Geothermal and ocean terms

x: EGS technology artificially stimulates geothermal reservoirs to improve access to underground heat.
About 20 deg C difference is needed.

secs.t: Feedstocks → fuel

x: The 2018 policy expanded ethanol feedstocks beyond molasses and recognised non-food oilseeds such as jatropha and pongamia, along with algae, for biodiesel.
Surplus food grains may be converted to ethanol only with NBCC approval (APPSC-G2 2025).
Uranium ore
is not a biofuel feedstock.
SAF uses
drop-in synthesised hydrocarbons
suitable for aviation fuel systems; it is not simply direct ethanol.

secs.t: Policies, programmes and schemes → year and provision — Biogas and bioenergy programmes

x: SATAT, or Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation, was launched in 2018 by MoPNG to promote CBG from agricultural residue and municipal waste.
GOBARdhan promotes conversion of cattle dung and farm solid waste into compost, biogas and CBG/bio-CNG.
Zakariyapura represents household units, Varanasi a centralised dairy plant and Banas a centralised large-scale model.
Phase I covers 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026, has an outlay of ₹858 crore and is implemented by MNRE through State Nodal Agencies.

secs.t: Policies, programmes and schemes → year and provision — National Policy on Biofuels 2018

x: The National Policy on Biofuels aims to reduce import dependence, promote domestic feedstock, strengthen energy security and generate employment.
The amendment allowed more feedstocks, covered biofuel units in SEZs and EOUs, and permitted exports in specific cases.

secs.t: Policies, programmes and schemes → year and provision — Support schemes and enablers

x: Viability Gap Funding, tax credits and differential pricing
are identified as enabling measures for advanced biofuels.
The revised scheme replaces the narrower expression '2G ethanol' with 'advanced biofuels', extends the timeline to 2028–29 and covers bolt-on and brownfield projects.
PM JI-VAN Yojana was launched in 2019 to support 2G ethanol and subsequently expanded to advanced biofuels.

secs.t: Policies, programmes and schemes → year and provision — SAF and geothermal policy

x: The SAF roadmap specifies 1% by 2027, 2% by 2028 and 5% by 2030, in line with ICAO’s net-zero 2050 objective.
The
BioE3 Policy 2024
supports bio-jet fuel.
MNRE notified it on 15 Sep 2025, India's first geothermal policy.

secs.t: Ethanol and biodiesel blending — milestones, pricing and data — Ethanol blending milestones

x: Mandatory E20 petrol with a minimum RON of 95 was scheduled from
1 April 2026
IS 19850:2026 covers
E22, E25, E27 and E30
petrol standards.
The Ethanol Blended Petrol programme is run by the
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
The sequence is pilot in 2001, E5 introduction on 1 January 2003, E10 achievement in June 2022, and mandatory E20 from 1 April 2026.

secs.t: Ethanol and biodiesel blending — milestones, pricing and data — Biodiesel - status and targets

x: Exam angle: E20 year, RON 95, feedstock list, gasohol/power alcohol meaning.
Biodiesel is mostly dependent on imported feedstock.
VITO launched a two-year biodiesel project at
Ayodhya
in April 2023.
The United States produces more ethanol than Brazil and mainly uses maize or corn, whereas Brazil mainly uses sugarcane.

secs.t: Places and sites → state and feature — 2G ethanol plants

x: IOCL Panipat is in Haryana and uses rice straw and bagasse; Numaligarh is in Golaghat, Assam and uses bamboo; HPCL Bathinda is in Punjab; BPCL Bargarh is in Odisha.
Run-of-river small hydro projects may use hill streams, canal falls and water released at dam toes.
Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttarakhand
together hold about half of India's small hydro potential.

secs.t: Places and sites → state and feature — Tidal, wave and OTEC sites

x: The
Gulf of Khambhat
in Gujarat is identified as India's best tidal-energy site, with an estimated potential of about 7,000 MW.
The Durgaduani Creek tidal project is a pilot project in the Sundarbans.
Lakshadweep and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands are identified as Indian OTEC locations.

secs.t: Organisations and institutes → role

x: SSS-NIBE is at
Kapurthala, Punjab
The National Institute of Ocean Technology (NIOT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, is India's lead ocean-energy research body.

secs.t: Data — capacity, potential and figures

x: India's estimated geothermal potential is about
10,600 MW from 381 hot springs
, according to the stated GSI estimate.

secs.t: Issues and challenges

x: These are the stated advantages.
The stated challenges are uneven reservoir distribution, high drilling costs, subsidence and water pollution from geothermal fluids.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — small hydro, bioenergy, WtE plants, biofuel policy

x: Jindal waste-to-energy plants are associated with Guntur, Naidupalem and Kapuluppada in Visakhapatnam.
The
AP Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024
supports biofuels.
AP had about
from biomass, bagasse and waste.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Mandatory E20 is scheduled from 1 April 2026, BIS standards extend up to E30, and the E20 roadmap indicates a possible 1–2% fuel-efficiency loss.
The debate covers diversion of land from pulses and oilseeds, rising maize area with declining pulse area, and concerns regarding rising sugar prices.
Denmark
has targeted 100% biomethane in its gas grid by 2030, with manure rather than crops as the stated source.

rows.title: Green hydrogen - National Green Hydrogen Mission, electrolysers, applications
sub: Group-II M2-B-41: Green hydrogen - National Green Hydrogen Mission and applications

secs.t: Green hydrogen — colour types, definitions and standard

x: Grey hydrogen releases carbon dioxide during steam methane reforming, blue hydrogen uses carbon capture and storage, and white hydrogen is naturally occurring geological hydrogen.
Green hydrogen comes from
electrolysis of water using renewable power
(PYQ 2023) and is the only zero-carbon colour.
The Green Hydrogen Standard permits well-to-gate emissions of not more than 2 kg CO2-equivalent per kg of hydrogen, measured as a 12-month average.

secs.t: National Green Hydrogen Mission — approval, outlay and components

x: The Mission has a total outlay of
₹19,744 crore
up to financial year 2029-30.
SIGHT has two incentives, electrolyser manufacturing and green H2 production.
ISTS charges are waived for eligible projects commissioned up to
December 2030
Four
Hydrogen Valley Innovation Clusters have been sanctioned with an allocation of approximately ₹170 crore.

secs.t: Targets and progress — data

x: The Mission targets 5 MMT of green hydrogen annually by 2030, with production potentially reaching 10 MMT when exports are included.
All four are stated Mission outcomes: about 50 MMT annual GHG reduction, more than ₹1 lakh crore lower fossil imports, over ₹8 lakh crore investment and 6 lakh jobs.
A supply of 20,000 MTPA of green hydrogen has been awarded for the refineries of
IOCL, BPCL and HPCL

secs.t: Technologies — electrolyser types, storage and fuel cells

x: Alkaline uses liquid KOH; PEM uses a solid polymer membrane; solid oxide uses high-temperature steam; and AEM uses an anion exchange membrane while avoiding precious metals.
PEM
electrolysers use a solid polymer membrane and respond quickly to variable renewable-energy input.
Hydrogen may be stored as compressed gas, cryogenic liquid hydrogen, or solid metal hydrides, and may also be carried as ammonia or methanol.

secs.t: Applications — industry, green ammonia, steel, mobility, H-CNG

x: Green ammonia is produced from
nitrogen and green hydrogen
Fertilisers, refineries and steel are hard-to-abate sectors for which hydrogen has important applications.
Hydrogen can replace
coking coal
as the reducing agent in DRI-based steel production, thereby reducing carbon emissions.
All four statements describe identified applications of green hydrogen, including industrial decarbonisation, heavy mobility, H-CNG and long-duration storage.

secs.t: Hydrogen vehicles and FIRSTs

x: The first hydrogen-powered train coach tested by the Railways was associated with Chennai’s Integral Coach Factory (ICF).
The first hydrogen fuel-cell train in service is described as a 10-coach train on the 89-km Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana from July 2026.
H-CNG buses, using hydrogen-blended compressed natural gas, were associated with
Delhi and IOCL in 2020

secs.t: Places — hydrogen hubs and ports

x: Deendayal (Kandla) is in Gujarat, V.O. Chidambaranar (Tuticorin) is in Tamil Nadu and Paradip is in Odisha.

secs.t: Issues and constraints

x: Approximately
9 litres
of purified water are required per kilogram of hydrogen, which can constrain projects in arid solar regions.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — green hydrogen and ammonia projects

x: SRM University-AP
is the state nodal agency for the Andhra Pradesh Green Hydrogen Valley.
The Centre of Excellence is associated with JK Srivastava
Hynfra, an Indo-Polish joint venture
Amaravati is associated with the Green Hydrogen Valley Declaration, not a Paradip green ammonia export terminal.
NTPC Simhadri began green hydrogen blending trials with
a seawater-to-hydrogen plant
in January 2026.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Green hydrogen is important for hard-to-abate sectors, energy independence by 2047 and the national net-zero objective for 2070.
India signed long-term green ammonia and green methanol export agreements with
Japan
ese companies.
United States credits of up to $3 per kg
can improve the competitiveness of US-produced hydrogen and create export competition for Indian producers.

rows.title: Energy storage - battery technologies, PLI for advanced chemistry cells, grid storage
sub: Group-II M2-B-42: Energy storage - battery technologies, PLI for advanced chemistry cells and grid storage

secs.t: Batteries — cell parts and types — Cell parts

x: Cell parts:.
Anode
= oxidation during discharge.
Cathode
= reduction.
Electrolyte
= lets ions flow, keeps electrodes apart.

secs.t: Batteries — cell parts and types — Battery types → electrodes → uses

x: A nickel-metal hydride battery replaces cadmium with a metal hydride and is used in hybrid vehicles and portable electronics.
Lead-acid is used for automotive starting and UPS; NMC has a nickel-manganese-cobalt cathode and high energy density; LFP is safe with long cycle life; flow batteries suit grid-scale storage.
Ni-Cd batteries (nickel and cadmium electrodes, rechargeable) are used in calculators, cordless appliances, transistors, torches and shavers.

secs.t: Mechanical and thermal storage — method → principle

x: Compressed air storage does compress air into caverns and later expand it through turbines.
Pumped storage uses surplus power to pump water to a higher elevation; the water is released through turbines when electricity is needed during peak periods.
Molten salt provides thermal storage in concentrated solar power plants, enabling electricity generation after sunset.

secs.t: Battery raw materials — critical elements, places and missions

x: KABIL is a joint venture of NALCO, HCL and MECL that pursues overseas mineral assets, including lithium blocks in Argentina.
Lithium carbonate is a white crystalline salt obtained from lithium minerals and brines and serves as
a key raw material for lithium-ion cells
More than 70% of lithium processing and most cobalt refining are concentrated in a few countries
, creating a supply-chain risk for battery manufacturing.

secs.t: Schemes and rules → year and provision — PLI for ACC batteries

x: Approved 12 May 2021 (launched Oct 2021).
The 40 GWh allocation comprised 20 GWh for Ola Electric, 15 GWh for Reliance in two portions, and 5 GWh for Rajesh Exports.
Visa delays, local-content rules and missing technology were identified as hurdles.
The remaining 10 GWh was put to global bids for
grid-scale storage

secs.t: Schemes and rules → year and provision — Storage framework and obligation

x: All three are stated policy measures: waiver of ISTS charges for eligible co-located storage, consumer ownership or leasing, and recognition of ESS as a power-system element.
The Energy Storage Obligation provided for a rise from
1 percent in 2023-24 to 4 percent in 2029-30
The requirement is 336 GWh, whereas the existing BESS capacity was about 500 MWh; these are not equal in magnitude.

secs.t: Schemes and rules → year and provision — EV schemes

x: Extended Producer Responsibility requires collection, recycling or refurbishment, and use of recycled material in new batteries.
The material recovery target is scheduled to rise to
90 percent
BPAN is mandatory for electric vehicle batteries and industrial batteries exceeding 2 kWh.
The Hazardous & Other Wastes (Amendment) Rules, 2025 extend EPR to specified non-ferrous scrap from
April 2026

secs.t: Data — storage need, progress and EV figures

x: The figures stated are more than 25 lakh registrations in FY 2025-26, approximately 8.5 percent penetration, and a 30 percent target by 2030.

secs.t: Places — gigafactories and projects

x: Ola Electric is associated with Tamil Nadu; Reliance New Energy and Tata (Agratas) with Gujarat; and Amara Raja with Telangana.
Adani Green commissioned the world’s largest single-location BESS outside China at Khavda in Gujarat in May 2026.

secs.t: Electric vehicles — types and powertrains

x: A BEV is powered only by a battery pack and normally receives energy through plug-in charging.
Hybrid vehicles combine an engine and battery-motor system, while a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle can be externally charged.
An FCEV converts hydrogen into electricity on board through a fuel cell, and water is its exhaust product.
BEVs, FCEVs and fuel cell-electric hybrids are all included among alternative powertrain vehicles.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — storage firsts and projects

x: Pinnapuram is located in
Kurnool
district and is associated with Greenko’s Integrated Renewable Energy Storage Project.
Greenko’s Pinnapuram project integrates solar and wind generation with pumped storage.
Andhra Pradesh is identified as one of
four
States getting a Rare Earth Corridor.
The device was unveiled at
Amaravati
on 6 August 2018 (APPSC 2018 key).

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Storage addresses the variability of renewable generation and helps provide 24×7 renewable electricity.
The sector faces import dependence for cell manufacturing and concentration of upstream minerals, with more than 70 percent of lithium processing in a few countries.
CEA plans 3,931 MW of battery storage and 7,370 MW of pumped storage for AP.

rows.title: Energy efficiency - Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Energy Conservation Act, PAT scheme, star labelling, UJALA
sub: Group-II M2-B-44: Energy efficiency and conservation - BEE, Energy Conservation Act, PAT, star labelling, UJALA

secs.t: Acts and amendments → provisions

x: The Act provides for norms for buildings with a connected load exceeding 100 kW or a contract demand exceeding 120 kVA.
The Act provides for mandatory audits of designated consumers, efficiency norms for appliances, equipment and buildings, and penalties for non-compliance.
All three are features of the 2022 amendment: non-fossil energy obligation, extension of building codes to large residential buildings, and efficiency norms for vehicles and vessels.

secs.t: Organisations → status and role

x: SEEI, PAT, Standards and Labelling, ECBC, CAFE and NECA are all associated with BEE.
BEE is a statutory body set up under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 and functions under the Ministry of Power (operational from 1 March 2002).
Both programmes are implemented by
Energy Efficiency Services Limited
(EESL), a joint venture of public-sector undertakings under the Ministry of Power.

secs.t: Schemes and programmes → year and feature

x: Over-achievers earn ESCerts, under-achievers buy them, and the certificates are traded on power exchanges, including the Indian Energy Exchange.
EESL runs the programme, which covers 20 lakh induction cookstoves, offers a stated 25–30% cost advantage over traditional cooking and is associated with MECS.
CAFE norms concern M1 cars, were first notified in 2017, are enforced by BEE, and SAKSHAM is conducted by PCRA for fuel conservation.

secs.t: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme — design and coverage

x: The scheme has a compliance mechanism, under which obligated industries earn or buy Carbon Credit Certificates, and a voluntary offset mechanism.
The stated goal is a 45% cut in GDP emission intensity by 2030 relative to the 2005 level.
CCTS is administered by BEE, regulated by CERC and has a compliance mechanism using Carbon Credit Certificates, so B, C and D are features.

secs.t: Standards and labelling — star label, mandatory vs voluntary

x: The Standards and Labelling programme is administered by the
Bureau of Energy Efficiency under the Ministry of Power
The programme covers more than 40 equipment categories, uses a one-to-five-star scale and each additional star is associated with approximately 10–15 per cent energy savings.
Manufacturers may be penalised if the actual energy consumption of a product deviates from the consumption declared through its label.

secs.t: Building codes → year and scope

x: ECBC applies to new commercial buildings, ECO Niwas Samhita applies to residential buildings, and ECSBC adds sustainability to the framework.
ECBC dates from 2007, applies to new commercial buildings and can reduce energy use by about 25–40 per cent; ECO Niwas Samhita dates from 2018 and covers residential buildings.
The AP model Super ECBC building is located at Sagar Nagar in Visakhapatnam.

secs.t: Lighting and everyday conservation — lamp types and practices

x: CFLs are more efficient than incandescent lamps but contain mercury and have a shorter life than LEDs.
LEDs, star-rated appliances, switching off idle loads and avoiding excessive air-conditioner use are the stated energy-conservation practices.
Induction cooking, using lids and using pressure cookers are recommended practices for improving cooking efficiency.
Correct tyre pressure, steady speed and switching off the engine at signals are fuel-saving practices.

secs.t: Indices, days and awards

x: SEEI was developed by BEE with AEEE, is used as the basis for the National Energy Conservation Awards, and classifies States into four categories including Front Runner and Aspirant.
Andhra Pradesh was rated a
Front Runner
, the top category, in the inaugural 2018 index prepared by NITI Aayog with BEE (APPSC 2018).

secs.t: Data — results and distribution

x: PAT, S&L and UJALA together saved about 53.6 Mtoe and avoided about 321.06 MT CO2 a year.
UJALA distributed about
36.86 crore
LED bulbs, along with 72.18 lakh LED tube lights and 23.59 lakh energy-efficient fans.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — APSECM, Energy Conservation Week and state measures — Energy Conservation Week in AP

x: The
School Education Department
collaborated in Andhra Pradesh’s National Energy Conservation Week awareness activities in 2024.
APSECM is India’s first standalone State Designated Agency of BEE and enforces the Energy Conservation Act, 2001, in Andhra Pradesh.
APSECM works with the State Industries Department and the Bureau of Energy Efficiency while implementing energy-efficiency and energy-conservation programmes.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — APSECM, Energy Conservation Week and state measures — AP measures

x: The IoT energy pilot was first undertaken at an MSME unit in
East Godavari
and was later extended to all districts with BEE.
PAT in Andhra Pradesh covered 59 energy-intensive industries and resulted in approximately 1.16 Mtoe of energy savings.
The four clusters were gold ornaments, imitation jewellery, food processing and pharmaceuticals.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: PAT is associated with energy-intensity certificates, called ESCerts, while CCTS is associated with emission-intensity certificates, called CCCs.
Energy efficiency is a relatively inexpensive route to reduce demand and emissions and improves energy security, particularly given India’s approximately 80 per cent oil-import dependence.
APSECM was a 2018 Front Runner, received the first NECA prize, and its 15th Executive Committee reviewed DSM, ECBC, PAT and Standards and Labelling.

rows.title: Energy access and distribution programmes - Saubhagya, DDUGJY, UDAY, PM-KUSUM, PM Surya Ghar

secs.t: Schemes → year, ministry and aim

x: PMUY was launched in 2016 by the
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
to provide deposit-free LPG connections to poor women.
UDAY, or Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana, was introduced by the Ministry of Power in November 2015 for the financial turnaround of state discoms.
IPDS strengthens
urban sub-transmission and distribution, metering and IT enablement

secs.t: Household electricity and clean cooking — provisions

x: ₹6,521 crore was sanctioned for 13.65 lakh leftover households, including PVTGs under PM-JANMAN, tribal households under DAJGUA, SC households under PMAJAY and border villages under Vibrant Villages.
Ujjwala 2.0 provides a free first refill and stove, permits migrants to use self-declaration, and provides cash assistance of ₹1,600 per 14.2 kg connection.

secs.t: Distribution reforms — IPDS, UDAY, RDSS provisions and targets

x: UDAY provided for State takeover of 75% of DISCOM debt in the two specified instalments, covering 97% of total outstanding debt.
RDSS was approved in 2021 with an outlay of ₹3,03,758 crore, including Gross Budgetary Support of ₹97,631 crore.
RDSS aims at pan-India
AT&C losses of 12–15% and an ACS-ARR gap of zero

secs.t: Solar for farmers and homes — PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar features

x: The outlay of PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana is
₹75,021 crore
The scheme targets rooftop solar installations in
1 crore households
by FY 2026-27, that is, March 2027.
The City Accelerator Programme, launched in June 2025, provides technical help to urban local bodies and discoms for urban rooftop solar.

secs.t: Data — achievements and progress

x: Saubhagya electrified
2.86 crore
willing households.
Phase I of PMUY targeted 8 crore deposit-free LPG connections by 2019; the reported number of connections later exceeded 9.5 crore.
Survey findings indicate that households generally want clean fuel but face affordability and established-habit barriers to regular refilling.

secs.t: Andhra Pradesh — free power, PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM, RDSS

x: Concessional tariffs are mentioned for BC/MBC professionals, dhobi ghats, handlooms and saloons;
large-scale automobile factories
are not included in this list.
The provision of free rooftop solar for SC/ST households is associated with
Virtual Net Metering
Andhra Pradesh had 10,639.75 MW of renewable-energy capacity, comprising 5,614.52 MW of solar and 4,397.67 MW of wind capacity.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The emphasis moved from providing connections through DDUGJY and Saubhagya, to quality and discom viability through UDAY and RDSS, and subsequently to prosumers through PM Surya Ghar.
Installed capacity was 509.74 GW and renewable energy constituted 49.83 per cent in November 2025.
The continuing concerns are weak discom finances, slow uptake of rooftop solar and difficulties in accessing loans.

secs.t: Solar park schemes — definitions, thresholds and largests

x: The Solar Park Scheme was launched by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy on
12 December 2014
An Ultra Mega Solar Park has a capacity of 500 MW or more at one location.
India has about 0.7 GW of floating solar capacity against an estimated 102 GW potential, and the 278 MW Omkareshwar project in Madhya Pradesh is the largest identified project.

secs.t: AP renewable projects → village and district

x: The project comprises 400 MW of solar capacity at Pathikonda in Kurnool and 400 MW of wind capacity at Kanekallu in Anantapur.
The
Kurnool
Ultra Mega Solar Park (1,000 MW) is at Gani-Sakunala, Panyam mandal, Kurnool (APPSC 2019).
The 25 MW floating solar plant is at NTPC Simhadri in Visakhapatnam (APPSC 2021).

secs.t: AP power plants → operator and capacity

x: Simhadri STPS at Visakhapatnam is operated by NTPC and has a capacity of 2,000 MW.
The combined APGENCO thermal capacity of NTTPS and RTPP is
Andhra Pradesh lost its coal mines after bifurcation, causing long coal haulage and exposure to poor coal quality.

secs.t: AP energy agencies → role

x: NREDCAP
is the State nodal agency for renewable energy and facilitates land, clearances and single-window services.
APTRANSCO handles transmission and had 13 ongoing 400 kV works valued at ₹3,698 crore.
NREDCAP is the renewable-energy nodal agency; it does not operate all thermal power plants.
APSECM
is the agency associated with energy conservation.

secs.t: Data — potential, capacity, rooftop and land

x: A subsidy of
is provided for 27.59 lakh BC households using less than 200 units.
The barren land was opened for solar leases to avoid diversion of farmland for renewable-energy projects.
Solar energy accounts for approximately 53% and wind energy for approximately 41% of Andhra Pradesh’s renewable-energy mix of 10,639.75 MW.

x: The 600 MW SAEL project in Kadapa is identified as a development under the
Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024
PM-KUSUM in Andhra Pradesh targets
2.93 lakh
farm pumps.
Leasing barren land is suggested as a response to food-versus-fuel conflicts, since renewable-energy projects may compete with agriculture for land.
Andhra Pradesh’s solar capacity in the cited comparison was 5.6 GW, not 32,000 MW.
