rows.title: Regulation and ethics of biotechnology - GEAC, biosafety, bioethics, biopiracy, IPR and the ethical/social/legal debate
sub: Group-II M2-B-83: Regulation of transgenics in India - GEAC, biosafety rules and GM crop status

secs.t: GEAC — ministry, Act, chair, role

x: The
Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee
(GEAC) is the apex statutory body regulating GMOs in India.
GEAC is chaired by a Special or Additional Secretary of MoEFCC.
GEAC deals with field trials, environmental release, commercial cultivation and large-scale use of hazardous microorganisms and recombinants.
GEAC is constituted in MoEFCC under the Rules, 1989 framed under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.

secs.t: Committees under Rules 1989 → level and role; field-trial process

x: RCGM is under DBT and monitors ongoing research and advises GEAC; GEAC (MoEFCC) approves environmental release and commercial use.
The process begins with committees’ safety assessments, followed by confined open-plot trials, evaluation of superiority without ecological harm, and only then commercial clearance.
Commercial clearance is contemplated only when trials show superiority over non-GM varieties without ecological harm.

secs.t: Acts, policies and proposed regulators → year and provision

x: GM food is governed by the
Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
, with the FSSAI GM food framework of 2024; import of GM food without approval of the competent authority is prohibited.
The Bill lapsed with the 15th Lok Sabha.
The
BioE3 Policy, 2024
proposes single-window clearance and regulatory sandboxes.

secs.t: GM crops approved for commercial cultivation

x: Bt cotton
was approved for commercial cultivation in March 2002.
Three MAHYCO hybrids were initially approved for three years, and Bt cotton remains the only GM crop commercially cultivated in India.
Maharashtra
is identified as the leading Bt cotton State.

secs.t: GM crops → introduced trait + source organism

x: Bollgard II cotton contains Cry1Ac and Cry2Ab genes sourced from Bacillus thuringiensis.
Bt brinjal was developed for resistance to the
fruit and shoot borer
insect.
Barnase-barstar comes from Bacillus amyloliquefaciens; Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of Bt genes.
Flavr Savr tomato was the first commercial GM food and was introduced in the USA in 1994.

secs.t: Genome-edited crops → developer, trait, regulation

x: Pusa Rice DST1 was developed by ICAR-IARI, Delhi; Kamala by ICAR through IIRR, Hyderabad; and the CRISPR phosphate-uptake rice by NIPGR.
Pusa Rice DST1 is an edited form of MTU1010, designed for drought and salinity tolerance through DST gene knockout using SDN-1.
The NIPGR rice is non-GMO, improves phosphate uptake and may reduce fertiliser imports, while Varuna is a CRISPR mustard associated with oil quality.

secs.t: GM crops in India — year → trials, moratoria and court cases

x: Bt cotton was introduced in 2002, the PIL was filed in 2006, the Bt brinjal moratorium was imposed in 2010, and GEAC cleared trials in 2014.
The 37th Report of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Agriculture
in 2012 recommended ending all GM field trials.
The Technical Expert Committee recommended a 10-year moratorium and trials were halted.

secs.t: GM debate — concerns and reasons for resistance

x: The primary environmental concern is cross-pollination or gene flow from GM crops to non-GM crops.
Overlapping mandates among DBT, GEAC, CDSCO, FSSAI and NBA, together with the absence of a biosafety liability law, contribute to delays.
Genetic modification is the technology flagged for biodiversity concerns (APPSC-GS 2023), through gene flow, monoculture and loss of diversity.

secs.t: Biosafety — Cartagena Protocol and BSL levels

x: Cartagena is in Colombia.
BSL-2 is for moderate-risk agents; lethal agents with no cure (e.g.
BSL-4 is used for lethal agents with no cure, such as Ebola, and the National Institute of Virology at Pune is identified in this context in India.

secs.t: Biosecurity and dual-use research — conventions, laws, index

x: The Biological Weapons Convention was opened in 1972 and entered into force in 1975.
The
Weapons of Mass Destruction Act, 2005
criminalises biological weapons.
DBT is associated with biocontainment, while NCDC is associated with surveillance in the stated biosecurity framework.
The stated gap is the
absence of a unified national biosecurity framework
, with laws also lagging behind synthetic biology and gene editing.

secs.t: IPR in biotech — Patents Act sections, PPVFR Act, cases, GURT

x: Section 3(j)
excludes plants, animals, seeds and essentially biological processes from patentability, while microbial processes can be patented.
In Novartis v. Union of India, the Supreme Court upheld rejection of the Glivec (imatinib) patent under
Section 3(d)
of the Patents Act.
PepsiCo sued Gujarat farmers over its FL-2027 (FC5) variety, later withdrew the suits, and the PPVFR Authority revoked the registration in 2021.

secs.t: Bioethics — guidelines, persons, ethical issues

x: “Designer babies” refers to the ethical concern that genetic technologies could be used to select or modify desired traits in human offspring.
He Jiankui’s human embryo-editing experiment in China became widely associated with the “CRISPR babies” controversy in 2018.
UNESCO’s International Bioethics Committee
monitors the ethical implications of genome editing.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Pusa Rice DST1 was described as India’s first genome-edited rice for commercial launch and was to be regulated like
a conventional crop
A GMO contains foreign genetic material and follows the full GEAC route.
The exemption has been criticised as a possible back door around the full GM regulatory route, with concerns about biosecurity gaps.

rows.title: Nanotechnology - nature, scope, applications, Nano Mission, health and environmental concerns

secs.t: Nanotechnology — definition, scale and properties

x: Quantum effects and the high surface-area-to-volume ratio produce enhanced reactivity and unusual optical and electrical behaviour.
Nanoparticles are
in size (APPSC 2018 key); one nanometre is one billionth (10^-9) of a metre.

secs.t: Scientists → contributions (FIRSTs of nanoscience)

x: Richard Feynman
proposed the foundational idea in his 1959 lecture, “There’s Plenty of Room at the Bottom.”.
Fullerene C60 is popularly called a buckyball and is associated with Kroto, Curl and Smalley, who received the Nobel Chemistry Prize in 1996.
Andre Geim and Konstantin Novoselov received the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics for work associated with graphene.

secs.t: Tools, synthesis and nanomaterials — terms → meaning

x: STM is used for imaging atoms on conducting surfaces, while AFM can work on non-conducting materials as well.
The top-down approach reduces bulk material to nanoscale dimensions through processes such as lithography, milling and etching.
Chemical vapour deposition
builds nanostructures from atoms or molecules and is therefore a bottom-up method.

secs.t: Generations of nanoproducts — four generations in order

x: Exam angle: "which is a third-generation nanosystem" - match example to generation.
The third generation consists of systems of nanosystems, including complex devices such as nanoelectronics and nanomedicine.
All four pairs correctly represent the four generations: passive structures, active structures, systems of nanosystems and molecular nanosystems.
The four-generation classification of nanoproducts is associated with
M. C. Roco

secs.t: Institutes and firms → nano developments (devices, medicine, water, energy)

x: Gold-nanoparticle lateral-flow kits can diagnose malaria, dengue and typhoid rapidly, while graphene enables bendable wearable sensors.
IIT Mandi developed renewable-resource-based natural-polymer nanoparticles for
colorectal cancer
applications.
The DCGI approved
Pulse Pharmaceuticals
’ nano-carrier Vitamin D3 oral dispersion, described as a claimed world first.
IIT Roorkee’s facility complements the
Semiconductor, Nano and Quantum missions
; it is not associated with Samudrayaan.

secs.t: Nano fertilisers — Nano Urea and Nano DAP data

x: Nano Urea has an indicated nitrogen-use efficiency of about 70%, compared with approximately 30–35% for conventional urea.
Nano Urea is approximately 20–50 nm, is used as a foliar spray and may reduce urea use by up to about 25%.
The Nano DAP specification was notified under the FCO on 2 March 2023, and it is used for seed treatment and foliar spray.

secs.t: Nano Mission and related programmes → year, department, outlay

x: The Nano Mission was launched in 2007 under the Department of Science and Technology as an umbrella programme.
The Nano Mission had an initial outlay of Rs 1,000 crore for a period of five years.
The Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST), Mohali, is among the institutions associated with the DST Nano Programme.

secs.t: Concerns and regulation — nanotoxicity, types, guidelines

x: Nanoparticles may induce
oxidative stress and inflammation
, with concerns also relating to long-term toxicity, persistence and bioaccumulation.
Volcanic ash, sea spray and smoke are natural sources.
DGFASLI guidelines, FSSAI guidelines of 2022 and the SCOMET framework are relevant.
The Department of Biotechnology issued the Guidelines for Evaluation of Nano-based Agri-input and Food Products in 2020.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: A major criticism is that nano-urea has been rolled out rapidly without adequate long-term studies.
Nano-inputs can raise
absorption efficiency
, which is one of the proposed agricultural benefits of nanotechnology.
Nanotechnology is associated with reducing fertiliser subsidy and imports, enabling frugal diagnostics and supporting targeted cancer drugs.

rows.title: Health and environment - vector-borne and water-borne diseases, air pollution and health, antimicrobial resistance, One Health
sub: Group-II M2-B-113: Health and environment linkages - air pollution, water-borne and vector-borne diseases, antimicrobial resistance, One Health

secs.t: Vector-borne diseases — disease → vector → pathogen

x: Exam angle: odd-one-out "not spread by mosquito" - kala-azar, sleeping sickness, scrub typhus.
Malaria destroys red blood cells, dengue mainly affects platelets, and chikungunya is caused by an alphavirus.
Japanese encephalitis
is transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, and pigs act as amplifying hosts.
Lymphatic filariasis is transmitted by Culex quinquefasciatus, sleeping sickness by the tsetse fly, scrub typhus by the chigger mite, and plague by the rat flea.

secs.t: Zoonotic diseases → animal source

x: Plague
is associated with rodents and is transmitted through rat fleas.
Kyasanur Forest Disease is associated with monkeys and is transmitted through ticks.
Rabies, anthrax and Nipah are zoonotic diseases associated with animal sources.
Anthrax is associated with
infected livestock

secs.t: Water-borne diseases and contaminants → pathogen / disease

x: Typhoid
is caused by Salmonella Typhi, and the Widal test is associated with its diagnosis.
The faecal-oral group includes
cholera, typhoid, hepatitis A and E, acute diarrhoea, dysentery and polio
Floods can spread
cholera, typhoid, hepatitis and leptospirosis
, in addition to supporting the spread of some vector-borne diseases.
Jal Jeevan Mission, Swachh Bharat Mission and AMRUT
are identified as relevant remedies or interventions.

secs.t: Disease → target organ or blood component

x: Malaria parasites first undergo development in the liver and then infect
red blood cells
Amoebiasis affects the large intestine and is caused by Entamoeba histolytica.
Dengue is associated with platelets.

secs.t: Vector control — programmes, bio-control agents, Wolbachia

x: Gambusia and guppy are larvivorous fish; Bti is a bacterial bio-larvicide; Wolbachia is associated with cytoplasmic incompatibility and pathogen blocking.
The Verily ‘Debug’ approach used Wolbachia-carrying males to suppress
Culex quinquefasciatus
, a vector associated with West Nile and St Louis encephalitis.
Of the six diseases covered (malaria, JE, dengue, chikungunya, kala-azar, LF), the elimination targets are
malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar

secs.t: Air pollution and climate → health effects

x: Air pollution primarily affects the
respiratory system
, although it is also associated with cardiovascular disease, stroke and lung cancer.
DALY
combines years of life lost due to premature death and years lived with disability, making it a disease-burden metric.
Climate change increases the risk of extreme weather events and several vector-borne diseases, and about 3.6 billion people are reported to live in highly vulnerable areas.

secs.t: Antimicrobial resistance — causes, terms, new antibiotic, policy

x: Biofilms are microbial or bacterial communities embedded in a self-made slimy matrix, which shields them from antibiotics and, in many cases, from host immunity.
Nafithromycin, or Miqnaf, is India’s first indigenous macrolide antibiotic intended for community-acquired bacterial pneumonia.
Nafithromycin was launched on 20 November 2024 by Dr Jitendra Singh and was developed by Wockhardt with BIRAC support.

secs.t: One Health, surveillance and immunisation — programmes and Acts

x: Biodiversity loss can increase zoonotic and pandemic risk by disturbing ecological relationships and interactions between humans, animals and pathogens.
The National One Health Mission is applicable to rabies, Nipah, avian influenza and AMR, among other linked health threats.

The UIP list includes all the diseases stated: diphtheria, pertussis, tetanus, polio, measles, rubella, childhood TB, hepatitis B, Hib disease, rotavirus diarrhoea, pneumococcal pneumonia and JE in endemic districts.

secs.t: AP angle — disease burden data and State response

x: The Andhra Pradesh workshop involved NCDC, the US CDC and Jhpiego, as part of preparation of a State Action Plan on zoonotic diseases.
The AP adult BCG drive began on 16 May 2024, administered 27.10 lakh doses and placed Andhra Pradesh first in India for this drive.
Scrub typhus accounted for 941 cases and was rising in ASR and Parvathipuram Manyam districts.
The response includes indoor residual spraying, long-lasting insecticidal nets and source reduction.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Life expectancy increased from 49.7 years in 1973 to 70.3 years in 2023, yet non-communicable diseases account for more than 57% of deaths and communicable diseases continue to persist, creating a double burden.
AP reported 7,895 malaria cases up to 30 August 2026, a 27.9% rise, concentrated in tribal districts such as ASR, Polavaram and Vizianagaram.

rows.title: Recent trends in India's disease burden - communicable and non-communicable diseases
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: Disease burden — terms → meaning and transition stages

x: The triple burden combines
communicable diseases, non-communicable diseases and injuries
such as road accidents and trauma.
The dual burden of malnutrition refers to undernutrition existing alongside adult overweight and obesity.
Dual burden (PYQ answer) means persistent communicable diseases such as TB, malaria and dengue coexisting with rising NCDs.
Omran's sequence proceeds from the Age of Pestilence and Famine to the Age of Receding Pandemics and then to the Age of Degenerative and Man-Made Diseases.

secs.t: Disease burden data — NCD share, leading causes, life expectancy, cancer

x: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of death in India, while WHO estimates identify ischaemic heart disease as the world's single biggest killer.
Most countries reduced NCD deaths, whereas India's probability of dying from an NCD rose, particularly in the specified age-sex groups.
The projected number of cancer cases is expected to rise from 1.41 million in 2022 to
2.46 million

secs.t: Communicable vs lifestyle diseases and emerging infections

x: The four major NCD groups are
cardiovascular diseases, cancers, chronic respiratory diseases and diabetes
ICMR's wastewater surveillance expanded from 5 to 50 cities, tracks 10 viruses including avian influenza, and also monitors antimicrobial resistance.
The
NCDC
's Public Health Emergency Operations Centre, or PHEOC, was activated in response to the reported Nipah cases.

secs.t: Lifestyle disease risk factors — PYQ statements and data

x: NFHS-5 reported overweight or obesity among 24% of women and 23% of men for 2019–21.

Both statements are correct (PYQ): bakery products use hydrogenated fats containing trans fats, and excess trans fats raise NCD risk, which is why FSSAI caps trans fat at 2% in fats and oils. '1 only' and '2 only' each reject a true statement; 'Neither' rejects both.

secs.t: Programmes, declarations and targets on NCDs

x: FSSAI has capped trans fat in fats and oils at 2%.
The declaration covers oral and lung health, childhood cancer, air pollution, lead and digital harms such as screen time.
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs screen for hypertension, diabetes, and oral, breast and cervical cancers.
Tele-MANAS
provides round-the-clock tele-mental-health support across all 36 States and Union Territories.

secs.t: AP disease burden — 2025 case load, Uddanam CKDu, NCD care

x: Andhra Pradesh set up task forces for scrub typhus under the cited state health measures.
The samples are tested for pesticides and heavy metals, not viruses and protozoa.
AIIMS Mangalagiri
conducts screening camps for chronic kidney disease of unknown cause in the Uddanam region.
Andhra Pradesh's first Diabetic Foot and Ulcer Clinic was opened at
Vizianagaram

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The growing NCD burden requires a shift from a predominantly curative approach towards screening and prevention.
The interim report found a high level of kidney disease in
Kaviti mandal
of the Uddanam region.
The Kidney Research Centre and Super Specialty Hospital is located at Palasa in Srikakulam district.
As of 4 July 2026, cancer was notifiable in 17 States, a step towards better NCD surveillance.

rows.title: Epidemic and pandemic challenges in India - major outbreaks, lessons from COVID-19
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: Outbreak terms → meaning

x: A disease constantly present at a baseline level in an area is described as
endemic
A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across countries and continents.
An epidemic among animals is termed an
epizootic
An
epidemic
is a sudden, severe outbreak in a region at a particular time.

secs.t: Global outbreaks → virus, host, PHEIC

x: Ebola virus was first found in 1976 near the Ebola River in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Ebola is associated with the genus Orthoebolavirus, family Filoviridae, fruit-bat reservoirs and the particularly deadly Zaire species.
The outbreak was declared a PHEIC but not a pandemic emergency.
The 2014–16 West African Ebola outbreak mainly affected
Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone

secs.t: Major outbreaks in India → place and year

x: Nipah has struck Kerala from 2018 onwards, Zika appeared in Kerala in 2021, Chandipura (sandfly-borne) broke out in Gujarat in 2024, and plague (Yersinia pestis) hit Surat, Gujarat, in 1994.
The plague outbreak in Surat, Gujarat, in 1994 was associated with
Yersinia pestis
and transmission through rat fleas.
The first Indian outbreak of avian influenza was reported at Navapur in
Maharashtra in 2006

secs.t: SARS-CoV-2 — naming, FIRSTs, entry, variants

x: SARS-CoV-2 causes COVID-19, which stands for Coronavirus Disease 2019.
SARS-CoV-2 was first identified in Wuhan in Hubei province of China in December 2019.
SARS-CoV-2 enters cells through the
ACE2 receptor
WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic on
11 March 2020
The
Delta
variant was first found in India.

secs.t: COVID-19 in India — timeline, strategy and data

x: The first case in Kerala occurred on 30 January 2020, the first wave peaked in September 2020, the Delta second wave occurred in April–May 2021 and the Omicron third wave came in January 2022.
All four were components of India's COVID-19 response strategy: test-track-treat-vaccinate, COVID-appropriate behaviour, MHA Empowered Groups and a three-tier facility arrangement.

secs.t: COVID-19 vaccines → developer → platform

x: Covishield was the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine made in India by the Serum Institute and used an adenovirus viral vector.
iNCOVACC
, developed by Bharat Biotech, was described as the world's first intranasal COVID-19 vaccine approved for the primary two-dose schedule and the heterologous booster.
ZyCoV-D
, developed by Zydus, was described as the world's first DNA vaccine approved for humans and used a needle-free injector.

secs.t: Schemes, platforms and State models → feature

x: The Lancet report of 24 February 2022 estimated that about
19 lakh
children in India lost a parent or caregiver to COVID-19.
Vaccine Maitri supplied vaccines to
low- and middle-income countries
The Covid Pharma app tracked over-the-counter sales of medicines used for fever and cough, helping monitor possible disease trends.

secs.t: Lessons from COVID-19 — gaps exposed, digital tools

x: The pandemic exposed gaps in health infrastructure and oxygen supply, created a migrant crisis, and revealed dependence on external supply chains.
CoWIN, U-WIN, ABDM and eSanjeevani are the digital tools identified as emerging from the pandemic experience.
The One Health approach links human, animal and environmental health rather than separating them entirely.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The stated current-relevance associations are Ebola as a PHEIC in May 2026, an H1N1 spike in August 2026, and Nipah in West Bengal in January 2026.
The Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri region and Uganda was declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in
May 2026

rows.title: Healthcare delivery in India - three-tier structure, human resources and infrastructure
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: Health committees → year → recommendation

x: The Bhore Committee recommended integrated preventive and curative care and a three-tier PHC-based system.
The correct sequence is Bhore (1943–46), Mudaliar (1959–62), Kartar Singh (1973), and Shrivastava (1975).

Mudaliar (1959-62) asked to consolidate PHCs and strengthen district hospitals (iii); Kartar Singh (1973) recommended multipurpose workers and one PHC per 50,000 (i); Shrivastava (1975) recommended village health guides and a Referral Services Complex (ii).

secs.t: Three-tier structure — tier → facility → norm; counts and IPHS

x: The
Sub Health Centre
is the first contact point in the primary healthcare tier.
A PHC is a primary-level referral centre for Sub Health Centres, not a tertiary referral hospital.
CHCs function as referrals for PHCs and are equipped with
operation theatres and beds
IPHS 2022 covers
SHC and HWC, PHC, CHC, sub-district hospitals and district hospitals

secs.t: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs and telemedicine — services and network

x: Mental health, ENT, eye care, geriatric and palliative care, and Yoga and wellness are all included in the stated CPHC package.
The CPHC package screens for hypertension, diabetes and the three common cancers: oral, breast and cervical.
eSanjeevani OPD
provides patient-to-provider consultation from home. eSanjeevani AAM is the provider-to-provider hub-and-spoke variant.

secs.t: Tertiary expansion schemes → provision

x: PMSSY was launched in 2003.
AIIMS Mangalagiri
is the AIIMS institution associated with Andhra Pradesh.
PM-JAY provides health cover of
Rs 5 lakh
per family per year.

secs.t: Human resources — ratios and shortages

x: About 1:834 against the WHO norm of 1:1000.
The nurse ratio is below global norms, while specialist posts at rural CHCs have high vacancies.
Community workers
are stated to carry the heaviest workload.

secs.t: Public vs private delivery — data and issues

x: NFHS-3 reported that the private sector was the main source of care for
of urban households.
The private sector handles
over 60% of inpatient care and about 70% of outpatient care
The committee made 368 recommendations, including
standard package rates and tariffs capped near nearby three-star hotel rates
The public system is largely curative with limited preventive and promotive care (UPSC 2023 statement).

secs.t: AP delivery network — facilities, AAM conversion, 104/108, specialty centres

x: The 108 service provides emergency ambulances, whereas 104 provides mobile medical units and health advisory services.
AIIMS Mangalagiri
is the telemedicine anchor and has over 2,500 OPD patients a day.
The Greyfield super-specialty blocks were being finished at
Anantapur, Nellore and Eluru
AP's UPHCs have been upgraded to IPHS norms; 92 are NQAS-certified and 267 scored above 70% for Kayakalp.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The programme issues ABHA IDs and integrates the 104 and 108 services, e-Aushadhi and telemedicine.
The Andhra Pradesh-specific references include village health clinics, the 104 and 108 services, Palasa, AIIMS Mangalagiri, and the new CCBs and IPHLs.
The stated concerns are high out-of-pocket expenditure, more than 40 crore people forming a 'missing middle' without cover, and the urban concentration of doctors.

rows.title: Health outcomes in India and Andhra Pradesh - IMR, MMR, TFR, life expectancy and nutrition indicators
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: Mortality indicators — definitions and national trend

x: Exam angle: matching year → IMR value; "which state has lowest IMR"; per-1,000 vs per-1,00,000 base.
IMR denotes deaths of infants under one year per 1,000 live births in a year.
The reported IMR values were 40, 39, 37 and 34 for 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2016 respectively.
India's MMR was 97 per 1,00,000 live births in SRS 2018-20.

secs.t: States and AP → mortality and life expectancy

x: Kerala
has the lowest IMR, attributed to adequate basic health and education facilities.
Life expectancy at Independence was approximately
32 years
All four statements correctly state the SRS abridged life-table values for India and Andhra Pradesh during 2016–20.
Life expectancy rose from 49.7 years (1973) to
70.3 years

secs.t: National Family Health Survey — round → year, coverage, sex ratio

x: Exam angle: "which indicator is NOT covered by NFHS" and round → year matching.
NFHS-5 added death registration, pre-school education, menstrual hygiene, alcohol and tobacco use, and NCD screening for all aged 15 years and above.
NFHS reports stunting, wasting and underweight as separate indicators; it does not provide one single overall ‘malnutrition percentage’.

secs.t: Malnutrition — forms and burdens (terms)

x: Madhya Pradesh showed high child wasting and underweight.
WHO’s broad definition includes undernutrition, micronutrient inadequacy, and overnutrition with diet-related non-communicable diseases.
The double burden refers to the simultaneous presence of
undernutrition and overnutrition
The triple burden consists of
undernutrition, micronutrient deficiency or anaemia, and overweight

secs.t: Child nutrition data — NFHS-4 to NFHS-6, SOFI

x: Stunting
is low height-for-age, defined here as more than two standard deviations below the WHO median.
NFHS-5 reported anaemia among 67.1% of children aged 6–59 months and 57.0% of women aged 15–49 years.
Underweight was highest among Scheduled Tribes at 44.1%, followed by Scheduled Castes at 39.1%.
SOFI 2025 reported India’s wasting rate as
, involving approximately 21 million children.

secs.t: Drivers of malnutrition → effect

x: Food insecurity and poverty can produce undernutrition while also encouraging consumption of inexpensive energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods that contribute to overnutrition.
NFHS tracks sanitation, drinking water, women’s schooling and child marriage, all of which are linked to child nutrition.
Poor dietary habits and food insecurity
are the main driver of malnutrition (APPSC 2025 key).

secs.t: Nutrition and maternal schemes — national and AP

x: Anemia Mukt Bharat
uses a 6x6x6 strategy consisting of six interventions, six target groups and six institutional mechanisms.
The specified fortified rice contains
iron, folic acid and vitamin B12
and is supplied through the PDS, ICDS and PM POSHAN.
Anna Amrutha Hastam
provides a nutritious meal and iron-folic acid tablets to pregnant and lactating women through Anganwadis.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: Andhra Pradesh has an MMR of 45 and an IMR of 24, both better than the corresponding national averages.

rows.title: Health financing in India - public expenditure, out-of-pocket spending and insurance
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: Public health expenditure — National Health Accounts data

x: Exam angle: statement sets on NHA (SHA 2011 base; GHE highest during COVID; OOPE fell, not rose, during COVID - 39.4% of THE).
Government Health Expenditure increased from 1.15% of GDP in 2013–14 to 1.43% in 2022–23, a rise of
0.28 percentage points
GHE reached
of GDP during the COVID peak in 2021–22.

secs.t: Targets and grants — NHP 2017 target, 15th Finance Commission

x: NHP 2017 targeted Government Health Expenditure of 2.5% of GDP by 2025, with the Centre’s share intended to be 40% of public spending.
The 15th Finance Commission recommended health grants amounting to
₹70,051 crore
through local governments for 2021–2026.
The grants support diagnostic infrastructure for sub-centres and PHCs, block public health units, urban health and wellness centres, and buildings for building-less SCs, PHCs and CHCs.

secs.t: Out-of-pocket expenditure — data and issues

x: OOPE declined from 64.2% of Total Health Expenditure in 2013–14 to 43.4% in 2022–23, although it remained about half of current health expenditure.
Outpatient care, diagnostics and medicines
account for over half of OOPE because insurance commonly does not cover them.
The “missing middle” refers to more than 40 crore Indians who lack adequate financial protection; NITI Aayog first flagged the term.

secs.t: Medicine-cost bodies and insurance schemes → provision

x: NPPA, established in 1997, fixes ceiling prices for scheduled NLEM drugs under the Drugs Price Control Order, 2013.
The survey reported that outpatient medicine bills in private pharmacies were about
six times
higher than those through Jan Aushadhi.
The Clinical Establishments Act, 2010 has been adopted in only about 11 States and 6 UTs, which is why private-sector regulation remains a gap.

secs.t: AP health assurance — Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, Employee Health Scheme, budget

x: Dr. NTR Vaidya Seva, earlier YSR Aarogyasri, is Andhra Pradesh’s flagship cashless health assurance scheme for economically vulnerable families.
The Andhra Pradesh scheme is implemented in convergence with PM-JAY, particularly providing portability and wider hospital empanelment.
Five
more critical cardiovascular procedures were added in March 2026 to widen access to advanced cardiac care.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The NHA 2022–23 assessment and the parliamentary panel discussion on the ‘missing middle’ both indicate that the 2.5% target remains unmet.
Praja Arogya Vedika sought a Right to Health Act and withdrawal of PPPs in government medical colleges.
A stated criticism is that insurance-led models may expand coverage without a corresponding increase in actual care.

rows.title: Recent public health initiatives - Ayushman Bharat, National Health Mission, Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: Health policies → year and NHP 2017 targets

x: NHP 2017 adopted an assurance-based approach and envisaged comprehensive primary care rather than an insurance-only or disease-specific model.
NHP 2017 included NCD, mental health, geriatric and palliative care within comprehensive primary care.
The National Policy for Rare Diseases was issued in 2021, while the India Newborn Action Plan dates to 2014.

secs.t: National Health Mission — structure, ASHA, components, funding

x: ASHA means Accredited Social Health Activist, and ASHAs and ANMs play a crucial role in linking rural communities with healthcare services.
Kilkari delivers 72 weekly audio messages over the stated period, while Mobile Academy provides an audio course for ASHAs.
The Free Drugs Service Initiative provides generic medicines free of cost at public facilities, and DVDMS manages the drug supply chain.

secs.t: Immunisation — Mission Indradhanush, U-WIN, age → vaccine

x: It is a December 2014 catch-up drive under UIP for zero-dose and partly immunised children.
The birth schedule includes BCG, OPV-0 and the birth dose of Hepatitis B.
DPT booster-2 is administered at 5–6 years, not at 6 weeks.
U-WIN digitises
maternal and child vaccination records
and supports immunisation tracking.

secs.t: Ayushman Bharat — pillar → role, campaigns

x: Ayushman Arogya Mandirs provide comprehensive primary care.
The target was 1,50,000 centres.
PM-ABHIM strengthens pandemic-related health infrastructure through the stated investments and facilities.
These campaigns are associated with
Ayushman Arogya Mandirs
and aim to increase community participation and saturation of health-related services.

secs.t: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission — components, ABHA data, platforms → purpose

x: The NMC directed medical colleges to generate and link ABHA IDs for all OPD, IPD and emergency patients, partly to detect fake patients during inspections.
All three statements are correct. eSanjeevani incorporates a Clinical Decision Support System, NextGen eHospital is ABDM-aligned, and AYUSH HMIS was linked to ABHA in 2024.

secs.t: Campaigns and institutions → year and objective (ICMR, WHO)

x: Swachh Bharat focuses on sanitation, Fit India on daily fitness, and Eat Right India on safe, healthy and sustainable diets.
Together, Eat Right India and Fit India aim to reduce deaths caused by
non-communicable diseases
through healthier diets and increased physical activity.
The Secretariat aims to reduce India’s import dependence in medical devices and diagnostics.

secs.t: AP healthcare interventions — telemedicine, Sanjeevani, PM-ABHIM, diagnostics

x: Sanjeevani aims to create
a digital health profile and ABHA ID for every citizen
of Andhra Pradesh.
Sanjeevani links PHCs, hospitals, laboratories, e-Aushadhi, 108 emergency services, 104 mobile medical units, telemedicine and AI assistance.
Union Health Minister J. P. Nadda inaugurated
10 Critical Care Blocks and 12 Integrated Public Health Laboratories
in Andhra Pradesh under PM-ABHIM.

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The criticism is that insurance-led policies can expand coverage while failing to ensure actual access to health services.
Sanjeevani makes Andhra Pradesh an ABDM-linked, citizen-wide digital health state through digital profiles, ABHA IDs and connected health services.
The Indian Research Fund Association, established in 1911, was renamed the Indian Council of Medical Research in 1949.

rows.title: Disease-specific programmes - TB elimination, malaria, HIV/AIDS, NCD and mental health programmes
sub: Group-II only - placed after Group-I F-96

secs.t: Eradication milestones → year

x: India became free of smallpox in 1977, Pulse Polio was launched in 1995, the last wild polio case occurred in January 2011, and the region was certified polio-free in 2014.
Guinea worm was certified free in 2000.

secs.t: Elimination missions — disease → target year

x: Exam angle: programme → launch year and disease → target year matching; the PYQ key:
NVBDCP
handles outbreaks of malaria, dengue, chikungunya.
India has set a target to eliminate sickle-cell anaemia by 2047 and to screen seven crore at-risk people.
Malaria, lymphatic filariasis and kala-azar
are the diseases identified for elimination under NVBDCP.

secs.t: TB elimination — NTEP, Ni-kshay, PM TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan, data

x: The campaign was launched in September 2022, uses Ni-kshay Mitras to adopt patients, and includes food-basket support.

The India TB Report 2022 recorded a 19% rise in notifications in 2021 over 2020 (APPSC 2022 PYQ). 'Fell by 19%' reverses the direction; 53% is the 2015 treatment-coverage figure; 28% is the fall in TB mortality during 2015-2024.

secs.t: Malaria elimination — framework, MERA India, malaria-free countries, vaccines

x: The National Framework for Malaria Elimination covers
and targets malaria elimination by 2030.
Sri Lanka, China and Timor-Leste
are the three countries identified as WHO-certified malaria-free in this group.
RTS,S/AS01, also known as Mosquirix, is associated with GSK.
Universal antibiotic prophylaxis
is not one of them.
MERA India stands for the
ICMR-led Malaria Elimination Research Alliance

secs.t: HIV/AIDS — NACP phases, NACO, Act 2017, terms, projects

x: VCTC means Voluntary Counselling and Testing Centre, and free lifelong ART is provided at ART centres.
The Act of 2017 bars
discrimination against people living with HIV
and provides a legal framework for their protection.
Treatment as Prevention, Test and Treat, PEP within 72 hours, PrEP and condoms are recognised prevention tools.

secs.t: HIV/AIDS — 95-95-95 targets and burden data

x: The three 95s refer respectively to knowledge of HIV status, treatment, and viral-load suppression among those treated.
India’s stated goal is to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
HIV-1 subtype C
is the dominant strain in India.

secs.t: NCD and mental health — Acts, programmes, burden

x: The India Hypertension Control Initiative targets hypertension-related deaths from
heart attack, stroke and kidney failure
Cervavac is India's first indigenous quadrivalent HPV vaccine, made by the Serum Institute of India against cervical cancer (Sept 2022).
DMHP covers more than 90% of districts, 1.73 lakh AAMs include mental health, MANODARPAN supports students, and KIRAN is associated with the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

secs.t: AP programme performance — HIV, NCD screening, disease programmes

x: In Andhra Pradesh, the expanded NP-NCD coverage includes mental health, elderly care, iodine deficiency disorders, tobacco control, fluorosis and oral health.
Malaria epidemiology is changing in both tribal and non-tribal districts of Andhra Pradesh, making continued surveillance necessary.
The state runs
NTEP, NCVBDC, NPCBVI, NLEP, rabies, leptospirosis and snake-bite programmes

secs.t: Universal angles

x: The report titled 'United to end AIDS' noted that new infections had reached a 30-year low, while available funding was $17.6 billion against a requirement of $21.9 billion.
SDG 3.3 specifically seeks to end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases by 2030.
IDSP is concerned with outbreak surveillance.
